records.title: CALGB 9344 (INT 0148)
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2003
records.body: Women with operable node-positive breast cancer after lumpectomy or mastectomy with axillary sampling and negative margins; systemic therapy began within 84 days, and breast radiotherapy was required after lumpectomy. The HER2 correlative report used 1,322 obtained specimens from 1,500 randomly selected participants; other parent-protocol criteria were not filed Cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² + doxorubicin 60, 75 or 90 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks ×4, then paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks ×4 or observation; factorial 3×2 comparison (about 3 vs 6 months of chemotherapy) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, toxicity Escalating doxorubicin above 60 mg/m² did not improve DFS or OS and increased long-term cardiotoxicity; adding paclitaxel reduced recurrence (HR 0.83, P=.0023) and death (HR 0.82, P=.0064). Receptor-status and HER2 companion findings were unplanned or correlative and are not treatment-selection proof.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2003;21:976-983   N Engl J Med 2007;357:1496-1506 HER2 predictive companion analysis 17928597

records.title: CALGB 9741
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2003
records.body: Women with completely resected T0-3 N1-2 M0 primary breast adenocarcinoma after lumpectomy plus axillary dissection or modified radical mastectomy, with negative invasive margins and no non-axillary metastases; chemotherapy began within 84 days. Normal bilirubin, ECG/chest radiograph and per-cycle blood-count thresholds were required; age and performance-status criteria were not stated Dose-dense AC → paclitaxel (Q2W with G-CSF) vs conventional Q3W scheduling, in a 2×2 also comparing sequential (doxorubicin → paclitaxel → cyclophosphamide) vs concurrent (AC → paclitaxel); adjuvant Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, toxicity Dose-dense treatment improved DFS (RR 0.74, P=.010; 4-year DFS 82% vs 75%) and OS (RR 0.69, P=.013), with no sequence effect or density-by-sequence interaction. This first report had 36 months' median follow-up and only 315 of 515 expected events, so the survival estimate was not fully mature.

records.title: NSABP B-28
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2005
records.body: Resected operable invasive breast adenocarcinoma, cT1-3 cN0-1 cM0, confined to breast/ipsilateral axilla with at least one pathologically positive axillary node; lumpectomy with free margins plus axillary dissection or modified radical mastectomy. Randomisation within 63 days of diagnosis, adequate marrow/hepatic/renal function and 10-year non-cancer life expectancy were required; prior breast cancer/DCIS or prior therapy for this cancer were excluded Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² IV + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV Q3W ×4, followed by paclitaxel 225 mg/m² IV over 3 hours Q3W ×4, vs AC alone; adjuvant, node-positive Primary: disease-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: recurrence-free interval Adding paclitaxel after AC improved DFS (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72–0.95, P=.006; 5-year DFS 76% vs 72%) but not OS (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.78–1.12, P=.46). There was no evidence that hormone-receptor subgroup effects differed (DFS interaction P=.30); they should not be used as predictive evidence.

records.title: ECOG E1199
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2008
records.body: Women with operable breast adenocarcinoma, no distant metastases, T1-3 N1-2 or high-risk T2-3 N0 disease. Reported ineligibility included margin <1 mm, fewer than six nodes removed, T4/N3 or pre-registration metastases. Other protocol criteria were in an unfiled supplement; 26 of 102 ineligibility reasons were unspecified After AC ×4: paclitaxel vs docetaxel, each given weekly vs every 3 weeks (2×2 taxane type × schedule); adjuvant Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety The factorial main effects of taxane type and schedule on DFS were null, and a taxane-by-schedule interaction complicated interpretation. Weekly paclitaxel improved DFS and OS vs paclitaxel Q3W; docetaxel Q3W improved DFS only. The eligible efficacy population was 4,950 of 5,052 enrolled patients.

records.title: US Oncology 9735
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2006
records.body: Women aged 18-75 with completely excised stage I-III invasive breast cancer, tumour >=1.0 and <7.0 cm, Karnofsky score >=80 and no metastatic disease; no neoadjuvant chemotherapy or prior chemotherapy/hormonal therapy for this cancer. Baseline marrow, hepatic and renal thresholds applied; pregnancy/lactation, serious infection and significant comorbidity were excluded TC ×4 (docetaxel 75 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²) vs AC ×4 (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²), each IV Q3W; adjuvant Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety At 7 years, TC improved DFS versus AC (81% vs 75%; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.56–0.98, P=.033) and OS (87% vs 82%; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50–0.97, P=.032). The comparator was 4 cycles of AC, so this trial does not establish TC against contemporary anthracycline–taxane regimens.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2006;24:5381-5387   J Clin Oncol 2009;27:1177-1183 7-yr OS update 19204201

records.title: ABC trials (USOR 06-090/B-46-I/B-49)
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2017
records.body: Resected high-risk HER2-negative invasive breast cancer: pT1-3 node-positive (including pN1mi), or node-negative ER/PR-negative, tumour >2 cm, or T1c ER/PR-positive grade 3 or high recurrence score. Adequate marrow/hepatic/renal function, LVEF >=50% and clear margins were required. Metastatic/T4/supraclavicular disease and recent ipsilateral or other invasive cancer were excluded Pooled analysis of three adjuvant trials: TC ×6 (docetaxel 75 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m², Q3W) vs standard taxane-plus-anthracycline (TaxAC) regimens ×6 (e.g. TAC, or AC → paclitaxel) Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: recurrence-free interval, overall survival, safety Six cycles of TC did not meet non-inferiority versus TaxAC for IDFS: final HR 1.14 (95% CI 0.99–1.32), and the prespecified 80% CI did not exclude the 1.18 margin. Recurrence-free interval favoured TaxAC (HR 1.38, P=.0003), while OS did not differ (HR 1.05, P=.64); the efficacy and harm trade-off does not establish equivalence.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2017;35:2647-2655   J Clin Oncol 2024;42:1344-1349 long-term follow-up 38335467

records.title: EBCTCG 15-year overview
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · N/A · 2005
records.body: Unconfounded randomized early-breast-cancer trials begun by 1995 of >1 month adjuvant chemotherapy, anthracycline versus CMF, tamoxifen duration/versus none, or ovarian ablation/suppression versus none. Short chemotherapy and local-treatment trials were excluded. No harmonized patient-level stage, histology, performance-status or organ-function criteria were reported About 6 months of anthracycline-based or CMF polychemotherapy vs none or each other; about 5 vs 1–2 years vs no tamoxifen; ovarian ablation or suppression vs none in women younger than 50 First recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, overall mortality, non-breast-cancer mortality, contralateral breast cancer, second primary cancers In this historical overview, about 6 months of anthracycline-based polychemotherapy reduced annual breast-cancer mortality by about 38% below age 50 and 20% at age 50–69, while about 5 years of tamoxifen reduced it by 31% in ER-positive disease. In women under 50, ovarian ablation or suppression reduced 15-year recurrence (47.3% vs 51.6%) and breast-cancer mortality (40.3% vs 43.5%); apparent attenuation with chemotherapy was uncertain.

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · N/A · 2012
records.body: Randomized early-breast-cancer trials begun 1973-2003 comparing taxane versus non-taxane regimens, anthracycline versus standard/near-standard CMF, higher versus lower anthracycline dose, or polychemotherapy versus none. Stem-cell-rescue and dose-density-only trials were excluded. Trial-level patient criteria and the web appendix were not filed Various polychemotherapy regimens vs no chemo or each other Recurrence, distant recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, overall mortality, acute mortality, acute-myeloid-leukaemia mortality, cardiac mortality Adding four taxane cycles to a fixed anthracycline backbone reduced breast-cancer mortality (RR 0.86, 2P=.0005), but not when control regimens received compensating extra non-taxane cycles (RR 0.94, 2P=.33). Standard 4AC and CMF had similar mortality, whereas higher-cumulative-dose anthracycline regimens outperformed CMF; the 'about one-third' reduction is an indirect product, not a head-to-head estimate.

records.title: NSABP B-18 & B-27
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · III · 2008
records.body: B-18: operable palpable T1-3 N0-1 M0 breast cancer. B-27: women with primary operable T1c-3 N0-1 M0 or T1-3 N1 M0 breast cancer. Diagnosis was by core biopsy or fine-needle aspiration; written consent was required. Other trial-specific inclusion/exclusion criteria were in prior reports and were not reproduced in the bound publication B-18: preoperative vs postoperative AC ×4 (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m², Q3W). B-27: preoperative AC ×4 then surgery, ± docetaxel 100 mg/m² Q3W ×4 given either before surgery (neoadjuvant) or after (adjuvant); tamoxifen 20 mg/d ×5 years in all Overall survival, disease-free survival, relapse-free interval, response rate, pathological complete response rate, breast-conserving surgery rate, first failure Giving the same AC before rather than after surgery did not improve long-term DFS or OS in B-18 but increased breast conservation. In B-27, adding preoperative docetaxel doubled pCR (13% to 26%, P<.001) without improving DFS (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.78–1.08, P=.29). pCR was prognostic for individual patients, but these trials did not validate it as a trial-level surrogate.

records.title: EBCTCG neoadjuvant meta-analysis
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · N/A · 2018
records.body: Randomized operable early-breast-cancer trials begun before 2005 comparing chemotherapy started preoperatively with the identical regimen started after surgery; trials with different postoperative chemotherapy, including B-27, were excluded. IPD covered 10 of 16 eligible trials. Trial-level stage, exclusions, laboratory criteria and the appendix were not filed Neoadjuvant chemotherapy vs identical adjuvant chemotherapy Response, breast-conserving therapy, local recurrence, distant recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, overall mortality Compared with the identical adjuvant regimen, neoadjuvant chemotherapy increased breast-conserving therapy (65% vs 49%) and 15-year local recurrence (21.4% vs 15.9%; RR 1.37, P=.0001). Distant recurrence, breast-cancer mortality and all-cause mortality did not differ. The trials largely predated taxanes and trastuzumab.

records.title: CTNeoBC pooled analysis
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · N/A · 2014
records.body: 2014 pool: neoadjuvant studies with >=200 primary-breast-cancer patients, surgery after chemotherapy, pCR/EFS/OS data and >=3 years median follow-up; postoperative-treatment patients, HER2-negative NOAH and patients never starting treatment were excluded. 2023 HER2-positive reanalysis required randomized anti-HER2 neoadjuvant trials with >=100 patients and the same outcomes/follow-up; trial-level criteria were not filed Neoadjuvant chemotherapy ± trastuzumab (pCR vs no pCR; patient- & trial-level analysis) Pathological complete response rate, event-free survival, overall survival Across 12 neoadjuvant trials, pCR in breast and nodes was strongly associated with better patient-level EFS and OS, especially in TNBC and HER2-positive/HR-negative disease. Treatment-induced pCR differences did not predict treatment effects on EFS or OS at trial level; the HER2-positive re-analysis likewise showed strong patient-level associations but weak trial-level R², so pCR was not validated as a trial-level surrogate.
records.keywords: Lancet 2014;384:164-172   J Clin Oncol 2023;41:2988-2997 HER2+ re-evaluation 36977286

records.title: Residual Cancer Burden (Symmans)
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · N/A · 2017
records.body: Five institutional cohorts of primary breast cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgery, spanning TNBC, HR-positive/HER2-negative and HER2-positive disease. Exclusions included prior invasive cancer, diagnostic excision before therapy, <75% of planned chemotherapy, additional/adjuvant systemic therapy beyond endocrine/HER2 therapy, inflammatory or stage IV disease, incomplete treatment, or unresectability; cohort-specific criteria were not stated Residual Cancer Burden index after NACT (RCB-0/pCR, RCB-I, RCB-II, RCB-III) Primary: relapse-free survival. Secondary: distant relapse-free survival, overall survival Residual Cancer Burden graded prognosis after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, but its relationship with 10-year RFS varied by phenotype. It was independently prognostic in TNBC and trastuzumab-treated HER2-positive disease, while HR-positive/HER2-negative class rates were non-monotonic and chemotherapy-only HER2-positive RCB-II and RCB-III rates did not separate.

records.title: EBCTCG adjuvant bisphosphonate meta-analysis
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Bone-targeted adjuvant therapy (bisphosphonates) · N/A · 2015
records.body: Unconfounded randomized early-breast-cancer trials begun before 2008 comparing any adjuvant bisphosphonate with placebo/open control and otherwise similar treatment. Individual data were available for 18,766 women in 26 trials; trial-specific stage, organ-function and other patient criteria were heterogeneous and not restated Bisphosphonate (zoledronate, clodronate, ibandronate, etc.) vs control Recurrence, distant recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, overall mortality, death without recurrence, bone recurrence, other distant recurrence, locoregional recurrence, contralateral breast cancer, fractures Adjuvant bisphosphonates reduced bone recurrence overall and reduced recurrence, distant recurrence and breast-cancer mortality among postmenopausal women; no benefit was apparent premenopausally. Menopausal-status heterogeneity was borderline for bone recurrence and correlated with age, and no preferred agent, schedule or duration was established.

records.title: ASCO Guideline (Visvanathan et al.)
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Primary prevention — endocrine chemoprevention · N/A · 2019
records.body: Women without prior breast cancer who were at increased risk. Anastrozole, exemestane and raloxifene recommendations apply only after menopause; tamoxifen may be used in eligible women aged >=35 who have completed childbearing. Risk selection included atypical hyperplasia/LCIS or sufficiently elevated modelled risk; agent-specific contraindications and bone/thromboembolic/endometrial risks apply Risk-reduction options: anastrozole 1 mg/day ×5 years (postmenopausal), exemestane, raloxifene, or tamoxifen; tamoxifen 20 mg/day ×5 years for eligible premenopausal women Breast-cancer incidence, adverse effects For postmenopausal women at increased breast-cancer risk, the guideline adds anastrozole 1 mg daily for 5 years as an option alongside exemestane, raloxifene or tamoxifen; selection should reflect baseline risk and adverse-effect profile. Aromatase inhibitors and raloxifene are not recommended for premenopausal risk reduction, for whom tamoxifen remains the endocrine option after childbearing.

records.title: SUBITO
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · High-dose chemotherapy & autologous stem-cell transplant · III · 2026
records.body: Stage IIIA-C, HER2-negative breast cancer with homologous recombination deficiency (germline BRCA1/2 mutation or HRD tumour testing), newly diagnosed, age 18-66 (Netherlands + France) Intensified alkylating chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell rescue (dose-dense AC then high-dose cyclophosphamide–thiotepa–carboplatin + ASCT) vs standard-of-care (dose-dense AC then carboplatin–paclitaxel) followed by adjuvant olaparib ×1 year Primary: overall survival. Secondary: recurrence-free survival, pathological complete response rate, toxicity, quality of life, cost-effectiveness Intensified chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell rescue did not improve 4-year OS, RFS or pCR versus chemotherapy plus olaparib in this small HRD stage III trial. The null superiority result is not equivalence, and intensified treatment markedly increased grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia, febrile neutropenia and serious adverse events; olaparib's independent contribution was not tested.

records.title: SENOMAC
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · III · 2024
records.body: Clinically node-negative T1–3 breast cancer with 1–2 sentinel-node macrometastases (>2 mm); mastectomy or BCS; ~89% received nodal radiotherapy Completion axillary-lymph-node dissection vs sentinel-node biopsy only (omission of completion ALND); adjuvant systemic therapy and radiotherapy per national guidelines Primary: overall survival. Secondary: recurrence-free survival, breast-cancer-specific survival, arm morbidity, quality of life Omitting axillary dissection was non-inferior for 5-year recurrence-free survival in the 2024 publication (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.66–1.19; margin 1.44). The primary overall-survival endpoint matured only in the 2026 conference abstract (HR 0.84, 0.64–1.12), so publication and abstract maturity should remain distinct; omission improved arm symptoms and function.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2024;390:1163-1175  38598571 J Clin Oncol 2026;44(suppl):LBA503 (ASCO 2026 abstract) overall survival & arm morbidity

records.title: ACOSOG Z0011 (Alliance)
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · III · 2011
records.body: Clinical T1-T2 breast cancer, no palpable adenopathy, 1-2 positive sentinel nodes, lumpectomy + whole-breast irradiation Randomised after a positive sentinel node to sentinel lymph node dissection (SLND) alone (no further axillary surgery) vs completion axillary lymph node dissection (ALND, levels I–II). Both arms received breast-conserving surgery, whole-breast tangential-field radiotherapy, and adjuvant systemic therapy (chemotherapy and/or endocrine therapy) at the treating team's discretion; no protocol-specified systemic regimen or dose Primary: overall survival, surgical morbidity. Secondary: disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival, locoregional recurrence Sentinel-node dissection alone was non-inferior to axillary dissection for 10-year OS (86.3% vs 83.6%; HR 0.85; upper confidence limit 1.16; margin 1.3). DFS and locoregional recurrence did not differ, but the trial closed early, accrued fewer deaths than planned and the completed-follow-up OS analysis was not prespecified.

records.title: AMAROS
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · III · 2014
records.body: Clinically node-negative (no palpable lymphadenopathy) T1–2 primary invasive breast cancer (initially unifocal ≤3 cm; amended Feb 2008 to include ≤5 cm and/or multifocal) with a tumour-positive sentinel node; ~82% breast-conserving surgery, ~18% mastectomy; 34 centres, 9 European countries; enrolled 2001–2010. Median follow-up 6.1 years (IQR 4.1–8.0) in sentinel-node-positive patients. EORTC 10981-22023; NCT00014612 Randomised before sentinel-node biopsy to axillary lymph-node dissection (levels I–II, ≥10 nodes) within 12 weeks vs axillary radiotherapy (levels I–III plus medial supraclavicular fossa; 25 × 2 Gy) starting within 12 weeks; allocated treatment delivered only if the sentinel node was positive. Breast surgery and adjuvant systemic therapy were given in both arms Primary: axillary recurrence. Secondary: axillary recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, overall survival, shoulder mobility, lymphoedema, quality of life Axillary radiotherapy and dissection produced very low 5-year axillary-recurrence rates, but formal non-inferiority of radiotherapy was not established because the confidence interval crossed the HR margin. DFS and OS did not differ; radiotherapy caused substantially less clinical lymphoedema at 1, 3 and 5 years.

records.title: MINDACT
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2016
records.body: Women aged 18-70 with histologically confirmed primary invasive T1-2 or operable T3 breast cancer; initially node-negative, later amended to allow up to three positive nodes. Clinical risk used modified Adjuvant! Online and genomic risk the 70-gene signature. Detailed laboratory and exclusion criteria were in an unfiled protocol/supplement Discordant clinical/genomic-risk groups were randomized to adjuvant chemotherapy versus no chemotherapy; concordant high-risk received chemotherapy and concordant low-risk did not. Chemotherapy regimen/duration were not protocol-uniform in the bound article Primary: distant-metastasis-free survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, overall survival Clinically high-risk, genomically low-risk women who omitted chemotherapy had 5-year distant-metastasis-free survival of 94.7%. The randomized chemotherapy comparison in that discordant group was underpowered and inconclusive (adjusted HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.50–1.21), so the result supports risk-informed de-escalation without proving chemotherapy is universally unnecessary or safe to omit.

records.title: TAILORx
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2018
records.body: Women aged 18-75 with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative, axillary node-negative breast cancer meeting NCCN criteria for recommended or considered adjuvant chemotherapy, with tumour available for the 21-gene assay. Full stage, organ-function and exclusion criteria were in an unfiled supplement Recurrence score 11–25: endocrine therapy alone (median 5.4 years; agent details unfiled) vs chemotherapy followed by endocrine therapy; among chemotherapy-treated patients, 56% received docetaxel–cyclophosphamide and 36% an anthracycline-containing regimen, with schedules and durations unfiled. Score ≤10 received endocrine therapy and score ≥26 chemoendocrine therapy non-randomly Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: distant recurrence-free interval, recurrence-free interval, overall survival For recurrence scores 11–25, endocrine therapy alone was non-inferior to chemoendocrine therapy for invasive DFS (HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.94–1.24). Age and recurrence-score interactions were prespecified exploratory analyses: younger women with scores 16–25 had signals of chemotherapy benefit, but these analyses did not demonstrate an OS advantage.

records.title: RxPONDER (SWOG S1007)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2021
records.body: Adults with HR-positive/HER2-negative, non-inflammatory N1 breast cancer without distant metastases after primary surgery, eligible for taxane- and/or anthracycline-containing chemotherapy and with tumour available for the 21-gene assay. Recurrence score >25 was ineligible; score 0-25 permitted randomisation. Full protocol criteria and allowed regimens were not filed Endocrine therapy alone vs chemotherapy followed by endocrine therapy; specific agents, schedules and durations were unavailable because the protocol was not filed Primary: invasive disease-free survival, recurrence-score–treatment interaction. Secondary: distant relapse-free survival, overall survival Chemotherapy did not improve invasive DFS in postmenopausal women with 1–3 positive nodes and recurrence score ≤25 (HR 1.02), but did in premenopausal women (HR 0.60). The continuous recurrence-score-by-treatment interaction was null and the menopausal analysis was exploratory; OS was immature.

records.title: Paik et al. (NSABP B-20 validation)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2006
records.body: Parent NSABP B-20: ER-positive, axillary node-negative invasive breast cancer randomized to 5 years tamoxifen with or without CMF/MF. Retrospective assay cohort additionally required an archived block with >=5% tumour, RNA >=0.5 microgram and adequate RT-PCR signal; 651 of 2,299 clinically eligible patients were assay-evaluable. Other parent-protocol criteria were not filed Parent NSABP B-20: tamoxifen 20 mg/day ×5 years alone versus tamoxifen plus CMF or MF chemotherapy; retrospective 21-gene Recurrence Score testing of archived tumour compared chemotherapy effects across score strata Primary: distant recurrence-free survival. Secondary: relapse-free survival, overall survival In the 651 assessable NSABP B-20 samples, recurrence score was associated with chemotherapy benefit for distant recurrence-free survival (interaction P=.038), with a large estimate in the high-score group and imprecise estimates at low scores. This retrospective correlative analysis does not prospectively validate a treatment-selection rule.

records.title: OPTIMA
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2026
records.body: High clinical-risk ER+/HER2- early breast cancer (0-9 involved nodes; 73% pN1; T>=30 mm if node-negative); women & men >=40 Standard chemotherapy → endocrine therapy (control) vs Prosigna (PAM50) ROR-directed: ROR >60 → chemo→ET, ROR <=60 → endocrine therapy alone; premenopausal ET included ovarian function suppression Primary: invasive breast-cancer-free survival In the bound ASCO 2026 abstract, Prosigna-directed treatment met the stated non-inferiority criterion for 5-year invasive breast-cancer-free survival, with 3.9 years' median follow-up and 280 events. The abstract-only, relatively immature result supports chemotherapy de-escalation in the tested population but does not establish long-term safety of omission.

records.title: ASTER 70s
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2025
records.body: Women >=70 years, ER-positive HER2-negative early breast cancer with genomic-grade-index (GGI) high-risk tumours (France, Belgium) Doxorubicin 60 mg/m², non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 60 mg/m² or docetaxel 75 mg/m², each with cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² every 3 weeks ×4 with mandatory G-CSF, then hormonotherapy for 5 years, vs hormonotherapy alone for 5 years (1:1) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival, breast-cancer-specific survival, safety, quality of life Adding chemotherapy did not improve OS in older patients with genomically high-risk HR-positive/HER2-negative disease (8-year OS 72.7% vs 68.3%; HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.63–1.11, P=.21) and increased grade ≥3 adverse events. The wide interval does not prove equivalence or justify universal omission.

records.title: MA.17 (NCIC CTG)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2003
records.body: Postmenopausal HR+ early breast cancer, disease-free after ~5 years of tamoxifen Extended letrozole x5 yr vs placebo Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, safety Extended letrozole after about 5 years of tamoxifen improved DFS at the first interim analysis (4-year 93% vs 87%; HR 0.57, P=.00008), while statistical significance was not reached for OS (HR 0.76, P=.25). The trial stopped early at 2.4 years median follow-up, so this report establishes an early recurrence benefit rather than a mature survival effect.

records.title: NSABP B-33
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2008
records.body: Postmenopausal HR+ early breast cancer, node-negative or node-positive (clinical T1-3 N0-1 M0), disease-free after 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen Extended exemestane 25 mg once daily ×5 years vs placebo, after 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, relapse-free survival Extended exemestane after tamoxifen produced 4-year DFS of 91% vs 89% (HR 0.68, P=.07) and improved relapse-free survival (HR 0.44, P=.004). Accrual stopped early and 44% of placebo patients crossed over after unblinding, truncating inference; exploratory nodal subgroup results do not define a predictive population.

records.title: BIG 1-98
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2005
records.body: Postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive early breast cancer. The bound first-results report includes 8,010 patients initially assigned to letrozole or tamoxifen monotherapy or one of two sequential-switch strategies; detailed stage, organ-function and exclusion criteria were not restated in the filed article Letrozole 2.5 mg/day ×5 years versus tamoxifen 20 mg/day ×5 years; sequential arms used letrozole→tamoxifen or tamoxifen→letrozole, switching after 2 years for a total 5 years Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, systemic disease-free survival, distant recurrence, safety At the first 25.8-month report, upfront letrozole improved DFS versus tamoxifen (HR 0.81, P=.003) and reduced distant recurrence (HR 0.73, P=.001). This source compares the monotherapy arms only; the sequential-switch arms and later survival maturity were not available in the bound report.

records.title: ATAC
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2002
records.body: Postmenopausal women with operable early breast cancer eligible for 5 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy, randomized to anastrozole, tamoxifen, or their combination; the efficacy interpretation is concentrated in the hormone-receptor-positive subset. The two bound reports do not reproduce every protocol exclusion or organ-function threshold Anastrozole 1 mg/day versus tamoxifen 20 mg/day versus the combination, each planned for 5 years; the combination arm was stopped after the first analysis Primary: disease-free survival, adverse events. Secondary: time to recurrence, distant recurrence, contralateral breast cancer, death after recurrence, overall survival, fractures, serious adverse events At 10 years, anastrozole improved DFS (HR 0.86) and time to recurrence (HR 0.79) over tamoxifen in HR-positive disease. The absolute recurrence difference widened from 2.7% at 5 years to 4.3% at 10 years and remained after treatment completion (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.67–0.98, P=.03); OS did not differ (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.84–1.06, P=.4).

records.title: EBCTCG tamoxifen meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2011
records.body: Randomized trials of about 5 years tamoxifen versus no adjuvant tamoxifen in early breast cancer, with the principal efficacy analysis restricted to ER-positive disease. Contributing trials used heterogeneous stage, nodal, chemotherapy and assay criteria; no harmonized patient-level protocol eligibility was stated ~5 years of tamoxifen vs no adjuvant tamoxifen Recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, all-cause mortality, contralateral breast cancer, uterine cancer 5 years of tamoxifen roughly halved the recurrence rate during years 0–4 (RR 0.53) and cut breast-cancer mortality by about a third throughout 15 years (RR 0.70) in ER-positive disease.

records.title: EBCTCG aromatase inhibitor vs tamoxifen meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2015
records.body: Postmenopausal women with ER-positive early breast cancer in nine randomized trials begun by 2005. Individual-patient data were available for 31,920 of 35,129 randomized patients; trial-specific stage, prior-treatment, organ-function and exclusion criteria were not restated 5y aromatase inhibitor vs 5y tamoxifen vs sequential tamoxifen→AI Recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, death without recurrence, all-cause mortality, second primary cancers, fractures Across 31,920 postmenopausal women, aromatase-inhibitor strategies reduced recurrence versus tamoxifen and 10-year breast-cancer mortality was 12.1% versus 14.2% for 5 years of AI versus tamoxifen. Aromatase inhibitors caused fewer endometrial cancers but more fractures; the comparison does not directly estimate benefit versus no endocrine therapy.

records.title: ATLAS
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2013
records.body: Women disease-free after about 5 years of tamoxifen and considered suitable to continue or stop, randomized in ATLAS; the principal efficacy analysis was the 6,846 patients with ER-positive disease. The trial included additional ER-unknown/negative patients, so 12,894 is the all-randomized denominator, not the ER-positive analysis population Adjuvant tamoxifen 20 mg once daily continued to 10 years vs stopped at 5 years Recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, all-cause mortality, pulmonary embolism, endometrial cancer Continuing tamoxifen to 10 years further reduced recurrence (years 5–14 21.4% vs 25.1%) and breast-cancer mortality (12.2% vs 15.0%; absolute reduction 2.8%), with benefit emerging mainly after year 10, at the cost of more endometrial cancer.

records.title: TEXT & SOFT (exemestane)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2014
records.body: Premenopausal HR+ early breast cancer receiving ovarian suppression Exemestane 25 mg once daily + ovarian suppression (triptorelin) vs tamoxifen 20 mg once daily + ovarian suppression; ×5 years Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: distant recurrence-free interval, freedom from breast cancer, freedom from distant recurrence, overall survival Exemestane plus ovarian suppression reduced recurrence endpoints vs tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression, and the advantage persisted at 12 years. Statistical significance was not reached for OS in the full population (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.78–1.11); time-varying and HER2-negative analyses are supportive rather than a separate confirmatory survival claim.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2014;371:107-118   J Clin Oncol 2023;41:1376-1382 long-term follow-up 36521078

records.title: SOFT
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2015
records.body: Premenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive early breast cancer. Women who remained premenopausal after chemotherapy entered within 8 months of completing it; women not receiving chemotherapy entered within 12 weeks of surgery. Tamoxifen-alone, tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression and exemestane plus ovarian suppression were randomized; detailed protocol criteria were not fully restated in every bound update Tamoxifen 20 mg once daily vs tamoxifen 20 mg once daily + ovarian suppression vs exemestane 25 mg once daily + ovarian suppression (triptorelin); ×5 years Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: freedom from breast cancer, freedom from distant recurrence, distant recurrence-free interval, overall survival, targeted adverse events DFS statistical significance was not reached when ovarian suppression was added to tamoxifen at 5.6 years; DFS and OS improved at 8 years, with a persisting but attenuated 12-year effect and an OS interval that included no effect. Benefit was greatest in women remaining premenopausal after chemotherapy; low-risk chemotherapy-naive patients had excellent outcomes with tamoxifen alone.

records.title: EBCTCG extended AI meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2025
records.body: Postmenopausal ER+ early breast cancer, recurrence-free after ≥5 years of endocrine therapy (12 randomised trials) Further aromatase inhibitor therapy (2–3 or 5 years) vs no further adjuvant endocrine therapy Invasive breast-cancer recurrence, distant recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, death without recurrence, all-cause mortality, fractures, cardiovascular death, second primary cancers Further aromatase-inhibitor therapy reduced recurrence, including distant recurrence, after at least 5 years of prior endocrine therapy, but did not reduce breast-cancer mortality in women previously exposed to an aromatase inhibitor. Absolute recurrence benefit was larger with node-positive disease, fractures increased and non-adherence was common.

records.title: lidERA (BC)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2026
records.body: ER+/HER2- stage I-III early breast cancer after surgery +/- (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy Giredestrant 30 mg PO once daily vs standard-of-care endocrine therapy (anastrozole/letrozole/exemestane or tamoxifen) for 5 years; premenopausal pts on giredestrant or AI received an LHRH agonist Invasive disease-free survival, distant recurrence-free interval Giredestrant iDFS effects were directionally consistent in premenopausal and postmenopausal patients, with similar distant-recurrence-free trends. The linked ASCO 2026 menopausal-status subgroup abstract does not contain the full primary trial report and cannot establish the overall primary result or mature benefit–risk profile.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2026;44(suppl):502 (ASCO 2026 abstract) menopausal-status subgroup; primary iDFS readout Bardia SABCS 2025

records.title: POSITIVE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2023
records.body: Women <=42 years with prior stage I-III HR-positive early breast cancer desiring pregnancy, after 18-30 months of adjuvant endocrine therapy Temporary interruption of endocrine therapy (up to 2 years) to attempt pregnancy vs external control cohort (SOFT/TEXT) Primary: breast-cancer events. Secondary: freedom from breast-cancer event, freedom from distant recurrence, pregnancy, live birth, endocrine-therapy resumption Temporary endocrine-therapy interruption to attempt pregnancy produced 44 breast-cancer events and no excess vs a non-randomized external control at 3 years. With median follow-up of 3.4 years against a planned 10-year endpoint, long-term recurrence safety remains unresolved.

records.title: EBCTCG premenopausal AI vs tamoxifen (ovarian suppression) meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2022
records.body: Premenopausal ER-positive early-stage breast cancer receiving ovarian function suppression (goserelin or triptorelin) or ablation; individual patient data from 4 randomised trials (ABCSG XII, SOFT, TEXT, HOBOE). N=7030 is the ER-positive analysis set (ER-negative/PR-positive women excluded; ~7230 randomised across the four trials) IPD meta-analysis — aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole, exemestane, or letrozole) + ovarian suppression (goserelin or triptorelin) or ablation vs tamoxifen + ovarian suppression; endocrine therapy for 3 years (ABCSG XII) or 5 years (SOFT, TEXT, HOBOE) Recurrence, distant recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, death without recurrence, all-cause mortality, fractures, second primary cancers With ovarian suppression, aromatase inhibitors reduced recurrence versus tamoxifen (RR 0.79; 5-year absolute risk 6.9% vs 10.1%) and distant recurrence (RR 0.83), but did not reduce breast-cancer or all-cause mortality at 8 years' median follow-up. Fractures were more frequent with aromatase inhibitors.

records.title: MA.17R
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2016
records.body: Postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive primary breast cancer, disease-free after 4.5-6 yr of adjuvant aromatase-inhibitor therapy (mostly preceded by tamoxifen); randomized within 2 yr of stopping the AI to 5 more yr of letrozole or placebo (1:1). ECOG <3; no age-only exclusion Extended letrozole 2.5 mg daily x5 yr vs Placebo Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, contralateral breast-cancer incidence, quality of life, safety 5 more years of letrozole after prior AI improved 5-year disease-free survival (95% vs 91%; HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.48–0.91) and reduced contralateral breast cancer (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.22–0.81), with no overall-survival difference (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.73–1.28). The recurrence benefit carried a bone cost: fractures 14% vs 9%, new osteoporosis 11% vs 6%, bone pain 18% vs 14%.

records.title: NSABP B-42
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2019
records.body: Postmenopausal women with stage I-IIIA ER- and/or PR-positive invasive ductal breast cancer, ECOG 0-1 and no recurrence after 57-63 months of an AI or <=3 years of tamoxifen followed by an AI; randomised within 6 months of therapy completion. Prior non-traumatic osteoporotic fracture and bilateral breast cancer were excluded Letrozole 2.5 mg orally once daily x5 yr vs Matching placebo orally once daily x5 yr Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, breast-cancer-free interval, distant recurrence, osteoporotic fractures, arterial thrombotic events An unplanned 10-year update found a modest DFS benefit with extended letrozole (75.9% vs 72.6%; HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74–0.96), after the protocol primary endpoint had been missed earlier. OS was unchanged (86.1% vs 86.2%; HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.82–1.15). Breast-cancer-free interval and distant recurrence favoured letrozole; osteoporotic fractures and arterial thrombotic events did not differ.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2019;20:88-99   J Natl Cancer Inst 2023;115:1302-1309 10-yr update

records.title: IDEAL (Investigation on the Duration of Extended Adjuvant Letrozole treatment); BOOG 2006-05
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2018
records.body: Postmenopausal HR-positive early breast cancer, disease-free after completing 5 years (plus or minus 3 months) of tamoxifen, an aromatase inhibitor, or sequential tamoxifen then an aromatase inhibitor; randomised within 2 years of stopping, with WHO performance status 0-1 Letrozole 2.5 mg once daily x2.5 years vs Letrozole 2.5 mg once daily x5 years Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant-metastasis-free interval, new primary breast malignancy, safety Extending letrozole from 2.5 to 5 years after 5 years of prior endocrine therapy did not improve DFS (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.74–1.16), OS or distant metastasis-free interval. Second primary breast cancer was less frequent with 5 years (1.1% vs 3.1%; HR 0.39), an exploratory secondary finding. Grade 3–4 events comprised 10.0% vs 8.8% of adverse events, and 23.5% vs 17.3% discontinued for toxicity.

records.title: ABCSG-16 / SALSA (Secondary Adjuvant Long-Term Study with Arimidex [anastrozole])
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2021
records.body: Postmenopausal women aged <=80 years with stage I-III invasive HR-positive early breast cancer, recurrence-free after completing 5 years (+/-12 months) of tamoxifen, an aromatase inhibitor, or sequential therapy; prior endocrine therapy completed within 12 months before randomisation Anastrozole 1 mg orally once daily x2 years vs Anastrozole 1 mg orally once daily x5 years; no dose modification; temporary interruption of up to 3 months permitted Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, local recurrence, distant recurrence, contralateral breast cancer, second primary cancer, fractures, serious adverse events, adherence Extending anastrozole from 2 to 5 additional years after 5 years of prior endocrine therapy did not improve DFS in the 3,208 patients still on trial and disease-free at the 2-year landmark (73.9% vs 73.6%; HR 0.99) or OS (87.3% vs 87.5%; HR 1.02). Clinical fractures were more frequent with 5 years (6.3% vs 4.7%; HR 1.35); serious-adverse-event comparisons covered unequal exposure periods.

records.title: monarchE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors (HR+/HER2- high-risk) · III · 2020
records.body: HR-positive/HER2-negative, node-positive high-risk early breast cancer after definitive surgery: >=4 positive nodes, or 1-3 positive nodes plus tumour >=5 cm, grade 3 disease, and in one cohort Ki-67 >=20%. Adjuvant/neoadjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy were allowed as indicated. Metastatic disease was excluded; report-specific protocol details and amendments remain source-bound Abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily ×2 years + standard adjuvant endocrine therapy vs endocrine therapy alone Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: distant relapse-free survival, overall survival, invasive disease-free survival in Ki-67-high disease, quality of life, safety In high-risk node-positive HR-positive/HER2-negative disease, 2 years of abemaciclib added to endocrine therapy improved iDFS and DRFS, and at the prespecified OS analysis improved survival (HR 0.842, 95% CI 0.722–0.981, P=.027; 7-year OS 86.8% vs 85.0%). The claim is confined to the monarchE population and regimen.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2020;38:3987-3998   Lancet Oncol 2023;24:77-90 4-yr interim OS 36493792 Ann Oncol 2026;37:155-165 primary OS analysis 41110697

records.title: NATALEE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors (HR+/HER2- high-risk) · III · 2024
records.body: Adjuvant HR+/HER2- stage II-III early breast cancer (broad, incl. selected node-negative) Ribociclib 400 mg once daily 3 weeks on / 1 week off ×3 years + nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor (letrozole 2.5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg once daily, ≥5 years) vs nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor alone Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: distant disease-free survival, recurrence-free survival, overall survival, safety, quality of life, pharmacokinetics Three years of ribociclib added to a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor improved iDFS, with the absolute difference widening to 4.5 percentage points at 5 years. Statistical significance was not reached for OS (HR 0.800, 95% CI 0.637–1.003); node-negative and other subgroup estimates are supportive.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2024;390:1080-1091   ESMO Open 2025;10:105858 5-yr follow-up, updated OS 41320342

records.title: PALLAS
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors (HR+/HER2- high-risk) · III · 2021
records.body: Adults with completely resected stage II-III HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer enrolled within 12 months of diagnosis and starting endocrine therapy within 6 months before randomisation; adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy was allowed. Full protocol exclusions and organ-function thresholds were in the unfiled appendix Palbociclib 125 mg once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle ×2 years + standard adjuvant endocrine therapy vs endocrine therapy alone Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival excluding second non-breast primaries, distant recurrence-free survival, locoregional recurrence-free survival, overall survival, safety, adherence, quality of life Two years of palbociclib added to endocrine therapy did not improve iDFS in stage II–III HR-positive/HER2-negative disease (3-year 88.2% vs 88.5%; HR 0.93), and the trial stopped for futility. Secondary analyses do not establish benefit.

records.title: PENELOPE-B
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors (HR+/HER2- high-risk) · III · 2021
records.body: HR-positive/HER2-negative residual invasive breast cancer after taxane-containing neoadjuvant chemotherapy, with high relapse risk by CPS-EG score (>=3, or 2 with ypN+), no distant disease and surgery completed. Randomized treatment began after local therapy; detailed protocol exclusions were not all restated in the bound publication Palbociclib 125 mg once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle ×13 cycles (~1 year) + endocrine therapy vs placebo + endocrine therapy Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival excluding second non-breast primaries, distant disease-free survival, overall survival, locoregional relapse-free interval, safety, compliance One year of palbociclib added to endocrine therapy did not improve iDFS in high-risk residual HR-positive/HER2-negative disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (HR 0.93, P=.53). Subgroup and secondary findings do not establish a benefiting population.

records.title: OlympiA
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Escalation for BRCA-mutated disease (PARP inhibition) · III · 2021
records.body: Germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic-variant, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer after local therapy and >=6 cycles of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. TNBC eligibility required residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy or node-positive/T2+ disease after adjuvant therapy; HR-positive eligibility required residual disease with CPS+EG >=3 or >=4 positive nodes. No metastatic disease Olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily ×1 year vs matching placebo orally twice daily ×1 year, with concurrent adjuvant endocrine therapy per local standards for at least 5 years Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: distant disease-free survival, overall survival, quality of life, safety One year of adjuvant olaparib improved 3-year iDFS in germline BRCA1/2-mutated, high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer (85.9% vs 77.1%; HR 0.58) and later improved 4-year OS (89.8% vs 86.4%; HR 0.68, P=.009). The evidence applies to this tested post-chemotherapy population without resolving sequencing with other agents.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2021;384:2394-2405   Ann Oncol 2022;33:1250-1268 overall survival analysis 36228963

records.title: NSABP B-31 / NCCTG N9831 (joint analysis)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2005
records.body: HER2-positive, node-positive (later high-risk node-negative) operable breast cancer AC (doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide) ×4 → paclitaxel + trastuzumab (4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg weekly, begun with the first dose of paclitaxel, to complete 52 weeks) vs AC → paclitaxel alone (joint analysis of the concurrent-trastuzumab and control arms) Primary: overall survival, disease-free survival. Secondary: relapse-free survival, late recurrence patterns, time to recurrence, distant recurrence, breast cancer-specific survival, second primary cancers, cardiac safety Concurrent trastuzumab added to AC→paclitaxel reduced recurrence and mortality; at final follow-up DFS HR was 0.60 and OS HR 0.63, with 10-year DFS 73.7% vs 62.2% and OS 84.0% vs 75.2%. NYHA III/IV heart failure or cardiac death at 3 years occurred in 4.1% in B-31 and 2.9% in N9831.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2005;353:1673-1684   Perez EA et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32:3744-3752 joint 10-yr OS analysis 25332249 Chumsri S et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:3425-3435 late-relapse combined analysis (N9831/B-31) 31622131

records.title: HERA (BIG 1-01)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2005
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer after surgery and at least 4 cycles of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy; node-positive or node-negative tumour >1 cm; LVEF ≥55%; no metastatic disease After locoregional therapy and at least 4 cycles of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy: observation vs trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W for 1 year vs the same for 2 years Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant recurrence, site of first relapse, cardiac safety One year of trastuzumab after chemotherapy improved DFS and OS vs observation; at 11 years DFS HR was 0.76 and OS HR 0.74, with 10-year DFS 69% vs 63%. Two years did not improve DFS vs 1 year (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.89–1.17). Severe cardiotoxicity was uncommon (0.5%).
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2005;353:1659-1672   Cameron D et al. Lancet 2017;389:1195-1205 11-yr final analysis 28215665

records.title: FinHer
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2006
records.body: HER2-positive subset of node-positive or high-risk node-negative operable breast cancer; age ≤65; WHO PS 0–1; randomised within 12 weeks of surgery Docetaxel 100 mg/m² IV day 1 Q3W ×3 (later 80 mg/m²) or vinorelbine 25 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 Q3W ×3 (day 15 omitted in cycle 3), then FEC Q3W ×3; with vs without concurrent trastuzumab 4 mg/kg loading then 2 mg/kg weekly ×8; 18 weeks total, including 9 weeks trastuzumab Primary: distant disease-free survival, recurrence-free survival. Secondary: adverse effects, left ventricular ejection fraction, overall survival, time to distant recurrence At 5 years, 9 weeks of trastuzumab did not establish DDFS improvement (83.3% vs 73.0%; HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.38–1.12), and OS improvement was not established (91.3% vs 82.3%; HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.27–1.11). Symptomatic heart failure occurred in 0.9% vs 1.7%. The mature result supersedes the interim RFS signal and does not establish 9 weeks as equivalent to 1 year.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2006;354:809-820   Joensuu H et al. J Clin Oncol 2009;27:5685-5692 final results, median 62 mo 19884557

records.title: BCIRG 006
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2011
records.body: HER2-positive, node-positive or high-risk node-negative early breast cancer AC (doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide) → docetaxel (AC-T, control) vs AC-T + trastuzumab (AC-TH) vs docetaxel–carboplatin + trastuzumab (TCH); trastuzumab given as 4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg weekly during chemotherapy, then 6 mg/kg Q3W to complete 1 year Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Global safety, Cardiac safety Both trastuzumab regimens improved DFS and OS vs AC-T; at 5 years DFS was 84% with AC-TH and 81% with TCH vs 75%, and OS 92% and 91% vs 87%. TCH caused less CHF and cardiac dysfunction than AC-TH; acute leukaemia occurred in 7 anthracycline-arm patients vs 1 with TCH. The trial was not powered to compare AC-TH directly with TCH, so it supports TCH as an effective, less cardiotoxic non-anthracycline option without proving equivalent efficacy between trastuzumab arms.

records.title: EBCTCG trastuzumab meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · N/A · 2021
records.body: Early-stage, node-negative or node-positive HER2-positive breast cancer (7 randomized trials) Meta-analysis of 7 randomised trials (13,864 women) — chemotherapy plus trastuzumab (adjuvant or neoadjuvant) vs the same chemotherapy alone Primary: any invasive breast cancer recurrence, breast cancer mortality, death without recurrence, all-cause mortality. Secondary: site of first recurrence, distant recurrence, local recurrence, contralateral breast cancer incidence, cardiovascular mortality Adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy reduced breast cancer recurrence (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.62–0.71) and breast cancer mortality (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.61–0.73). Absolute 10-year reductions were 9.0% for recurrence and 6.4% for breast cancer mortality; all-cause mortality also fell, with no evidence of increased death without recurrence. Relative benefit was similar by ER and nodal status; absolute benefit increased with baseline risk.

records.title: PHARE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · III · 2013
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer who received adjuvant trastuzumab Adjuvant trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W: 6 months vs 12 months total duration (non-inferiority) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, metastasis-free survival, cardiac safety Six months of trastuzumab did not establish non-inferiority to 12 months: at 7.5 years DFS HR was 1.08 (95% CI 0.93–1.25) against a 1.15 margin. The estimate is compatible with little difference but its CI crosses the prespecified margin; it does not prove a real excess hazard. Overall survival and metastasis-free survival also showed no clear advantage for shortening. PHARE therefore retained 12 months as standard.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2013;14:741-748   Pivot X et al. Lancet 2019;393:2591-2598 final analysis, 7.5-yr 31178155

records.title: ShortHER
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · III · 2018
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer (adjuvant) 9 weeks vs 1 year of adjuvant trastuzumab (with chemotherapy) Primary: disease-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: 2-year failure rate, cardiac safety Nine weeks of trastuzumab did not establish non-inferiority to 1 year: 10-year DFS HR 1.13 (90% CI 0.89–1.42) against a 1.29 margin; 10-year DFS was 78% vs 77% and OS 88% vs 89% (9 weeks vs 1 year). Accrual stopped at 1,254 rather than the planned 2,332. Outcomes were similar in node-negative and 1–3-node subgroups but poorer with 9 weeks in ≥4-node disease; no subgroup interaction test was reported. Cardiac toxicity was lower with 9 weeks. The study does not support replacing 1 year generally.
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2018;29:2328-2333   Conte P et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:4976-4981 10-yr update 37748109

records.title: PERSEPHONE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · III · 2019
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer receiving adjuvant trastuzumab + chemotherapy Adjuvant trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W (or 600 mg SC): 6 months (9 cycles) vs 12 months (18 cycles) total duration (non-inferiority) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free interval, distant disease-free interval, distant disease-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, breast cancer-specific survival, cardiac safety, quality of life, cost-effectiveness Six months of trastuzumab met the prespecified non-inferiority criterion vs 12 months: 4-year DFS was 89.4% vs 89.8% (HR 1.07, 90% CI 0.93–1.24). Severe adverse events were lower with 6 months (19% vs 24%), as was early stopping for cardiotoxicity (3% vs 8%).
records.keywords: Lancet 2019;393:2599-2612   Earl HM et al. Health Technol Assess 2020;24:1-190 HTA final report 32880572

records.title: NeoSphere
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2012
records.body: HER2-positive locally advanced, inflammatory or early (>2 cm) breast cancer (neoadjuvant) Four neoadjuvant cycles Q3W: trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + docetaxel (group A) vs pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) + trastuzumab + docetaxel (group B) vs pertuzumab + trastuzumab, no chemotherapy (group C) vs pertuzumab + docetaxel (group D); all then surgery, adjuvant FEC, and trastuzumab to complete 1 year Primary: breast pathological complete response rate. Secondary: progression-free survival, disease-free survival, clinical response rate, time to response, breast-conserving surgery rate, safety Adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab–docetaxel increased breast pCR from 29.0% to 45.8% (P=.0141). Chemotherapy-free pertuzumab–trastuzumab produced pCR in 16.8%. Grade ≥3 toxicity and serious adverse events were concentrated in the docetaxel-containing arms; survival comparisons were exploratory.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2012;13:25-32   Gianni L et al. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:791-800 5-yr PFS/DFS analysis 27179402

records.title: TRYPHAENA
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2013
records.body: HER2-positive operable, locally advanced or inflammatory breast cancer (neoadjuvant) Neoadjuvant trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) added to 6 cycles of chemotherapy: FEC → docetaxel with dual blockade throughout (Arm A) vs FEC → docetaxel with dual blockade during docetaxel only (Arm B) vs docetaxel–carboplatin (TCH) with dual blockade throughout (Arm C); trastuzumab continued to complete 1 year Primary: cardiac safety. Secondary: pathological complete response rate, clinical response rate, breast-conserving surgery rate, disease-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety Pertuzumab–trastuzumab with anthracycline-containing or anthracycline-free chemotherapy had low cardiac toxicity: symptomatic LV systolic dysfunction occurred in 2 patients, and LVEF decline ≥10 points to <50% in 3.9–5.6% across arms. Descriptive pCR rates were 61.6%, 57.3% and 66.2%, respectively; the study was not designed to compare efficacy between regimens.
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2013;24:2278-2284   Schneeweiss A et al. Eur J Cancer 2018;89:27-35 long-term (3-yr) DFS analysis 29223479

records.title: TRAIN-2
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer Neoadjuvant trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) concurrent throughout, with FEC ×3 → paclitaxel–carboplatin ×6 (anthracycline) vs paclitaxel–carboplatin ×9 (anthracycline-free); trastuzumab continued to complete 1 year Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, recurrence-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, breast cancer-specific survival, overall survival, breast-conserving surgery rate, safety Adding anthracyclines to neoadjuvant paclitaxel–carboplatin plus trastuzumab–pertuzumab did not improve pCR (67% vs 68%) or show an EFS or OS advantage at 48.8 months; 3-year EFS was 92.7% vs 93.6% (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.50–1.63). Anthracyclines increased grade ≥3 febrile neutropenia (10% vs 1%), severe LVEF decline (7.7% vs 3.2%), and caused 2 acute leukaemias.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2018;19:1630-1640   van der Voort A et al. JAMA Oncol 2021;7:978-984 3-yr EFS/OS analysis 34014249

records.title: TRAIN-3
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2026
records.body: Stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer (hormone receptor-negative and hormone receptor-positive cohorts); multicentre, Netherlands (single-arm) Paclitaxel + carboplatin + trastuzumab + pertuzumab for up to 9 cycles, with MRI-guided surgery at first complete radiological response; pCR: trastuzumab–pertuzumab to complete 1 year; residual disease: complete 9 neoadjuvant cycles then T-DM1 every 3 weeks ×14 cycles Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, pathological complete response rate, radiological response, quality of life, safety MRI-guided early surgery after neoadjuvant paclitaxel–carboplatin–trastuzumab–pertuzumab was feasible: pCR after 3 cycles occurred in about one-third of HR-negative and one-sixth of HR-positive patients; 3-year EFS was 92.2% and 92.0%, respectively. Patients stopping after 1–3 cycles were selected by early radiological response and had favourable outcomes, while toxicity rose with cycle count. This single-arm, response-selected study does not establish that shortening preserves efficacy vs a fixed course.
records.keywords: Louis FM et al. Lancet Oncol 2026;27:349-360

records.title: KRISTINE (TRIO-021)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2018
records.body: HER2-positive stage II-III operable breast cancer (neoadjuvant) Six neoadjuvant cycles Q3W: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) vs docetaxel–carboplatin + trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (TCHP); after surgery the assigned HER2 regimen continued for 12 more cycles (18 cycles total, ~1 year) Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, overall survival, breast-conserving surgery rate, quality of life, safety Neoadjuvant T-DM1–pertuzumab produced lower pCR than TCHP (44.4% vs 55.7%; difference −11.3%, 95% CI −20.5 to −2.0) and worse 3-year EFS (85.3% vs 94.2%; HR 2.61, 95% CI 1.36–4.98), driven by preoperative progression. Surgery-landmark iDFS was similar (93.0% vs 92.0%; HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.52–2.40) but excludes 15 preoperative progressions; OS had only 11 deaths. Grade 3–4 adverse events were lower with T-DM1–pertuzumab (13% vs 64%).
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2018;19:115-126   Hurvitz SA et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:2206-2216 3-yr outcomes 31157583

records.title: DESTINY-Breast11
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2026
records.body: High-risk HER2-positive early breast cancer (neoadjuvant) Neoadjuvant T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W ×8 cycles (alone), or T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg Q3W ×4 → paclitaxel + trastuzumab (6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) ×4 (T-DXd-THP), vs dose-dense AC (doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide Q2W) ×4 → THP ×4 (standard of care); post-neoadjuvant trastuzumab ± pertuzumab to 1 year, or T-DM1 ×14 cycles if residual disease Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, overall survival, residual cancer burden, safety Neoadjuvant T-DXd→THP improved pCR vs dose-dense AC→THP (67.3% vs 56.3%; difference 11.2%, 95% CI 4.0–18.3), while T-DXd alone was inferior (43.0%) and closed early. Grade ≥3 adverse events were 37.5% vs 55.8%; drug-related ILD was about 4% in each comparison arm. EFS was only 4.5% mature (HR 0.56), so survival benefit is not established.

records.title: neoCARHP
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Stage II-III HER2-positive invasive breast cancer, previously untreated (neoadjuvant); multicentre China Six 3-weekly cycles of investigator-selected taxane (docetaxel, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel) + trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W), without carboplatin (THP; docetaxel 100 mg/m²) vs with carboplatin AUC 6 (TCbHP; docetaxel 75 mg/m²); adjuvant trastuzumab ± pertuzumab to complete 1 year, or T-DM1 ×14 cycles if residual disease Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: clinical response rate, breast-conserving surgery rate, event-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, overall survival, safety Omitting carboplatin from neoadjuvant taxane–trastuzumab–pertuzumab was non-inferior for pCR (64.1% vs 65.9%; difference −1.8%, 95% CI −8.5 to 5.0). Grade 3–4 adverse events were lower without carboplatin (20.7% vs 34.6%), as were serious adverse events (1.3% vs 4.7%); EFS and OS remain immature.

records.title: PHERGain-2
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2026
records.body: Treatment-naive, centrally confirmed HER2-positive (IHC 3+), node-negative early breast cancer, tumours 5-30 mm by MRI (single-arm) Fixed-dose SC trastuzumab–pertuzumab every 3 weeks ×8 neoadjuvant cycles (+ endocrine therapy if HR-positive), then surgery; pCR: HP ×10 adjuvant cycles; residual disease/ypN0(i+/mol+)/ypN1mi: T-DM1 ×10 cycles; ypN1–3: chemotherapy permitted then T-DM1 ×10 cycles; adjuvant endocrine therapy ≥5 years if HR-positive Primary: global health status, recurrence-free interval. Secondary: pathological complete response rate, objective response rate, breast-conserving surgery rate, event-free survival, relapse-free survival, disease-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, overall survival, safety Chemotherapy-free neoadjuvant HP achieved pCR in 59.6%; 1-year global health status declined ≥10% in 42.8% of questionnaire respondents. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 86.6% (5.6% grade ≥3), with 1 T-DM1-attributed pneumonitis death. The report is noncomparative and 3-year recurrence-free interval is pending, so it supports feasibility and response-adapted escalation but does not establish efficacy preservation vs chemotherapy.
records.keywords: Garrigós L et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:837-848

records.title: WSG-ADAPT-TP
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2023
records.body: Hormone receptor-positive/HER2-positive early breast cancer, clinical stage I-III 12 weeks of neoadjuvant T-DM1, or T-DM1 + endocrine therapy, or trastuzumab + endocrine therapy (1:1:1); adjuvant chemotherapy optional at investigator discretion after pCR (76 of 117 received it) and mandatory after non-pCR Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival, overall survival, biomarkers T-DM1-based chemotherapy-free neoadjuvant therapy produced higher pCR than trastuzumab + endocrine therapy; 5-year iDFS was 88.9%, 85.3% and 84.6% across the 3 arms, but the trial was not powered for survival and non-pCR patients received mandatory chemotherapy. pCR was associated with better iDFS, yet post-pCR chemotherapy use was nonrandomised. These data identify a favourable response-selected group; they do not prove that chemotherapy can safely be omitted.
records.keywords: Harbeck N et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:3796-3804

records.title: WSG-TP-II
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2026
records.body: Hormone receptor-positive/HER2-positive early breast cancer 12 weeks neoadjuvant trastuzumab + pertuzumab (HP) + endocrine therapy vs HP + weekly paclitaxel (1:1); all received adjuvant dual HER2 blockade; standard chemotherapy mandatory if non-pCR, optional after pCR Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: overall survival, event-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, safety Neoadjuvant HP + paclitaxel produced more pCR than chemotherapy-free HP + endocrine therapy (56.4% vs 23.7%). Five-year OS was 97.9% vs 100%, untested; prespecified EFS-DCIS was 94.8% vs 92.1%. A separate exploratory surgery-landmark iDFS analysis was based on 7 events and gave imprecise, directionally conflicting results. The study supports feasibility of response-guided de-escalation but does not establish survival equivalence or safe chemotherapy omission.
records.keywords: Gluz O et al. J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1974-1980

records.title: Neoadjuvant HER2+ therapy NMA (Villacampa)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · N/A · 2023
records.body: Operable / local-regionally advanced HER2+ breast cancer (neoadjuvant; 46 RCTs, 32 regimens) Network meta-analysis of neoadjuvant anti-HER2 regimens (trastuzumab +/- pertuzumab or TKI; +/- anthracycline; +/- carboplatin) Primary: pathological complete response. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, safety, trial-level pathological-complete-response–survival association Across 46 neoadjuvant RCTs, dual HER2 blockade + chemotherapy improved pCR and network estimates of EFS and OS vs trastuzumab + chemotherapy, with more cardiotoxicity. Anthracycline-containing regimens were not superior to non-anthracycline regimens; carboplatin-containing anthracycline-free regimens ranked favourably. Indirect comparisons and trial heterogeneity do not establish a single preferred regimen.

records.title: APHINITY
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant dual blockade & post-neoadjuvant escalation · III · 2017
records.body: HER2-positive, node-positive or high-risk node-negative early breast cancer Standard adjuvant chemotherapy (anthracycline → taxane, or docetaxel–carboplatin ×6) + trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) vs + placebo; anti-HER2 therapy from the first taxane cycle to complete 1 year (max 18 cycles) Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free survival, relapse-free interval, distant relapse-free interval, quality of life, cardiac safety, overall safety Adjuvant pertuzumab modestly improved iDFS vs placebo when added to chemotherapy–trastuzumab (8-year HR 0.77). Descriptive estimates favoured node-positive disease (HR 0.72) but not node-negative disease (HR 1.01); the nodal interaction did not reach statistical significance. OS remained immature and did not reach statistical significance (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.68–1.02; P=.078). Grade ≥3 diarrhoea was about 10% vs 4%.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2017;377:122-131   Loibl S et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:3643-3651 third interim OS / 8.4-yr 39259927 Loibl S et al. ESMO Breast Cancer 2025, LBA1 final analysis 11.3-yr (congress abstract, pending full publication)

records.title: KATHERINE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant dual blockade & post-neoadjuvant escalation · III · 2019
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemo + HER2 therapy Adjuvant T-DM1 (trastuzumab emtansine) 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W vs trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV Q3W (8 mg/kg loading), ×14 cycles, for residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane + trastuzumab Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free survival, distant recurrence-free survival, safety Post-neoadjuvant T-DM1 improved iDFS and OS vs trastuzumab in residual HER2-positive invasive disease. At the final iDFS analysis, iDFS HR was 0.54 (7-year iDFS 80.8% vs 67.1%); at the second interim OS analysis, OS HR was 0.66 (95% CI 0.51–0.87; 7-year OS 89.1% vs 84.4%). Grade ≥3 adverse events were more frequent with T-DM1 (26.1% vs 15.7%); grade ≥3 thrombocytopenia occurred in 5.7% vs 0.3%.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2019;380:617-628   Geyer CE et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392:249-257 OS analysis 39813643

records.title: DESTINY-Breast05
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant dual blockade & post-neoadjuvant escalation · III · 2026
records.body: High-risk HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease (breast and/or axilla) after neoadjuvant therapy Post-neoadjuvant T-DXd (trastuzumab deruxtecan) 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W vs T-DM1 (trastuzumab emtansine) 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W, ×14 cycles, for residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane + trastuzumab Primary: Invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, Overall survival, Distant recurrence-free interval, Brain metastasis-free interval, Safety Post-neoadjuvant T-DXd improved iDFS vs T-DM1 (3-year iDFS 92.4% vs 83.7%; HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.34–0.66). Drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 9.6% vs 1.6%, with 2 T-DXd-related ILD deaths. OS is immature.

records.title: ExteNET
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Extended adjuvant therapy · III · 2016
records.body: HER2-positive stage I–III operable breast cancer without recurrence after (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy and trastuzumab; protocol later narrowed to stage II–III node-positive disease and enrolment within 1 year of trastuzumab Extended adjuvant neratinib 240 mg orally once daily ×1 year vs placebo, begun after completion of trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, time to distant recurrence, distant disease-free survival, CNS recurrence, overall survival, safety Extended adjuvant neratinib improved 5-year iDFS vs placebo (90.2% vs 87.7%; HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.57–0.92). Hormone-receptor-positive and within-1-year subgroup estimates were exploratory; interaction tests did not establish differential benefit (P=.063 and P=.406). Grade 3 diarrhoea occurred in 40% without mandated prophylaxis; OS was not analysed at this cut.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2016;17:367-377   Martin M et al. Lancet Oncol 2017;18:1688-1700 5-yr iDFS analysis 29146401

records.title: APT (Adjuvant Paclitaxel + Trastuzumab)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · De-escalation for low-risk / node-negative disease · II · 2015
records.body: HER2-positive invasive tumours <=3 cm, node-negative, or one nodal micrometastasis after axillary dissection with no further involvement (small, low-risk) (single-arm) Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly ×12 + trastuzumab (4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg weekly ×12), then trastuzumab monotherapy (6 mg/kg every 3 weeks or weekly) to complete 1 year Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: recurrence-free interval, breast cancer-specific survival, overall survival, biomarkers, safety Weekly paclitaxel–trastuzumab followed by trastuzumab to complete 1 year produced 10-year iDFS 91.3%, recurrence-free interval 96.3%, OS 94.3% and breast cancer-specific survival 98.8% in this single-arm, predominantly stage I cohort. Grade 3 neuropathy occurred in 3.2% and symptomatic heart failure in 0.5%. Without a comparator, the study provides a low-risk outcome benchmark rather than a comparative efficacy estimate.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2015;372:134-141   Tolaney SM et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:1868-1875 7-yr DFS analysis 30939096 Lancet Oncol 2023;24:273-285 10-yr final analysis 36858723

records.title: ATEMPT
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · De-escalation for low-risk / node-negative disease · II · 2021
records.body: Centrally confirmed HER2-positive stage I invasive breast cancer, tumour <=2 cm, node-negative or one nodal micrometastasis (N1mi) Adjuvant T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W ×17 cycles vs paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly ×12 + trastuzumab (4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg weekly), then trastuzumab 6 mg/kg Q3W ×39 weeks (TH); both to complete 1 year Primary: clinically relevant toxicity, invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: recurrence-free interval, quality of life, safety T-DM1 produced 5-year iDFS 97.0%, recurrence-free interval 98.3% and breast cancer-specific survival 99.4% in stage I HER2-positive disease. Clinically relevant toxicity was not reduced vs paclitaxel–trastuzumab (46% vs 47%, P=.83); the toxicity profile shifted from neuropathy and alopecia toward thrombocytopenia and transaminitis. Efficacy was not designed as a between-arm comparison.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2021;39:2375-2385   Tarantino P et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:3652-3665 5-yr results 38935923

records.title: GeparSixto
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · II · 2014
records.body: Neoadjuvant stage II–III triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC cohort of GeparSixto) Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² weekly + non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m² weekly + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg Q3W for 18 weeks, with vs without weekly carboplatin AUC 2.0 (reduced to AUC 1.5 during the trial) Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: disease-free survival, overall survival, alternative pathological complete response rates, treatment delivery, safety Adding carboplatin to the GeparSixto TNBC regimen increased pathological complete response (53.2% vs 36.9%, P=.005) and improved 3-year DFS at later analysis (86.1% vs 75.8%; HR 0.56, P=.022); OS did not differ. Haematologic toxicity increased, and the HRD score did not predict differential platinum benefit.
