records.title: CALGB 40603 (Alliance)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · II · 2015
records.body: Previously untreated, operable, biopsy-confirmed stage II-III non-inflammatory invasive TNBC (ER/PR <=10%; HER2 IHC 0-1+ or non-amplified), with adequate marrow, renal, hepatic and cardiac function. Grade >=2 neuropathy or bevacizumab contraindications were excluded. The long-term analysis used the 443 patients who started protocol treatment Weekly paclitaxel → dose-dense doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide (ddAC) as neoadjuvant backbone; 2×2 factorial ± carboplatin AUC 6 IV Q3W ×4 and/or bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV Q2W ×9 Primary: breast pathological complete response rate, breast-and-axillary pathological complete response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, distant recurrence-free interval, residual cancer burden, treatment delivery, safety Adding carboplatin increased pathological complete response in breast and axilla (54% vs 41%, P=.003), but no EFS or OS improvement was established at 7.9 years in this phase 2 trial, which was not powered for survival. Pathological complete response was strongly prognostic for patients, but the randomized treatment effect did not establish a survival benefit; correlative immune findings were exploratory.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2015;33:13-21   J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1323-1334 long-term outcomes 35044810

records.title: BrighTNess
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · III · 2018
records.body: Neoadjuvant stage II–III triple-negative breast cancer All arms: weekly paclitaxel ×12 then AC ×4. Randomization 2:1:1 to carboplatin AUC6 every 3 weeks ×4 + veliparib, carboplatin alone, or paclitaxel alone before AC Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival Carboplatin increased pCR and improved EFS versus paclitaxel alone, whereas veliparib added no pCR benefit beyond carboplatin. The EFS comparison was secondary, so the data support carboplatin's contribution without a confirmatory survival claim for veliparib.

records.title: TMC TNBC Platinum Trial (Gupta)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · III · 2026
records.body: Women aged 18-80 with previously untreated invasive TNBC, stage II or locally advanced stage III, ECOG 0-1 and adequate organ function; metastatic disease was excluded Weekly carboplatin AUC 2 + weekly paclitaxel ×8 weeks → anthracycline (doxorubicin or epirubicin)–cyclophosphamide Q3W ×4 (neoadjuvant) vs the same taxane–anthracycline backbone without carboplatin Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, pathological complete response rate Adding carboplatin missed the primary EFS endpoint (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.62–1.03, P=.081). OS and pathological complete response favoured carboplatin only in secondary analyses, and the menopausal-status interaction and premenopausal subgroup estimates are hypothesis-generating rather than proof that benefit is confined by menopausal status.

records.title: KEYNOTE-522
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2020
records.body: High-risk stage II–III triple-negative breast cancer (neoadjuvant/adjuvant) Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W + carboplatin–paclitaxel ×4 cycles → pembrolizumab + AC/EC ×4 cycles, then adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×9 cycles vs placebo + the same chemotherapy backbone → adjuvant placebo Primary: pathological complete response rate, event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, alternative pathological complete response rates, distant progression-free survival, distant recurrence-free survival, residual cancer burden, safety Adding pembrolizumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, then continuing it adjuvantly, increased pCR (64.8% vs 51.2%). At the fourth interim analysis, it improved EFS (36-month 84.5% vs 76.8%; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.48–0.82, P<.001). At the final OS analysis, 5-year OS was 86.6% vs 81.7% (P=.002), and updated EFS had HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51–0.83). Grade ≥3 immune-mediated events were 13.0% vs 1.5%, and treatment-related deaths 0.5% vs 0.3%.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2020;382:810-821   N Engl J Med 2022;386:556-567 event-free survival interim analysis 35139274 N Engl J Med 2024;391:1981-1991 final overall survival (filed col K) 39282906 Ann Oncol 2024;35:429-436 RCB exploratory analysis 38369015

records.title: NeoPACT
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · II · 2024
records.body: Stage I-III triple-negative breast cancer (neoadjuvant; single-arm) (single-arm) Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks + carboplatin–docetaxel ×6 cycles (anthracycline-free) Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: residual cancer burden, event-free survival, safety, biomarkers Anthracycline-free carboplatin–docetaxel plus pembrolizumab produced pCR in 58% and 3-year EFS of 86% in this single-arm phase 2 study. Outcomes differed strongly by pCR, but without a randomized comparator the regimen cannot be judged equivalent or superior to an anthracycline-containing standard.

records.title: GeparNuevo (durvalumab)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · II · 2019
records.body: Early triple-negative breast cancer (cT1b-cT4a-d) Durvalumab 1.5 g IV Q4W (0.75 g window dose 2 weeks before chemotherapy) + nab-paclitaxel → dose-dense epirubicin–cyclophosphamide (neoadjuvant) vs placebo + the same chemotherapy backbone; no adjuvant checkpoint continuation Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival, overall survival, alternative pathological complete response rates, clinical outcomes, surgical outcomes Adding neoadjuvant durvalumab did not improve pathological complete response (53.4% vs 44.2%; OR 1.45, P=.287). Long-term secondary iDFS, distant-DFS and OS estimates favoured durvalumab, but the small phase 2 study provides no confirmatory survival evidence; the apparent response–survival discordance remains hypothesis-generating.
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2019;30:1279-1288   J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1580-1586 long-term analysis 42008768

records.title: CREATE-X (JBCRG-04)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — post-neoadjuvant therapy (residual disease) · III · 2017
records.body: HER2-negative (TNBC and HR+) residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant anthracycline/taxane Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily, days 1–14 Q3W ×8 cycles vs observation (standard postsurgical therapy without capecitabine) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety Adjuvant capecitabine improved DFS and OS vs observation in HER2-negative residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. TNBC subgroup estimates favoured capecitabine (DFS HR 0.58; OS HR 0.52) but were not a primary test; sequencing with other post-neoadjuvant agents was not evaluated.

records.title: RJBC-1501
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin) · III · 2026
records.body: Patients with completely resected early-stage TNBC eligible for adjuvant epirubicin-cyclophosphamide followed by a taxane, with no metastatic disease. The bound article does not provide a more granular harmonized stage/exclusion description beyond the protocol-defined postoperative population Adjuvant EC x4 → taxane + carboplatin (AUC-2 weekly or AUC-5–6 q3wk with docetaxel) vs EC x4 → taxane alone Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: distant disease-free survival, overall survival, toxicity Adding carboplatin to adjuvant epirubicin–cyclophosphamide then taxane improved the primary DFS endpoint (3-year 93.1% vs 89.8%; HR 0.66, P=.034). Distant DFS and OS also favoured carboplatin as secondary outcomes; grade 3–4 haematologic toxicity increased.

records.title: OlympiA
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — adjuvant targeted therapy (germline BRCA-mutated) · III · 2021
records.body: Germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic-variant, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer after local therapy and >=6 cycles of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. TNBC eligibility required residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy or node-positive/T2+ disease after adjuvant therapy; HR-positive eligibility required residual disease with CPS+EG >=3 or >=4 positive nodes. No metastatic disease Adjuvant olaparib 300 mg twice daily ×1 year vs placebo Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: distant disease-free survival, overall survival, quality of life, safety One year of adjuvant olaparib improved 3-year iDFS (85.9% vs 77.1%; HR 0.58, P<.001) and distant DFS in germline BRCA1/2-mutated, high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer, and later improved 4-year OS (89.8% vs 86.4%; HR 0.68, P=.009). Anaemia increased; MDS/AML did not.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2021;384:2394-2405   Ann Oncol 2022;33:1250-1268 overall survival analysis 36228963

records.title: IMpassion130
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated metastatic/unresectable locally advanced TNBC (PD-L1 IC+ subgroup primary) Atezolizumab 840 mg IV days 1 & 15 of a 28-day cycle + nab-paclitaxel vs placebo + nab-paclitaxel; to progression Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, response duration, quality of life, safety Atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel improved ITT PFS (HR 0.80, P=.002), but statistical significance was not reached for final ITT OS (HR 0.87, P=.077). The PD-L1-positive OS estimate (25.4 vs 17.9 months; HR 0.67) remained descriptive and cannot support a confirmatory subgroup survival claim.

records.title: KEYNOTE-355
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2020
records.body: Untreated locally recurrent inoperable/metastatic TNBC (PD-L1 CPS ≥10 subgroup) Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) + chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine–carboplatin) vs placebo + the same chemotherapy Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, response duration, disease control, safety Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy improved PFS and OS in the PD-L1 CPS ≥10 population (OS 23.0 vs 16.1 months; HR 0.73, P=.0185). Benefit below CPS 10 was not established, and without a reported treatment-by-PD-L1 interaction the nested CPS populations do not prove benefit was confined to CPS ≥10.
records.keywords: Lancet 2020;396:1817-1828   N Engl J Med 2022;387:217-226 final OS analysis 35857659

records.title: IMpassion131
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated advanced TNBC (PD-L1 IC+ primary analysis) Atezolizumab 840 mg IV on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle + paclitaxel 90 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8 and 15 versus placebo + the same paclitaxel; continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, quality of life, safety Atezolizumab plus solvent-based paclitaxel did not improve PFS in PD-L1-positive disease (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.60–1.12, P=.20), and OS numerically favoured placebo in both PD-L1-positive and ITT analyses. The trial does not establish corticosteroid or taxane formulation as the cause and does not itself support a regulatory or cross-trial inference.

records.title: ASCENT-04 (KEYNOTE-D19)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated PD-L1+ (CPS ≥10) locally advanced/metastatic TNBC Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 & 8 of a 21-day cycle + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) vs chemotherapy (physician's choice — taxane or gemcitabine–carboplatin) + pembrolizumab Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, response duration, time to response, quality of life, safety Sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab improved PFS versus chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab in first-line PD-L1 CPS ≥10 mTNBC (11.2 vs 7.8 months; HR 0.65, P<.001) and prolonged response duration. OS was immature and not formally tested, so the result is PFS-led pending survival maturity.

records.title: ASCENT-03
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line TROP2 ADCs (immunotherapy-ineligible) · III · 2025
records.body: Untreated advanced TNBC ineligible for PD-(L)1 inhibitors (PD-L1-negative or prior IO) Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 & 8 of a 21-day cycle vs chemotherapy (physician's choice — paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, or gemcitabine–carboplatin) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, response duration, time to response, safety First-line sacituzumab govitecan improved PFS versus single-agent chemotherapy in checkpoint-inhibitor-ineligible mTNBC (9.7 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.62, P<.001) and prolonged response duration. OS was descriptive without formal testing. Grade ≥3 neutropenia was frequent in both arms (43% vs 41%); adverse-event discontinuation was less frequent with sacituzumab govitecan (4% vs 12%).

records.title: TROPION-Breast02
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line TROP2 ADCs (immunotherapy-ineligible) · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated advanced TNBC for whom immunotherapy was not an option Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) 6 mg/kg IV Q3W vs investigator's choice chemotherapy (paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, carboplatin, eribulin, or capecitabine) Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, response duration, disease control, quality of life, safety Datopotamab deruxtecan improved PFS (HR 0.57) and OS (HR 0.79) versus chemotherapy in checkpoint-inhibitor-ineligible mTNBC. ORR was higher, and adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis occurred in 3%, including one grade 5 event. No head-to-head comparison with another ADC was performed.

records.title: ASCENT
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — pretreated disease (antibody-drug conjugates) · III · 2021
records.body: Relapsed/refractory metastatic TNBC, ≥2 prior chemotherapy lines (no active brain metastases) Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 & 8 of a 21-day cycle vs single-agent chemotherapy (physician's choice — eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine, or gemcitabine) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, response duration, time to response, safety Sacituzumab govitecan improved PFS, OS and response versus chemotherapy in the brain-metastasis-negative primary population; the final ITT analysis including patients with brain metastases confirmed an OS benefit (11.8 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.42–0.63). Grade ≥3 neutropenia and diarrhoea were common; this trial did not compare first-line regimens.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2021;384:1529-1541   J Clin Oncol 2024;42:1738-1744 final results 38422473

records.title: DESTINY-Breast04
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — pretreated disease (antibody-drug conjugates) · III · 2022
records.body: Pretreated HER2-low metastatic breast cancer (exploratory HR-negative/TNBC cohort, n=58) Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W vs physician's choice chemotherapy (eribulin, capecitabine, gemcitabine, paclitaxel, or nab-paclitaxel) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, response duration, safety In the exploratory HR-negative cohort of 58 patients, T-DXd had median PFS of 8.5 vs 2.9 months (HR 0.46) and median OS of 18.2 vs 8.3 months (HR 0.48). This small subgroup does not independently establish efficacy for TNBC.

records.title: OlympiAD
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — germline BRCA-mutated disease (PARP inhibitors & platinum) · III · 2017
records.body: Germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer (≤2 prior chemotherapy lines) Olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily vs physician’s-choice single-agent capecitabine, eribulin or vinorelbine, each until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival 2, objective response rate, response duration, quality of life, safety Olaparib improved PFS (7.0 vs 4.2 months; HR 0.58, P<.001) and response vs physician-choice chemotherapy in germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. Final OS improvement was not established overall (HR 0.90), and the first-line metastatic subgroup finding was exploratory; platinum was not a comparator.

records.title: EMBRACA
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — germline BRCA-mutated disease (PARP inhibitors & platinum) · III · 2018
records.body: Germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (≤3 prior chemotherapy lines) Talazoparib 1 mg orally once daily vs physician’s-choice single-agent capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine or vinorelbine, each until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, clinical benefit, response duration, quality of life, safety Talazoparib improved PFS vs physician-choice chemotherapy (8.6 vs 5.6 months; HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41–0.71, P<.001). Statistical significance was not reached for final OS (19.3 vs 19.5 months; HR 0.848, 95% CI 0.670–1.073, P=.17). Time to definitive deterioration in global health status/quality of life was longer (26.3 vs 6.7 months; HR 0.385), while grade 3–4 haematologic adverse events were more frequent (56.6% vs 38.9%).

records.title: TNT (CRUK/07/012)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — germline BRCA-mutated disease (PARP inhibitors & platinum) · III · 2018
records.body: First-line advanced/metastatic TNBC or germline BRCA1/2 breast cancer Carboplatin AUC6 IV every 3 weeks ×6 versus docetaxel 100 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks ×6; crossover to the alternate drug was offered at progression Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, crossover response, tolerability, safety Carboplatin and docetaxel had similar response rates in unselected advanced TNBC, but carboplatin produced a higher response rate in germline BRCA carriers (68% vs 33%; treatment–biomarker interaction P=.01). BRCA1 methylation, low BRCA1 mRNA and the tested HRD score did not predict platinum benefit; the finding is specific to the eligible TNT population.

records.body: First-line endocrine-therapy-naive HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer Fulvestrant 500 mg IM (days 0, 14, 28, then every 28 days) vs anastrozole 1 mg once daily; to progression Primary: progression-free survival. records.title: SONIA
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · CDK4/6-inhibitor sequencing & continuation · III · 2024
records.body: First-line HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer (early vs deferred CDK4/6i strategy) Aromatase inhibitor + CDK4/6 inhibitor first line → fulvestrant at progression vs aromatase inhibitor first line → fulvestrant + CDK4/6 inhibitor at progression; each line to progression Primary: progression-free survival after 2 treatment lines. Secondary: progression-free survival after 1 line, overall survival, chemotherapy-free survival, objective response rate, quality of life, cognitive function, cost-effectiveness, biomarkers, safety First-line rather than deferred second-line CDK4/6 inhibition did not improve final OS (47.9 vs 48.1 months; HR 0.91), while updated PFS2 modestly favoured first-line use (HR 0.82). At the primary report, PFS2 superiority was not established (31.0 vs 26.8 months; HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.74–1.03), and first-line treatment caused more toxicity, exposure and cost. The post hoc premenopausal OS result is hypothesis-generating.

Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of response, quality of life, safety Talazoparib improved PFS vs physician-choice chemotherapy (8.6 vs 5.6 months; HR 0.54) and patient-reported outcomes. OS improvement was not established.

records.title: H0648g (pivotal trastuzumab)
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2001
records.body: Untreated HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer First-line trastuzumab 4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg IV weekly (to progression) added to chemotherapy — doxorubicin (or epirubicin)–cyclophosphamide, or paclitaxel if prior adjuvant anthracycline, Q3W for 6 cycles — vs the same chemotherapy alone Primary: time to disease progression, incidence of adverse effects. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, time to treatment failure, overall survival Adding trastuzumab to first-line chemotherapy prolonged time to progression (7.4 vs 4.6 months), increased objective response (50% vs 32%), and improved OS (25.1 vs 20.3 months). Concurrent anthracycline–trastuzumab caused cardiac dysfunction in 27% vs 8% with anthracycline alone, supporting avoidance of that combination.

records.title: CLEOPATRA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2012
records.body: Untreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer Pertuzumab 840 mg loading then 420 mg IV Q3W + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg IV Q3W + docetaxel (≥6 cycles); antibodies to progression vs placebo + trastuzumab + docetaxel (same) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, time to symptom progression, biomarkers, safety Adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab–docetaxel improved PFS (18.5 vs 12.4 months; HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.51–0.75) and final OS (56.5 vs 40.8 months; HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.56–0.84). Eight-year survival was 37% vs 23%, with no added cardiotoxicity.

records.title: HER2CLIMB-05
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2026
records.body: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer without progression after first-line induction with a taxane + trastuzumab + pertuzumab Maintenance tucatinib 300 mg twice daily + trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV Q3W + pertuzumab 420 mg IV Q3W; to progression vs placebo + trastuzumab + pertuzumab (same) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, CNS progression-free survival, safety Adding tucatinib to maintenance trastuzumab–pertuzumab prolonged PFS (24.9 vs 16.3 months; HR 0.641). Subgroup estimates were descriptive; OS was immature.

records.title: DESTINY-Breast09
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated HER2-positive advanced/metastatic breast cancer First-line trastuzumab deruxtecan + pertuzumab vs taxane (paclitaxel or docetaxel) + trastuzumab + pertuzumab (THP); to progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, safety T-DXd–pertuzumab improved interim PFS vs THP (40.7 vs 26.9 months; HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.44–0.71). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 63.5% vs 62.3%.

records.title: PERUSE
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2019
records.body: HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH-positive) unresectable locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer, with no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease except <=2 endocrine lines; stable treated CNS metastases allowed; excluded progression during (neo)adjuvant trastuzumab/lapatinib or recurrence within 6 mo of adjuvant non-hormonal therapy (single-arm) Investigator-selected docetaxel, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel weekly or Q3W + pertuzumab 840 mg loading then 420 mg Q3W + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W; to progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or death Primary: safety and tolerability. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of response, time to response, patient-reported outcomes Mature single-arm PERUSE suggests paclitaxel is a practical taxane alternative with first-line pertuzumab-trastuzumab; at 5.7 years' median follow-up, PFS was 20.7 mo and OS 65.3 mo overall. Paclitaxel and docetaxel subgroups had descriptively similar PFS (23.2 vs 19.4 mo) and OS (64.0 vs 66.5 mo); taxane choice was not randomised and no formal comparisons were performed. ORR was 79%. Grade 3+ neutropenia was 5% with paclitaxel vs 15% with docetaxel and febrile neutropenia 1% vs 11%, while grade 3+ diarrhoea was 9% vs 8%; fatal AEs occurred in 2%.

records.title: EMILIA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Second-line metastatic disease · III · 2012
records.body: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after trastuzumab + a taxane T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W vs lapatinib 1,250 mg once daily + capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle; both to progression Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival, safety. records.title: DESTINY-Breast03
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Second-line metastatic disease · III · 2022
records.body: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after trastuzumab + a taxane T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W vs T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W; to progression Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Objective response, Safety T-DXd improved PFS vs T-DM1 (median not reached vs 6.8 months; HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.22–0.37) and objective response (79.7% vs 34.2%). OS was immature.

records.title: EGF100151 (lapatinib + capecitabine)
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2006
records.body: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer progressing after anthracycline, taxane, and trastuzumab Lapatinib 1250 mg once daily + capecitabine 2000 mg/m² daily days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle vs capecitabine 2500 mg/m² daily days 1–14 alone; to progression Primary: time to progression. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, safety Lapatinib–capecitabine prolonged independently assessed time to progression vs capecitabine alone (8.4 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34–0.71). records.title: TH3RESA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2014
records.body: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after ≥2 HER2-directed regimens (incl. trastuzumab and lapatinib) T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W; to progression vs treatment of physician's choice Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, landmark survival, quality of life, pain, safety T-DM1 improved PFS (6.2 vs 3.3 months; HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.42–0.66) and final OS (22.7 vs 15.8 months; HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.54–0.85) vs physician-choice therapy. Grade ≥3 haemorrhage occurred in 4% vs <1%.

records.title: DESTINY-Breast01
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · II · 2020
records.body: HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic breast cancer after T-DM1 and at least 2 prior anti-HER2 regimens (single-arm) Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks; treatment duration not stated in the bound report Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, time to response, progression-free survival, overall survival, disease-control rate, clinical benefit rate, safety, pharmacokinetics Single-arm T-DXd produced confirmed objective response in 60.9% (95% CI 53.4–68.0) with median PFS 16.4 months after T-DM1. Interstitial lung disease occurred in 13.6%, including 4 fatal events (2.2%); no comparator was included.

records.title: DESTINY-Breast02
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2023
records.body: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after T-DM1 T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W vs treatment of physician's choice — capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg IV Q3W, or capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 + lapatinib 1250 mg once daily; to progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety T-DXd improved PFS (17.8 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.28–0.45) and OS (39.2 vs 26.5 months; HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50–0.86) vs physician-choice therapy after T-DM1. Drug-related ILD occurred in 10% vs <1%, with 2 grade 5 events on T-DXd.

records.title: HER2CLIMB
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2020
records.body: HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic breast cancer after trastuzumab, pertuzumab and T-DM1; brain metastases permitted, including untreated or progressing lesions not requiring immediate local therapy Tucatinib 300 mg twice daily + trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV Q3W (8 mg/kg loading) + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle; to progression vs placebo + trastuzumab + capecitabine (same) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, CNS progression-free survival, objective response rate, safety Tucatinib added to trastuzumab–capecitabine improved PFS (7.8 vs 5.6 months; HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.42–0.71) and OS (21.9 vs 17.4 months; HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50–0.88). In patients with brain metastases, progression or death was reduced (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.34–0.69).

records.title: NALA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2020
records.body: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after ≥2 HER2-directed regimens Neratinib 240 mg once daily + capecitabine 750 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle (with loperamide prophylaxis) vs lapatinib 1250 mg once daily + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14; to progression Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: time to CNS intervention, progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, clinical benefit rate, quality of life, safety Neratinib–capecitabine improved centrally reviewed PFS vs lapatinib–capecitabine (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.63–0.93; 12-month PFS 29% vs 15%) and reduced CNS intervention (22.8% vs 29.2%). OS improvement was not established (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.72–1.07).

records.title: SOPHIA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2021
records.body: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after ≥2 HER2-directed therapies Margetuximab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W + physician's-choice chemotherapy (capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine) vs trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV Q3W (8 mg/kg loading) + the same chemotherapy; to progression Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, safety Margetuximab–chemotherapy modestly improved PFS vs trastuzumab–chemotherapy (5.8 vs 4.9 months; HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.59–0.98). OS benefit was not established at the interim analysis (21.6 vs 19.8 months; HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.69–1.13); the CD16A-158F subgroup signal was exploratory.

records.title: HORIZON-Breast01
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2026
records.body: HER2-positive unresectable/metastatic breast cancer previously treated with a taxane and trastuzumab (advanced-stage) or progressing within 12 months of (neo)adjuvant anti-HER2 antibody + taxane (China, 50 hospitals) Trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR-A1811) 4.8 mg/kg IV day 1 Q3W vs pyrotinib 400 mg once daily + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle; to progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety Trastuzumab rezetecan improved interim PFS vs pyrotinib–capecitabine (30.6 vs 8.3 months; HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.15–0.34, P<.0001). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 70% vs 63%; ILD occurred in 3%. OS was immature.

records.title: PRECIOUS
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2022
records.body: HER2-positive locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer progressing after prior pertuzumab-containing 1st/2nd-line therapy (Japan) Pertuzumab 840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W + physician-choice chemotherapy vs trastuzumab + physician-choice chemotherapy; duration not stated in the bound reports Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, quality of life, safety Pertuzumab retreatment improved investigator-assessed PFS (5.3 vs 4.2 months; HR 0.76), but independent-review PFS was identical (4.4 vs 4.4 months; HR 1.03). Final OS was descriptively longer with retreatment (36.2 vs 26.5 months; HR 0.73), but inferential confirmation was not provided. The open-label, single-country study was underpowered.

records.title: DESTINY-Breast12
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · CNS / brain metastases · N/A · 2024
records.body: HER2-positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer after 1–2 prior anti-HER2 regimens; tucatinib-naive; stable or active brain metastases permitted; leptomeningeal disease excluded (single-arm) Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks until extra-CNS progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal; isolated CNS progression could receive local therapy and continue until second CNS or systemic progression Primary: progression-free survival, objective response rate. Secondary: CNS progression-free survival, overall survival, progression-free survival 2, time to progression, duration of response, new symptomatic CNS metastases, safety T-DXd produced median PFS 17.3 months and intracranial objective response 71.7% in 263 patients with baseline brain metastases, including active lesions; the study was single-arm and excluded prior tucatinib. Interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis occurred in 16%, including grade 5 events in 2.3%.

records.title: PATINA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · HR-positive / HER2-positive — endocrine-containing maintenance · III · 2026
records.body: HR-positive/HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer without progression after first-line induction chemotherapy + HER2 therapy Maintenance palbociclib 125 mg once daily (3 weeks on, 1 week off) + anti-HER2 therapy (trastuzumab + pertuzumab) + endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant); to progression vs anti-HER2 + endocrine therapy alone Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, overall survival, safety Adding maintenance palbociclib prolonged PFS (44.3 vs 29.1 months; HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.59–0.96); OS was immature (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.61–1.23). Grade 3 adverse events occurred in 79.7% vs 30.6%, grade 4 events in 10.0% vs 3.6%, and grade ≥3 neutropenia in 60.5% vs 2.0%.

records.title: NLST (National Lung Screening Trial)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Screening · N/A · 2011
records.body: Age 55-74 years; >=30 pack-year smoking history; current smokers or former smokers who quit within 15 years. Excluded previous lung cancer, chest CT within 18 months, haemoptysis, or unexplained recent weight loss Low-dose multidetector chest CT, three screens (T0, T1, T2) at 1-year intervals; positive if noncalcified nodule at least 4 mm or another suspicious abnormality vs Single-view posteroanterior chest radiography, three screens at the same 1-year intervals; positive if any noncalcified nodule/mass or another suspicious abnormality Primary: Lung-cancer-specific mortality. Secondary: All-cause mortality; lung-cancer incidence; screening performance; diagnostic-evaluation complications Annual low-dose CT screening reduced lung-cancer mortality versus chest radiography: 247 vs 309 deaths per 100,000 person-years, a 20.0% relative reduction (356 vs 443 deaths). All-cause mortality was 6.7% lower. Positive screens occurred in 24.2% vs 6.9%, and 96.4% of CT-positive results were false positive; 1 lung-cancer death was prevented per 320 people screened.

records.title: NELSON (Dutch-Belgian Lung Cancer Screening)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Screening · N/A · 2020
records.body: Age 50-74 years; current smokers or former smokers who quit within 10 years; >15 cigarettes/day for >25 years or >10/day for >30 years. Excluded moderate/severe health limitation, inability to climb two flights, weight >140 kg, specified prior cancers, lung cancer within 5 years, or chest CT within 1 year Volume-based low-dose CT at baseline, year 1, year 3, and year 5.5, with repeat CT for indeterminate nodules and pulmonology referral for positive tests vs No lung-cancer screening Primary: Lung-cancer-specific mortality. Secondary: All-cause mortality; lung-cancer incidence; screening performance; lung-cancer-specific mortality in women 4-round volume-based low-dose CT screening reduced 10-year lung-cancer mortality in men: 2.50 vs 3.30 deaths per 1,000 person-years (rate ratio 0.76). All-cause mortality was unchanged (rate ratio 1.01, 95% CI 0.92-1.11). In women, the lung-cancer mortality rate ratio was 0.67 (0.38-1.14). Across 22,600 CT scans, 1.2% were false positive; no screening adverse events were reported.

records.title: PLUS trial (van Tinteren et al.)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2002
records.body: Suspected operable NSCLC undergoing preoperative staging Conventional workup vs conventional workup + whole-body FDG-PET Futile thoracotomy (surgery not resulting in cure) Adding PET to conventional staging reduced futile thoracotomies from 41% to 21% (relative reduction ~51%) by detecting unsuspected advanced/metastatic disease; established PET in preoperative NSCLC staging.

records.title: Fischer et al. (PET-CT staging)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2009
records.body: Age 18-80 years; newly diagnosed or highly suspected NSCLC considered operable after conventional staging. Excluded confirmed distant metastases, another malignancy, type 1 diabetes, claustrophobia, or estimated postoperative FEV1 <30% Conventional staging plus integrated PET-CT, then mandatory mediastinoscopy and other invasive staging as indicated vs Conventional staging alone, then mandatory mediastinoscopy and other invasive staging as indicated Primary: Futile thoracotomy. Secondary: Total and justified thoracotomies; diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity for operability; relapse; overall survival Adding PET-CT to conventional preoperative staging reduced futile thoracotomy from 42% to 21%, avoiding 1 futile operation per 5 PET-CT scans. Among patients undergoing thoracotomy, futile procedures were 35% vs 52%. Total thoracotomy was also lower (61% vs 80%), without an overall-survival improvement (median 31 vs 49 months).

records.title: Maziak et al. (PET-CT staging)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2009
records.body: Clinical stage I-IIIA NSCLC considered resectable Conventional staging vs conventional + PET-CT Correct upstaging / disease stage PET-CT more often correctly upstaged disease and identified patients who would not benefit from surgery, refining selection for thoracotomy.

records.title: Schoenmaekers et al. (brain MRI vs CE-CT)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2019
records.body: Stage III NSCLC staged by FDG-PET/CE-CT, neurologically asymptomatic Dedicated contrast-enhanced brain CT vs additional brain MRI Occult brain metastases on MRI missed by CE-CT Brain MRI detected occult brain metastases not seen on dedicated CE-CT in a meaningful proportion of asymptomatic stage III patients, supporting brain MRI over CT for staging of locally advanced NSCLC.

records.title: Streamline L trial (Taylor et al.)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2019
records.body: Histologically proven or clinically diagnosed NSCLC on chest CT, referred for staging and potentially radically treatable (TNM7 stage <=IIIB, T1-4 N0-2 M0). Non-NSCLC histology was excluded; clinically diagnosed NSCLC remained eligible. Excluded MRI contraindication, pregnancy, severe systemic disease, or inappropriate further workup Whole-body MRI staging pathway (diffusion, T2, and pre/post-gadolinium T1 sequences) plus additional tests generated by multidisciplinary review vs Contemporaneous standard NHS staging investigations selected in usual care, interpreted without WB-MRI findings Primary: Sensitivity for metastatic disease. Secondary: Specificity; treatment-decision agreement; staging time; test number and cost; per-organ accuracy; T-stage and N-stage agreement Whole-body MRI did not improve per-patient sensitivity for metastatic disease versus standard staging: 50% vs 54%, difference -4 points (95% CI -15 to 7; P=.73); specificity was 93% vs 95%. It shortened median staging time from 19 to 13 days and reduced mean cost from £620 to £317, but N-stage agreement was lower (65% vs 75%). No imaging-pathway adverse events were reported.

records.title: IALT (International Adjuvant Lung Cancer Trial)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2004
records.body: Pathologically documented AJCC 1986 stage I-III NSCLC after complete resection; age 18-75 years; each centre prospectively selected eligible stages. Excluded previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy, chemotherapy contraindication, or prior cancer other than nonmelanoma skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ 3-4 cycles of centre-selected cisplatin plus vindesine, vinblastine, vinorelbine, or etoposide; optional conventional PORT <=60 Gy by centre policy after chemotherapy vs Observation; optional conventional PORT <=60 Gy by centre policy Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival; second primary cancers; adverse effects Adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy improved 5-year OS (44.5% vs 40.4%), but the benefit attenuated with longer follow-up: whole-period OS HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.81-1.02; P=.10). OS favoured chemotherapy during years 0-5 (HR 0.86) and reversed beyond 5 years (HR 1.45, 1.02-2.07; interaction P=.006). Whole-period DFS improved (HR 0.88). Non-lung-cancer mortality was higher beyond 5 years (HR 2.46, 1.15-5.28).

records.title: JBR.10 (NCIC CTG)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2005
records.body: Completely resected pathological stage IB (T2N0) or II (T1-2N1) NSCLC after lobectomy or pneumonectomy with specified nodal sampling. Excluded incomplete staging/resection, station 10 or central mediastinal nodal disease, mixed histology, T3 tumours, diffuse/multifocal bronchioloalveolar carcinoma, or recent other cancer Cisplatin 50 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8 every 4 weeks for 4 cycles plus vinorelbine 25 mg/m2 weekly for 16 weeks (initially 30 mg/m2 before August 1995 amendment) vs Observation Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Relapse-free survival; Safety; Quality of life Adjuvant cisplatin-vinorelbine improved OS versus observation: 5-year OS 69% vs 54%, median 94 vs 73 months, HR 0.69. Grade 3-4 neutropenia occurred in 73%, febrile neutropenia in 7%, and 2 treatment-related deaths (0.8%) occurred.

records.title: ANITA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2006
records.body: Histologically proven primary NSCLC other than bronchoalveolar carcinoma; pathological stage I (T2N0 only), II, or IIIA by 1986 TNM; age 18-75 years; complete R0 resection. Excluded concurrent malignancy except adequately treated nonmelanoma skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ, and other previous primary tumours Vinorelbine 30 mg/m² days 1,8,15,22 every 4 weeks up to 16 doses plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² days 1,29,57,85; optional postoperative RT by center policy vs Observation; optional postoperative RT by center policy Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Disease-free survival; Safety Adjuvant cisplatin-vinorelbine improved OS versus observation: median 65.7 vs 43.7 months, HR 0.80, with an 8.6-point absolute 5-year benefit; DFS also improved (HR 0.76). Among 368 treated patients, grade 3-4 neutropenia occurred in 85%, febrile neutropenia in 9%, and 7 treatment-related deaths occurred.

records.title: CALGB 9633
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2008
records.body: Completely resected pathological T2N0 stage IB NSCLC after lobectomy or pneumonectomy; no planned adjuvant radiotherapy Paclitaxel 200 mg/m2 IV over 3 hours plus carboplatin AUC 6 IV over 45-60 minutes every 3 weeks for 4 cycles vs Observation Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Disease-free survival; Treatment delivery and toxicity Adjuvant paclitaxel-carboplatin did not improve OS in resected stage IB disease: median 95 vs 78 months, HR 0.83 (90% CI 0.64-1.08); DFS also did not improve. An unplanned tumour >=4 cm subgroup suggested benefit (OS HR 0.69) but is hypothesis-generating. Grade 3 and grade 4 maximum toxicity occurred in 41% and 28%; there were no treatment deaths.

records.title: LACE (Lung Adjuvant Cisplatin Evaluation) meta-analysis
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · N/A · 2008
records.body: Individual-patient-data meta-analysis of five trials since 1995 with >300 patients randomised after complete NSCLC resection to postoperative cisplatin-based chemotherapy vs no chemotherapy. Excluded incomplete resection, neoadjuvant or non-cisplatin chemotherapy, preoperative chemotherapy, and concurrent chemoradiotherapy Cisplatin-based postoperative chemotherapy as assigned in ALPI, BLT, IALT, JBR.10, or ANITA vs No adjuvant chemotherapy control as assigned in the constituent trial Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Disease-free survival; Lung-cancer mortality; Non-lung-cancer mortality; Treatment delivery and toxicity Postoperative cisplatin-based chemotherapy improved OS versus no chemotherapy across 5 trials (HR 0.89), an absolute 5.4-point benefit at 5 years; DFS also improved (HR 0.84). Non-lung-cancer mortality increased (HR 1.36), concentrated in the first 6 months (HR 2.41); 19 chemotherapy deaths (0.9%) occurred, 18 within 6 months.

records.title: NSCLC Meta-analysis Collaborative Group (preoperative chemo)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · N/A · 2014
records.body: Resectable NSCLC across 15 randomised trials Neoadjuvant (preoperative) chemotherapy + surgery vs surgery alone Overall survival Neoadjuvant chemotherapy improved OS (HR 0.87; 5-yr absolute benefit ~5%, 40% to 45%), comparable to adjuvant chemotherapy; established preoperative chemotherapy as a valid alternative strategy.

records.title: ADAURA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2020
records.body: Completely resected nonsquamous AJCC 7th-edition stage IB-IIIA NSCLC with centrally confirmed EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R. Adjuvant chemotherapy was allowed but not mandatory; preoperative, postoperative, or planned radiotherapy was prohibited Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily for 3 years or until recurrence/discontinuation, after optional adjuvant chemotherapy vs Matched placebo orally once daily for 3 years or until recurrence/discontinuation, after optional adjuvant chemotherapy Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; health-related quality of life; safety; site of recurrence; CNS disease-free survival Adjuvant osimertinib improved final 5-year OS after resection of EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R NSCLC: 85% vs 73% in stage II-IIIA and 88% vs 78% in stage IB-IIIA (HR 0.49 for both). Earlier stage II-IIIA 24-month DFS was 90% vs 44% (HR 0.17). Grade >=3 AEs were 20% vs 13%; interstitial lung disease occurred in 3% vs 0 and was mild/moderate.

records.title: ALINA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Completely resected AJCC 7th-edition stage IB (tumour >=4 cm)-IIIA ALK-positive NSCLC; eligible for platinum chemotherapy; no previous systemic anticancer therapy Alectinib 600 mg orally twice daily for 24 months or until recurrence/toxicity/withdrawal vs Four 21-day cycles of IV platinum doublet: cisplatin 75 mg/m2 day 1 (carboplatin AUC 5-6 if intolerant) plus vinorelbine 25 mg/m2 days 1,8, gemcitabine 1250 mg/m2 days 1,8, or pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 day 1 Primary: Disease-free survival. records.body: Untreated advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² and cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then osimertinib + pemetrexed maintenance until progression/toxicity vs osimertinib 80 mg once daily until progression/toxicity Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, BICR PFS, ORR, duration of response, disease control, CNS outcomes, safety Osimertinib-chemotherapy improved final OS vs osimertinib alone (47.5 vs 37.6 months; HR 0.77) after improving PFS (25.5 vs 16.7 months; HR 0.62). At final OS follow-up, grade >=3 AEs were 70% vs 34%, serious AEs 46% vs 27%, fatal AEs 8% vs 4%, and any-treatment discontinuation 54% vs 7%.

records.title: MARIPOSA
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated advanced EGFR-mutant (ex19del/L858R) NSCLC First-line amivantamab (1050 mg IV, 1400 mg if ≥80 kg; weekly ×4 then Q2W) + lazertinib 240 mg once daily vs osimertinib 80 mg once daily; to progression Primary: BICR progression-free survival for amivantamab-lazertinib vs osimertinib. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, symptomatic progression, subsequent-treatment outcomes, intracranial efficacy, safety Amivantamab-lazertinib improved OS vs osimertinib (HR 0.75; 3-year OS 60% vs 51%) after improving PFS (23.7 vs 16.6 months; HR 0.70). Grade >=3 AEs were 80% vs 52%; venous thromboembolism 40% vs 11%, and fatal AEs 9% vs 8%.

records.title: AURA3
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2017
records.body: Advanced EGFR T790M-positive NSCLC after progression on prior EGFR TKI Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles, then optional pemetrexed maintenance until progression/toxicity Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary: ORR, duration of response, disease control, tumour shrinkage, OS, patient-reported outcomes, safety Osimertinib improved PFS vs platinum-pemetrexed after T790M-positive progression (10.1 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.30), including baseline CNS metastases (8.5 vs 4.2 months; HR 0.32); ORR was 71% vs 31%. Grade >=3 AEs were 23% vs 47%; ILD-like events were 4% vs 1%, including one osimertinib-arm death.

OS was immature (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.42-1.09). Grade >=3 AEs were 75% vs 54%; fatal AEs 5% vs 3%, including one considered amivantamab related.

records.title: Sampath (osimertinib + consolidative RT)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · II · 2025
records.body: Advanced EGFR exon 19/21-mutant NSCLC, treatment-naive to EGFR or checkpoint inhibitors Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily; after 8-10 weeks, responders/stable disease received radiotherapy to residual disease at up to 6 sites, then continued osimertinib until progression/toxicity (single-arm) Primary: investigator-assessed PFS from osimertinib initiation. Secondary: OS, response, duration of osimertinib, radiotherapy delivery, progression patterns, safety including pneumonitis Response-adapted consolidative radiotherapy with osimertinib produced median PFS 32.3 months and OS 45.0 months; 76% received radiotherapy. The uncontrolled design precludes comparison with osimertinib alone. Pneumonitis occurred in 2/42 (5%), including one grade 4 event; no other grade >=3 radiation-related or late radiation events were reported.

records.title: ACHILLES/TORG1834
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2025
records.body: Treatment-naive nonsquamous NSCLC with sensitizing uncommon EGFR mutations (excluding exon 20 insertions and T790M) Afatinib 30 or 40 mg orally once daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 6 every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression/toxicity Primary: investigator-assessed PFS from randomisation. Secondary: ORR, disease control, time to treatment failure, OS, duration of response, safety PFS improved with afatinib vs platinum-pemetrexed (10.6 vs 5.7 months; HR 0.421; P=.0010). Mutation-specific ORRs (major uncommon 55.8%, compound 72.7%, other 60.0%) were exploratory without an interaction test. OS was immature (29 deaths). Grade >=3 AEs were 44% vs 37%; one afatinib-related death occurred.

records.title: Robichaux et al. (structure-based EGFR classification)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · N/A · 2021
records.body: EGFR-mutant NSCLC (all mutation subtypes, exons 18-21) N/A — retrospective structure-function analysis of drug sensitivity across EGFR-TKIs Structural EGFR classification, mutation prevalence, drug-response associations, time to treatment failure, duration of treatment, objective response, preclinical sensitivity Retrospective structure-function grouping classified EGFR mutations as classical-like, T790M-like, exon20ins-loop or PACC and predicted TKI sensitivity better than exon grouping. In PACC mutations, time to treatment failure was 21.7 months with second-generation vs 10.0 with first-generation and 4.1 with third-generation TKIs (second vs third HR 0.23). This retrospective/preclinical analysis did not assess comparative treatment safety.

records.title: LUX-Lung 2/3/6 pooled (Yang)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · N/A · 2015
records.body: EGFR mutation-positive advanced (stage IIIb-IV) NSCLC adenocarcinoma, TKI-naive, with uncommon EGFR mutations (75 of 600 afatinib-treated patients across LUX-Lung 2/3/6) Afatinib 40 or 50 mg orally once daily in LUX-Lung 2 and 40 mg once daily in LUX-Lung 3/6, until progression/toxicity/withdrawal (pooled treated cohort) Objective response rate, PFS and OS by uncommon EGFR mutation group Post-hoc pooled analysis of afatinib-treated uncommon EGFR mutations: point mutations/duplications (n=38) had ORR 71.1%, PFS 10.7 months and OS 19.4 months; de-novo T790M (n=14) and exon 20 insertions (n=23) had ORR 14.3%/8.7%, PFS 2.9/2.7 months and OS 14.9/9.2 months. No formal comparisons or interaction test were performed; this publication did not provide a comparative safety analysis.

records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · II · 2020
records.body: Metastatic/recurrent NSCLC with uncommon EGFR mutations; exon 19 deletion, L858R, T790M and exon 20 insertion excluded Osimertinib 80 mg once daily (single-arm); to progression Primary: investigator-assessed objective response rate. Secondary: PFS, OS, duration of response, disease control, CNS response, safety Single-arm osimertinib produced ORR 50% and median PFS 8.2 months in uncommon EGFR-mutant NSCLC; exploratory ORRs were 78% for L861Q, 53% for G719X and 38% for S768I. OS was immature (7/36 deaths). Grade 3/4 AEs occurred in 2/36 (6%); no ILD, QT prolongation, AE discontinuation or treatment-related death was reported.

records.title: CHRYSALIS-2 Cohort C (Tomasini)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · I · 2026

Secondary: duration of response, clinical benefit rate, PFS, OS, time to treatment discontinuation, safety Single-arm amivantamab-lazertinib produced ORR 52%, median response duration 14.1 months and PFS 11.1 months; OS was not estimable. Grade >=3 AEs occurred in 70%, venous thromboembolism in 30% (grade 3, 10%), and treatment-related death in 1%.

records.title: Marcoux et al. (EGFR-mutant SCLC transformation)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · N/A · 2019
records.body: Retrospective 8-centre cohort of 67 patients with EGFR-mutant SCLC or high-grade neuroendocrine lung cancer treated in 2006-2018: 58 had initial NSCLC, predominantly adenocarcinoma, followed by transformation after EGFR-TKI exposure; 9 had de novo SCLC or mixed histology N/A — retrospective multicentre cohort; treatment was clinician-selected before and after transformation or, for de novo/mixed cases, after SCLC diagnosis; platinum-etoposide was the most common post-SCLC regimen Clinical response to systemic therapy after SCLC transformation or de novo SCLC diagnosis, Progression-free survival, Overall survival, CNS progression, Histologic and molecular characteristics At progression, repeat tissue biopsy is important if SCLC transformation is suspected. Retrospective cohort: 58 EGFR-mutant NSCLC cases transformed to SCLC/high-grade neuroendocrine disease; 9 were de novo/mixed (N=67). During pooled post-SCLC treatment, platinum-etoposide response was 54% (46 evaluable); transformed-case PFS was 3.4 months (48 at risk). Taxane response was 50% (20 evaluable); transformed-case PFS was 2.7 months (17 at risk). Checkpoint response was 0/17; cohorts were uncontrolled/non-comparative. Of 59 with follow-up radiographic information after SCLC diagnosis, 38 (64%) developed CNS progression. Pooled median OS from SCLC transformation/diagnosis was 10.9 months (95% CI 8.0-13.7). All 59 patients genotyped at first SCLC evidence retained founder EGFR; 15/19 previously T790M-positive cases lost T790M. Responses were investigator-estimated using general RECIST principles, without formal measurement/confirmation or standard intervals; no safety table was reported.

records.title: PROFILE 1014
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ALK-positive · III · 2014
records.body: Untreated advanced ALK-positive non-squamous NSCLC Crizotinib 250 mg orally twice daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5-6 IV every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles Primary: independent-review progression-free survival. Secondary: ORR, duration of response, OS, patient-reported outcomes, safety Crizotinib improved independent-review PFS vs platinum-pemetrexed (10.9 vs 7.0 months; HR 0.45) and ORR (74% vs 45%). OS was immature and inconclusive (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.54-1.26) with 70% crossover. Grade 3/4 aminotransferase elevation occurred in 14% vs 2%; one fatal treatment-related pneumonitis occurred after crossover to crizotinib.

Grade 3 treatment-related hypophosphataemia and neutropenia each occurred in 10%, ALT elevation in 4%, and no treatment-related grade 4/5 events occurred. records.title: Entrectinib (integrated ALKA/STARTRK)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ROS1-positive · I/II · 2020
records.body: Adults with locally advanced/metastatic ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC, ROS1-inhibitor naive, RECIST 1.1 measurable disease, ECOG 0-2, treated with at least one 600 mg entrectinib dose and followed at least 12 months; prior non-ROS1 therapy and asymptomatic or controlled brain metastases were allowed (single-arm pooled efficacy n=53) Entrectinib at least 600 mg orally once daily in 4-week cycles, continued until radiographic progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal (single-arm pooled efficacy analysis). ALKA-372-001 and STARTRK-1 included other dose levels/schedules, but efficacy eligibility required at least one 600 mg dose; STARTRK-2 used 600 mg once daily. Dose reductions for toxicity were in 200 mg decrements, maximum two. Primary: BICR objective response rate and duration of response. Secondary: BICR PFS, OS, safety; prespecified CNS endpoints: intracranial response, intracranial duration of response, intracranial PFS, time to CNS progression In this descriptive single-arm pooled efficacy population (n=53), BICR ORR was 77% (41/53; 95% CI 64–88), median DOR among 41 responders 24.6 months (95% CI 11.4–34.8) and median PFS 19.0 months (95% CI 12.2–36.6; 25 events). In the BICR baseline-CNS subgroup, intracranial ORR was 55% (11/20; 95% CI 32–77); radiotherapy-timing subgroups were small, descriptive and had no interaction test. In the safety set (n=134), 34% had grade 3–4 treatment-related AEs, 11% serious treatment-related AEs, 5% discontinued for treatment-related AEs, and all 9 deaths were deemed unrelated to treatment.

ORR was 59% with G2032R and intracranial ORR 89%/38% in the two cohorts. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 122/426; fatal AEs in 19/426, with none treatment related.

records.title: LIBRETTO-431

records.title: KEYNOTE-024
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2016
records.body: Untreated advanced NSCLC, PD-L1 >=50%, no EGFR/ALK First-line pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles / 2 years) vs platinum-doublet chemotherapy (4–6 cycles) Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, PFS2, safety At 5 years, pembrolizumab improved OS vs platinum chemotherapy in untreated PD-L1 TPS >=50% NSCLC (26.3 vs 13.4 months; HR 0.62; 5-year OS 31.9% vs 16.3%); updated PFS HR was 0.50. Treatment-related grade 3-5 AEs were 31.2% vs 53.3% and related deaths 1.3% vs 2.0%.

records.title: KEYNOTE-042
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated advanced NSCLC, PD-L1 >=1%, no EGFR/ALK First-line pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) vs platinum-doublet chemotherapy (4–6 cycles) Primary: OS in PD-L1 TPS >=50%, >=20% and >=1% populations. records.title: Di Federico high-PD-L1 meta-analysis
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · N/A · 2026
records.body: Treatment-naive advanced/metastatic NSCLC with high PD-L1 (24 phase 3 RCTs; TPS >=50%, except IMpower TC >=50% or IC >=10%) PD-(L)1 inhibitor + platinum-based chemotherapy vs PD-(L)1 inhibitor monotherapy (indirect comparison; no head-to-head RCT) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: PFS, treatment-related toxicity and discontinuation Indirect and reconstructed-IPD comparisons favoured chemoimmunotherapy over checkpoint monotherapy in high-PD-L1 disease: OS HR 0.85 by meta-regression and 0.74 in reconstructed IPD; PFS HR 0.61 and 0.67. records.title: SACHI
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2026
records.body: EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified locally advanced/metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC after first-line EGFR-TKI failure Savolitinib 600 mg (>=50 kg) or 400 mg (<50 kg) + osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 IV every 21 days for 4-6 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression Primary: investigator-assessed PFS hierarchically in third-generation EGFR-TKI-naive then ITT populations. Secondary: IRC PFS, ORR, disease control, duration of response, OS, safety Savolitinib-osimertinib improved PFS vs chemotherapy in the third-generation-TKI-naive population (9.8 vs 5.4 months; HR 0.34) and ITT population (8.2 vs 4.5 months; HR 0.34). OS was immature and inconclusive (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.55-1.29). Grade >=3 AEs were 57% in both arms; treatment-related deaths 2% vs 0%.

records.title: HERTHENA-Lung02
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Advanced EGFR-mutant (Ex19del or L858R) NSCLC after progression on a 3rd-generation EGFR TKI Patritumab deruxtecan (HER3-DXd) vs platinum-based chemotherapy; dose, component drugs, schedules and treatment duration were not stated in the filed conference abstract Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, intracranial PFS, safety Conference-abstract evidence: patritumab deruxtecan improved BICR PFS vs platinum chemotherapy (5.8 vs 5.4 months; HR 0.77) and ORR was 35.2% vs 25.3%; OS was immature. Grade >=3 AEs were 73% vs 57%; adjudicated ILD occurred in 5%, including two grade 5 cases. Full publication remains unfiled.

records.title: OptiTROP-Lung04
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2026
records.body: EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC after EGFR-TKI progression Sacituzumab tirumotecan 5 mg/kg IV days 1 and 15 every 28 days until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV every 21 days for up to 4 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, investigator-assessed PFS, ORR, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety Sacituzumab tirumotecan improved PFS vs platinum-pemetrexed (8.3 vs 4.3 months; HR 0.49) and interim OS (median not reached vs 17.4 months; HR 0.60; 18-month OS 65.8% vs 48.0%). Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs were 58.0% vs 53.8%; no drug-related ILD was reported.

records.title: ATTLAS (KCSG-LU19-04)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Stage IV EGFR-mutated or ALK-translocated NSCLC after relevant TKI progression Atezolizumab 1200 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5/5.5 IV every 21 days for 4 or 6 cycles, then atezolizumab-bevacizumab maintenance until progression vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 70 mg/m² for 4 or 6 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, landmark PFS and OS, safety Atezolizumab-bevacizumab-carboplatin-paclitaxel improved PFS vs pemetrexed-platinum (8.48 vs 5.62 months; HR 0.62; P=.004); ORR was 69.5% vs 41.9%. OS was negative (20.63 vs 20.27 months; HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.69-1.46). PD-L1 subgroup estimates were exploratory without an interaction test. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs were 35.1% vs 14.9%; related deaths 3/151 vs 0/74.

records.title: CURB
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · II · 2024
records.body: Adults with histologically confirmed metastatic NSCLC or breast cancer after at least one systemic-therapy line, with extracranial oligoprogression in up to five RECIST/PERCIST lesions all safely amenable to SBRT; prior brain metastases/radiotherapy were allowed, but same-site re-irradiation was not. Standard-of-care systemic therapy per physician discretion (no protocol SBRT) vs SBRT to all oligoprogressive sites plus standard-of-care systemic therapy per physician discretion; SBRT dose/fractionation selected by the treating radiation oncologist, usually 27-30 Gy in 3 fractions or 30-50 Gy in 5 fractions, with other schemes used infrequently for organ-at-risk constraints Primary: PFS to 12 months from randomisation to systemic disease progression. Secondary: OS, time to new systemic therapy and PFS by disease site, SBRT toxicity, quality of life, paired-blood biomarkers At the planned interim analysis, SBRT improved the alpha-protected pooled primary PFS endpoint vs standard of care (7.2 vs 3.2 months; HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.81; P=.0035, crossing the P<.006 boundary). In the prespecified NSCLC subgroup, median PFS was 10.0 vs 2.2 months (nominal HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.22-0.75; P=.0039); 86% had no actionable driver alteration. The breast-cancer subgroup was negative (4.4 vs 4.2 months; HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.43-1.43), with no treatment-by-disease interaction reported. Pooled OS was inconclusive (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.55-1.81); grade >=2 adverse events occurred in 62% vs 41%, including SBRT-attributed grade >=2 toxicity in 16%.

records.title: Pignon Meta-Analysis
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — chemoradiation · N/A · 1992
records.body: Individual-patient data from 13 randomised trials of chemotherapy plus or minus thoracic RT in limited-stage SCLC; extensive-disease patients were excluded; trial eligibility, chemotherapy, RT timing/dose/fractionation and PCI varied Trial-defined chemotherapy + thoracic RT (32–50 Gy in 8–25 fractions; start day 1–224; concurrent/alternating or sequential; some PCI) vs the same chemotherapy without thoracic RT Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: 3-year survival, sensitivity analyses, indirect RT timing/sequence comparisons, exploratory modifiers Adding thoracic RT reduced mortality (RR 0.86; p=.001) and improved 3-year OS 14.3% vs 8.9% (+5.4 points). Indirect comparisons did not show a clear early-vs-late or sequential-vs-nonsequential advantage. Nonfatal toxicity could not be pooled reliably

records.title: INT-0096 (Turrisi)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — chemoradiation · III · 1999
records.body: Previously untreated, histologically/cytologically confirmed LS-SCLC confined to one hemithorax and ipsilateral supraclavicular fossa, without pleural effusion or contralateral hilar/supraclavicular adenopathy; ECOG 0–2 with adequate marrow, renal, hepatic, pulmonary and cardiac function Thoracic RT from chemotherapy cycle 1: 45 Gy/30 BID fractions (1.5 Gy) over 3 weeks vs 45 Gy/25 QD fractions (1.8 Gy) over 5 weeks; both with cisplatin 60 mg/m² day 1 + etoposide 120 mg/m² days 1–3 Q21D ×4; complete responders offered PCI 25 Gy/10. No haematopoietic growth factors or cycle 1–2 dose adjustment; in cycles 3–4 reduce etoposide for grade-4 toxicity, febrile neutropenia/infection or bleeding thrombocytopenia, and cisplatin for creatinine 1.6–2.5 mg/dL with further reduction at ≥2.6 mg/dL. Interrupt RT only for platelets <50,000/mm³, weight loss ≥4.5 kg or admission for neutropenic fever/sepsis; not for dysphagia or fever with leukopenia alone. Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Treatment failure/local failure, response and toxicity; no prespecified secondary alpha hierarchy or multiplicity adjustment. Twice-daily RT improved primary OS versus once-daily: median 23 vs 19 months; HR for death with once-daily vs twice-daily 1.2 (95% CI 1.0–1.6), p=.04; 5-year OS 26% vs 16%. This benefit came with more grade-3 oesophagitis (27% vs 11%; the nominal p<.001 applied to the overall ordinal/incidence comparison, not grade 3 alone). There were 11 treatment-related deaths (6 vs 5).

records.title: CONVERT
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — chemoradiation · III · 2017
records.body: Adults with cytologically/histologically confirmed LS-SCLC encompassable in a radical RT portal, ECOG 0–1 or disease-related ECOG 2; no malignant pleural/pericardial effusion; acceptable RT volume, FEV1 >1 L or 40% predicted and DLCO >40%; no more than one adverse factor (ALP >1.5×ULN, sodium <LLN, LDH >ULN) Thoracic RT from day 22/cycle 2: 45 Gy/30 BID 1.5-Gy fractions ≥6 h apart over 19 days vs 66 Gy/33 QD 2-Gy fractions over 45 days; both with cisplatin–etoposide Q3W for 4 or 6 cycles (etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–3 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 or 25 mg/m² IV days 1–3), mandatory 3D conformal RT without elective nodal irradiation, and PCI within 6 weeks of final chemotherapy for eligible non-progressors. Delay then full dose was preferred. For first grade-4 febrile neutropenia, grade-4 thrombocytopenia requiring intervention or grade ≥2 bleeding with thrombocytopenia, full-dose chemotherapy with G-CSF or 20% reduction was allowed; second episode prompted 30% reduction, third removed the patient from trial. Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Treatment compliance, acute/late toxicity, local/metastatic progression-free survival; response was prespecified but not analysed. No secondary multiplicity adjustment or alpha hierarchy. Once-daily RT did not improve modified-ITT primary OS versus twice-daily: median 25 vs 30 months; HR for death 1.18 (95% CI 0.95–1.45), p=.14. This negative superiority result does not establish equivalence. Grade 3–4 oesophagitis was 47/246 vs 47/254 (19% in each arm; nominal p=.85). Grade 3–4 pneumonitis was 4/246 vs 4/254 (nominal p=.70); grade 3–5 counts were 6 vs 5, including 2 vs 1 deaths, with no separate p value. The headline reported 11 treatment-related deaths (8 vs 3), but detailed causes enumerate 12 instances; the discrepancy remains unresolved.

records.title: PCI Overview Collaborative Group (Aupérin)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI) · N/A · 1999
records.body: IPD from 7 randomised trials of histologically proven SCLC in complete remission after induction chemotherapy ± thoracic RT, with no brain metastases or prior cranial RT; trials included both limited- and extensive-stage disease PCI (n=526; trial-defined 8–40 Gy in 1–20 fractions, most commonly 24 Gy/8 fractions) vs no PCI (n=461); one cranial-irradiation course after complete response Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, brain and other metastases, local/regional recurrence PCI improved OS (RR death 0.84; p=.01) and 3-year OS 20.7% vs 15.3% (+5.4 points). Brain metastases were reduced (RR 0.46; p<.001; 3-year incidence 33.3% vs 58.6%). Only 140 patients had extensive-stage disease, limiting stage-specific certainty. Neurotoxicity evidence was limited and longer follow-up was needed

records.title: ADRIATIC
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — consolidation immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Adults with medically inoperable stage I–II or stage III LS-SCLC, WHO 0–1, no progression after definitive concurrent platinum–etoposide CRT, and no unresolved grade ≥2 CRT toxicity; prior PCI allowed After concurrent platinum–etoposide CRT ± PCI: durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W vs durvalumab 1500 mg + tremelimumab 75 mg IV Q4W ×4 then durvalumab Q4W vs placebo; continue to progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or 24 months Primary: Overall survival and progression-free survival for durvalumab. Secondary: Overall survival and progression-free survival for durvalumab+tremelimumab, objective response, response duration, survival landmarks, safety including pneumonitis Both primary endpoints were met with durvalumab vs placebo: interim median OS 55.9 vs 33.4 mo (HR 0.73; p=.01) and median PFS 16.6 vs 9.2 mo (HR 0.76; p=.02). The durvalumab+tremelimumab OS endpoint was not met and that arm remained blinded. Grade 3/4 all-cause AEs were 24.4% vs 24.2%, AE deaths 2.7% vs 1.9%, and pneumonitis/radiation pneumonitis 38.2% vs 30.2%, including one grade-5 event with durvalumab

records.title: ACHILES
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — consolidation immunotherapy · II · 2025
records.body: LS-SCLC, PS 0–2, without progression after concurrent platinum–etoposide plus BID thoracic RT, randomised 3–7 weeks after CRT; complete protocol eligibility is unavailable from this one-page conference abstract Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV Q3W for 1 year, starting 3–7 weeks after CRT, until progression/unacceptable toxicity vs observation; CRT responders in either arm were offered PCI 25–30 Gy, which could begin after atezolizumab started Primary: Overall survival from post-CRT randomisation. Secondary: Response rate, progression-free survival and toxicity; no secondary multiplicity control or gatekeeping sequence was reported in the conference abstract. Consolidation atezolizumab did not improve primary OS versus observation: median 43.3 vs 38.8 months; HR for death 1.14 (95% CI 0.76–1.72), alpha-protected p=.5. Secondary PFS was 21.1 vs 15.9 months (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.60–1.28; nominal p=.5). Post-randomisation grade 3–4 toxicity was 34% vs 20%, with unspecified denominators; treatment-related deaths were 3 vs 0. Evidence is limited to a one-page conference abstract without formal analysis-set definitions or complete safety detail.

records.title: JCOG9511 (Noda)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemotherapy · III · 2002
records.body: Japanese patients age ≤70 with untreated ES-SCLC and ECOG 0–2; symptomatic brain metastases requiring WBRT or steroids were excluded Irinotecan 60 mg/m² IV days 1, 8, 15 + cisplatin 60 mg/m² day 1 Q4W ×4 vs etoposide 100 mg/m² days 1–3 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² day 1 Q3W ×4 Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Complete response rate, overall response rate, progression-free survival, relapse sites, toxicity Irinotecan–cisplatin improved final median OS to 12.8 vs 9.4 mo (RR death 0.60; p=.002) and 2-year OS to 19.5% vs 5.2%. Secondary PFS was 6.9 vs 4.8 mo (p=.003) and ORR 84.4% vs 67.5% (p=.02); PFS monitoring could be biased. In safety sets of 75 vs 77, grade 3/4 neutropenia was 65.3% vs 92.2%, thrombocytopenia 5.3% vs 18.2%, and diarrhoea 16.0% vs 0%; treatment-related deaths were 3 vs 1

records.title: SECSG CAV/EP (Roth)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemotherapy · III · 1992
records.body: ≥18; SCLC histology/cytology; no prior chemo/RT; beyond primary/mediastinum/ipsilateral SC nodes; bidimensionally measurable; Zubrod 0–3. Pleural effusion alone excluded; effusions/positive bone/liver scans not indicator lesions. Brain mets required concurrent WBRT. Excluded cancer except treated NMSC/cervical CIS; CHF, treated arrhythmia or MI <3 mo. WBC/platelets >4000/100,000 per µL (>3000/50,000 with marrow involvement); bilirubin <2 mg/dL; creatinine <1.8 men/<1.5 women mg/dL; consent. EP: cisplatin 20 mg/m²/day + etoposide 80 mg/m²/day IV days 1–5 Q3W ×4; CAV: cyclophosphamide 1000 mg/m² + doxorubicin 40 mg/m² + vincristine 1 mg/m² (max 2 mg) IV day 1 Q3W ×6; alternating CAV/EP: CAV day 1 then EP days 22–26, repeating the 6-week sequence ×3. Brain metastases received concomitant WBRT. Cisplatin hydration targeted urine output ≥100 mL/h before and for 4 h after dosing, with optional mannitol/loop diuretic. Delay 1 week for day-1 leukocytes <4000/µL or platelets <100,000/µL. After fever/infection with nadir granulocytes <500/µL or significant bleeding with nadir platelets <50,000/µL, reduce etoposide (EP), cyclophosphamide+doxorubicin (CAV), or all three (alternating) 25%; do not reduce cisplatin/vincristine for haematologic toxicity. If creatinine exceeded 150% of baseline, omit cisplatin for one course, resume only at baseline and cross to CAV if persistent. At progression, EP crossed to CAV up to 6 cycles, CAV to EP up to 4; alternating-arm salvage was investigator-selected Primary: Overall survival from registration. Secondary: Objective/complete response, time to best response, time to progression, crossover response and toxicity. Pairwise three-group comparisons used Bonferroni alpha .017; no sequential gatekeeping hierarchy linked endpoints. In 437 eligible patients, EP, CAV and alternating CAV/EP showed no primary OS advantage: medians 8.6, 8.3 and 8.1 months (stratified p=.425); this was not an equivalence/noninferiority test. Response was 60.7%, 50.6% and 59.4% among 140, 140 and 138 assessable patients (nominal p=.175). In this 140+140+138 response-assessable population, alternating-vs-CAV TTP p=.008 met the paper's pairwise .017 threshold, but treatment was not retained in the final Cox model. Therapy-related deaths were 9/159, 6/156 and 11/162.

records.title: Japanese CAV/PE trial (Fukuoka)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemotherapy · N/A · 1991
records.body: Histologically/cytologically proven SCLC reviewed by ≥2 pathologists; no prior therapy; measurable/evaluable disease; ECOG 0–3; age <75.
