Secondary: overall survival, overall response rate, safety, quality of life, clinical benefit DCF improved TTP vs CF (5.6 vs 3.7 mo; HR 1.47, reported CF relative to DCF); median OS was 9.2 vs 8.6 mo (HR 1.29) and 2-year survival was 18% vs 9%. Severe treatment-related events were 69% vs 59%, neutropenia 82% vs 57% and complicated neutropenia 29% vs 12%; deaths within 30 days were 10% vs 8%.

records.title: REAL-2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2008
records.body: Previously untreated locally advanced inoperable or metastatic adenocarcinoma, squamous-cell carcinoma or undifferentiated carcinoma of the oesophagus, GEJ or stomach; prior radical surgery with tumour within 1 mm of the margin was eligible without measurable disease ECF vs ECX vs EOF vs EOX: epirubicin 50 mg/m2 d1 + cisplatin 60 mg/m2 or oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 d1 + continuous fluorouracil 200 mg/m2/d or capecitabine 625 mg/m2 twice daily; q3w for ≤8 cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, response rate, toxicity, quality of life Capecitabine and oxaliplatin were each noninferior to fluorouracil and cisplatin for OS; EOX had longer OS than ECF in an unadjusted secondary comparison (11.2 vs 9.9 mo; HR 0.80), while PFS did not differ by either substitution. Oxaliplatin reduced thromboembolism but increased neuropathy/diarrhoea; mortality within 60 days was 5.6–7.2% across arms.

records.title: GASTFOX (PRODIGE 51)
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2025
records.body: Previously untreated HER2-negative locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma; perioperative fluoropyrimidine ± platinum allowed only if relapse ≥12 mo later; excluded baseline grade ≥2 neuropathy, prior docetaxel and cerebral/meningeal metastases TFOX: docetaxel 50 mg/m2 + folinic acid 400 mg/m2 + oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2 → fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 continuous IV over 46 h vs FOLFOX: folinic acid 400 mg/m2 + oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2 + fluorouracil 400 mg/m2 IV bolus → 2400 mg/m2 continuous IV over 46 h; q2w until progression/toxicity/decision/withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, safety, quality of life, therapeutic index ratio TFOX improved final ITT PFS by 12-month RMST (7.52 vs 6.62 mo) after nonproportional hazards; median OS was 15.08 vs 12.65 mo (HR 0.82) vs FOLFOX. Severe diarrhoea, neuropathy, neutropenia and fatigue were more frequent; serious treatment-related events were 27% vs 13% and treatment-related deaths 2 vs 1.

records.title: GO2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic gastro-oesophageal cancer (oesophagus, GOJ or stomach; adenocarcinoma or squamous) judged by the treating oncologist unsuitable for full-dose combination chemotherapy on grounds of advanced age and/or frailty; no chronological age, performance-status or frailty threshold specified, but patients had to be judged fit for every arm of their randomisation CHEMO-INTENSITY: oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 d1 + capecitabine 625 mg/m2 twice daily d1–21 q3w at 100% vs 80% vs 60% dose; mean treatment duration 4.4 vs 4.6 vs 5.4 cycles. Separate CHEMO-BSC: 60% dose vs best supportive care Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: overall treatment utility, response rate, quality of life, fatigue, symptoms, quality-adjusted survival, safety In older/frail patients unsuitable for full-dose chemotherapy, both reduced oxaliplatin-capecitabine doses were noninferior to full dose for PFS; the lowest dose reduced severe non-haematological toxicity within 9 weeks (23% vs 38%) and improved unmodified 3-cycle delivery (58% vs 32%). No subgroup was shown to benefit from higher dose. The 45-patient chemotherapy-vs-supportive-care comparison was exploratory and did not reach statistical significance.

records.title: ToGA
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · III · 2010
records.body: First-line inoperable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma; HER2-positive by central gastric-specific IHC 3+ or FISH ratio ≥2; excluded prior metastatic chemotherapy, major cardiac disease, active GI bleeding and brain metastases Trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading → 6 mg/kg IV q3w until progression/toxicity/withdrawal + cisplatin/capecitabine or cisplatin/fluorouracil q3w for 6 cycles vs the same chemotherapy alone for 6 cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to progression, overall response rate, duration of response, safety Adding trastuzumab improved OS (13.8 vs 11.1 mo; HR 0.74), PFS and response. Grade 3–4 adverse events were 68% in both arms; diarrhoea was 9% vs 4%, treatment-related mortality 3% vs 1%, and LVEF dysfunction 5% vs 1%.

records.title: KEYNOTE-811
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · III · 2023
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (central IHC 3+ or IHC 2+/ISH+); enrolled regardless of PD-L1; excluded prior advanced-disease or checkpoint therapy, active CNS disease, active autoimmune disease and immunodeficiency Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading → 6 mg/kg q3w + CAPOX or FP vs placebo + trastuzumab + CAPOX or FP; ≤35 cycles (~2 y) or until progression/toxicity/decision/withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, safety, health-related quality of life Adding pembrolizumab improved PFS at interim analysis (10.0 vs 8.1 mo; HR 0.72); OS had not met its interim criterion (20.0 vs 16.8 mo; HR 0.84) and final follow-up was planned. Grade ≥3 treatment-related events were 58% vs 51%; treatment-related deaths were 1% in each arm.

records.title: DESTINY-Gastric01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · II · 2020
records.body: Centrally confirmed high-HER2 locally advanced or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma progressing after >=2 regimens including fluoropyrimidine, platinum and trastuzumab; active, suspected or prior glucocorticoid-treated ILD/pneumonitis excluded Trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg IV q3w until progression, consent withdrawal or unacceptable adverse events vs Physician choice irinotecan 150 mg/m2 IV q2w or paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 IV days 1,8,15 q4w until progression, consent withdrawal or unacceptable adverse events Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival, duration of response, disease control, safety T-DXd improved ORR (51% vs 14%); at interim OS analysis (101/133 planned deaths), OS was 12.5 vs 8.4 mo (HR 0.59) vs physician-choice chemotherapy. Severe neutrophil decrease was 51% vs 24%; adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis occurred in 10% (3 severe cases), with 1 drug-related pneumonia death.

records.title: DESTINY-Gastric04
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · III · 2025
records.body: HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma progressing during trastuzumab-based therapy, with HER2 confirmed on a post-progression tumour biopsy; excluded current, prior glucocorticoid-treated or suspected ILD/pneumonitis Trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg IV q3w vs ramucirumab 8 mg/kg d1,15 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 d1,8,15 q4w; until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or physician decision Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control, duration of response, safety At the prespecified interim analysis (266/339 planned deaths), T-DXd improved OS (14.7 vs 11.4 mo; HR 0.70), PFS (6.7 vs 5.6 mo; HR 0.74) and response (44% vs 29%) vs ramucirumab/paclitaxel. Severe drug-related events were 50% vs 54%; drug-related ILD/pneumonitis 13.9% vs 1.3% and fatal drug-related events 1.6% vs 0.9%.

records.title: HERIZON-GEA-01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · III · 2026
records.body: Previously untreated centrally HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+/ISH+) unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic gastric, GEJ or oesophageal adenocarcinoma; no prior systemic advanced-disease, HER2-targeted or checkpoint therapy; enrolled irrespective of PD-L1 Zanidatamab weight-based IV q3w + tislelizumab 200 mg q3w + CAPOX/FP vs zanidatamab + CAPOX/FP vs trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading → 6 mg/kg q3w + CAPOX/FP; chemotherapy could stop after 6 cycles; antibody duration not reported Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, safety Zanidatamab-tislelizumab-chemotherapy improved PFS (12.4 vs 8.1 mo) and interim OS (26.4 vs 19.2 mo) vs trastuzumab-chemotherapy. Zanidatamab-chemotherapy improved PFS, but interim OS had not met its criterion. Severe adverse events were 83%, 74% and 75%; severe diarrhoea 25%, 20% and 13%; drug-related deaths 2.4%, 0.3% and 1.3%.

records.title: CSCO HER2 Guideline (2025 Ed.)
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · N/A · 2026
records.body: China-focused patients with gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma across HER2 testing and targeted-therapy decisions; systemic recommendations primarily advanced/recurrent/metastatic disease, with separate locally advanced perioperative and advanced conversion scenarios; HER2-high=IHC3+ or IHC2+/FISH+, intermediate=IHC2+/FISH-, low=IHC1+, absent=IHC0 HER2 testing and treatment guideline (not comparative arms): first-line trastuzumab-based therapy by PD-L1 CPS; second-line T-DXd or trastuzumab/paclitaxel if trastuzumab-naive; later-line disitamab vedotin or T-DXd; maintenance, resistance, perioperative and conversion recommendations retain stated GRADE strength HER2 classification and testing, evidence quality and recommendation strength, line- and biomarker-specific HER2-targeted treatment, safety management CSCO classifies HER2 as high (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+/FISH+), intermediate (IHC 2+/FISH−), low (IHC 1+) or absent (IHC 0). Strong/high-quality recommendations support trastuzumab-chemotherapy for CPS <1 and pembrolizumab-trastuzumab-chemotherapy for CPS ≥1; second-line T-DXd is strong/high-quality. Later-line, maintenance, perioperative and conversion recommendations retain lower evidence or weak-strength boundaries; zanidatamab was not yet approved in China.

records.title: CheckMate 649
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · III · 2021
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable advanced or metastatic gastric, GEJ or oesophageal adenocarcinoma; known HER2-positive disease excluded but unknown status permitted; enrolled regardless of PD-L1; prior perioperative chemotherapy, radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy allowed if completed >=6 mo before randomisation Nivolumab 360 mg q3w + XELOX or 240 mg q2w + FOLFOX vs XELOX/FOLFOX alone; until progression/toxicity/withdrawal/study end, nivolumab ≤2 y Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, landmark survival, biomarker analyses, health-related quality of life, symptom deterioration, safety At interim OS and final PFS analyses, nivolumab-chemotherapy improved OS and PFS in CPS ≥5; OS also improved in all randomised patients (13.8 vs 11.6 mo; HR 0.80), while all-population PFS was not formally tested. Severe treatment-related events were 59% vs 44%, serious events 22% vs 12%, discontinuation of any component 36% vs 24%, and treatment-related deaths 2% vs 1%.

records.title: KEYNOTE-859
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · III · 2023
records.body: Previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, HER2-negative by local IHC 0/1+ or ISH ratio <2 with mean copy number <4; enrolled regardless of PD-L1 CPS; excluded immunodeficiency/chronic immunosuppression, treatment-requiring autoimmune disease and active CNS metastases Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w + CAPOX or FP vs placebo + CAPOX or FP; pembrolizumab/placebo ≤35 cycles, platinum could stop after 6 cycles; no crossover Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety At the protocol-specified interim analysis, pembrolizumab-chemotherapy improved OS (12.9 vs 11.5 mo; HR 0.78), PFS and response vs chemotherapy alone; effect estimates were larger at higher CPS, but subgroup patterns do not establish a treatment mandate. Severe treatment-related events were 59% vs 51%; treatment-related deaths 1% vs 2%; potentially immune-mediated events 27% vs 9%.

records.title: RATIONALE-305
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · III · 2024
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma; prior perioperative therapy allowed only if progression-free interval ≥6 mo; enrolled regardless of PD-L1; excluded active CNS disease, treatment-requiring autoimmune disease, systemic immunosuppression and prior checkpoint therapy Tislelizumab 200 mg IV q3w + CAPOX or FP vs placebo + CAPOX or FP; chemotherapy ≤6 cycles, then tislelizumab/placebo with optional capecitabine maintenance until progression/toxicity; conditional stop at 2 y Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety, quality of life Tislelizumab-chemotherapy improved OS in TAP ≥5% and at final ITT analysis (15.0 vs 12.9 mo; HR 0.80); the response-rate test in TAP ≥5% did not reach significance and stopped the hierarchy before ITT PFS/ORR. Severe treatment-related events were 54% vs 50%, serious events 23% vs 15%, discontinuation 16% vs 8%, and treatment-related deaths 6 vs 2.

records.title: SPOTLIGHT
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Claudin 18.2-positive disease · III · 2023
records.body: Previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, HER2-negative and CLDN18.2-positive by central VENTANA 43-14A IHC (>=75% tumour cells with moderate-to-strong membranous staining) Zolbetuximab 800 mg/m2 loading → 600 mg/m2 twice per 42-d cycle + mFOLFOX6 for 4 cycles vs placebo + mFOLFOX6; thereafter zolbetuximab/placebo + fluorouracil/folinate until progression/toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, quality of life, safety Zolbetuximab-mFOLFOX6 improved PFS (10.6 vs 8.7 mo; HR 0.75) and interim OS (18.2 vs 15.5 mo; HR 0.75). Grade ≥3 adverse events were 87% vs 78%; nausea 82% vs 61%, vomiting 67% vs 36%, and treatment-related deaths 2% vs 1%.

records.title: GLOW
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Claudin 18.2-positive disease · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, HER2-negative and CLDN18.2-positive by central VENTANA 43-14A IHC (>=75% tumour cells with moderate-to-strong membranous staining); prior perioperative systemic therapy permitted only if completed >=6 mo before randomisation Zolbetuximab 800 mg/m2 loading → 600 mg/m2 q3w + CAPOX for 8 cycles vs placebo + CAPOX; thereafter zolbetuximab/placebo with optional capecitabine until progression/toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, quality of life, safety Zolbetuximab-CAPOX improved PFS (8.2 vs 6.8 mo; HR 0.69) and interim OS (14.4 vs 12.2 mo; HR 0.77). Severe adverse events were 73% vs 70%; nausea 69% vs 50%, vomiting 66% vs 31%, and treatment-related deaths 2.4% vs 2.8%.

records.title: REGARD
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2014
records.body: Metastatic or unresectable locally recurrent gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma; progression during or within 4 mo of first-line metastatic platinum/fluoropyrimidine, or within 6 mo of comparable adjuvant therapy; excluded recent major GI bleeding, arterial thromboembolism and poorly controlled hypertension Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV q2w + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care; until progression, unacceptable toxicity or death; no crossover Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control, duration of response, quality of life, performance-status deterioration, safety Ramucirumab improved OS (5.2 vs 3.8 mo; HR 0.78) and PFS vs placebo, but objective response was 3% in both arms and 6-wk quality-of-life data were sparse. Grade ≥3 adverse events were 57% vs 58%; grade ≥3 hypertension 8% vs 3%; treatment-related deaths 2% in each arm.

records.title: RAINBOW
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2014
records.body: Metastatic or unresectable locally advanced gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma progressing during or within 4 mo of first-line platinum-fluoropyrimidine ± anthracycline; excluded squamous/undifferentiated histology and recent major GI perforation, fistula, bleeding or arterial thromboembolism Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV d1,15 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 IV d1,8,15 q4w vs placebo + paclitaxel; until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal; no crossover Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety Ramucirumab-paclitaxel improved OS (9.6 vs 7.4 mo; HR 0.81), PFS and response vs paclitaxel. Grade 3–4 neutropenia was 41% vs 19%, grade 3 hypertension 15% vs 3%, and study-drug-related fatal events 2% in each arm.

records.title: TAGS
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2018
records.body: Unresectable metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after >=2 advanced-disease regimens, with progression within 3 mo or last-line intolerance; prior fluoropyrimidine, platinum, and taxane or irinotecan required, plus anti-HER2 therapy if available for HER2-positive tumours Trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m2 orally twice daily d1–5,8–12 q4w + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care; until progression, intolerable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control, performance-status deterioration, health-related quality of life, safety Trifluridine/tipiracil improved OS (5.7 vs 3.6 mo; HR 0.69) and PFS in heavily pretreated disease. Grade ≥3 adverse events were 80% vs 58%, chiefly neutropenia 34% vs 0 and anaemia 19% vs 8%; treatment-related deaths were <1% vs 1%.

records.title: ATTRACTION-2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2017
records.body: Unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after ≥2 prior chemotherapy regimens, refractory to or intolerant of standard therapy; PD-L1 selection not required; excluded autoimmune disease, ILD, symptomatic brain metastases and prior checkpoint therapy Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV q2w vs placebo q2w; until progression or toxicity requiring discontinuation; protocol-permitted treatment beyond progression Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control, duration of response, safety Nivolumab improved OS (5.3 vs 4.1 mo; HR 0.63; 12-mo OS 26% vs 11%) in ≥third-line disease. Grade 3–4 treatment-related events were 10% vs 4%, serious events 10% vs 5%, and treatment-related deaths 2% vs 1%; ILD occurred in 2% with nivolumab.

records.title: KEYNOTE-590
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal & GEJ — first-line immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic oesophageal adenocarcinoma or squamous-cell carcinoma, or Siewert type 1 GEJ adenocarcinoma; known HER2-positive disease excluded; excluded active CNS disease, treatment-requiring autoimmune disease, immunodeficiency/chronic immunosuppression and noninfectious/current pneumonitis Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w + cisplatin 80 mg/m2 d1 + fluorouracil 800 mg/m2/d d1–5 q3w vs placebo + the same chemotherapy; cisplatin ≤6 cycles, pembrolizumab/placebo ± chemotherapy ≤35 cycles; no crossover Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, health-related quality of life, safety At the first interim OS and final PFS analysis, pembrolizumab-chemotherapy improved OS (12.4 vs 9.8 mo; HR 0.73), PFS and response; benefit estimates were largest in ESCC CPS ≥10, without a reported predictive interaction. Severe treatment-related events were 72% vs 68%, treatment-related deaths 2% vs 1%, and pneumonitis 6% vs 1%.

records.title: CheckMate 648
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal & GEJ — first-line immunotherapy · III · 2022
records.body: Unresectable advanced, recurrent or metastatic oesophageal squamous-cell or adenosquamous carcinoma not amenable to curative treatment; no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease; enrolled regardless of PD-L1 Nivolumab 240 mg IV q2w + cisplatin/fluorouracil vs nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6w vs cisplatin/fluorouracil; immunotherapy ≤2 y, treatment otherwise until progression/toxicity/withdrawal/trial end Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety At interim analysis, nivolumab-chemotherapy improved overall-population OS vs chemotherapy (13.2 vs 10.7 mo; HR 0.74), as did nivolumab-ipilimumab (12.7 vs 10.7 mo; HR 0.78). Nivolumab-chemotherapy overall-population PFS did not meet its criterion; nivolumab-ipilimumab PFS failed in PD-L1 ≥1%, stopping overall PFS testing. Severe treatment-related events were 47%, 32% and 36%; treatment-related deaths were 2% in each arm.

records.title: ESCORT-1st
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic ESCC not amenable to oesophagectomy or definitive chemoradiation; age ≤75; prior perioperative therapy or definitive chemoradiation allowed only if progression occurred ≥6 mo later; excluded active or historical autoimmune disease and CNS metastases Camrelizumab 200 mg IV q3w + paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 + cisplatin 75 mg/m2 d1 q3w vs placebo + the same chemotherapy; chemotherapy ≤6 cycles, camrelizumab/placebo until confirmed progression/toxicity/withdrawal/death/new therapy Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, disease control, duration of response, landmark overall survival, health-related quality of life, safety At the first interim OS and final PFS analysis, camrelizumab-chemotherapy improved OS (15.3 vs 12.0 mo; HR 0.70) and PFS (6.9 vs 5.6 mo; HR 0.56). Severe treatment-related events were 63% vs 68%; serious events 30% vs 23%; reactive capillary endothelial proliferation 80% vs 11%; treatment-related deaths 3.0% vs 3.7%.

records.title: ORIENT-15
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2022
records.body: Untreated unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic ESCC unsuitable for curative surgery or definitive chemoradiotherapy; prior perioperative chemotherapy or definitive chemoradiotherapy allowed only if progression occurred >6 mo later; excluded aortic/tracheal invasion, hepatic metastases occupying >50% of liver and active autoimmune disease or steroid-requiring ILD Sintilimab 3 mg/kg (<60 kg) or 200 mg (≥60 kg) IV q3w + cisplatin/paclitaxel or cisplatin/fluorouracil vs placebo + the same chemotherapy; chemotherapy ≤6 cycles, sintilimab/placebo ≤24 mo Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, progression-free survival, disease control, duration of response, health-related quality of life, safety At interim analysis (351/500 planned all-patient OS deaths), sintilimab-chemotherapy improved OS in all patients (16.7 vs 12.5 mo; HR 0.63) and CPS ≥10, plus PFS and response; no formal PD-L1 interaction supported subgroup selection. Severe treatment-related events were 60% vs 55%, serious events 28% vs 20%, discontinuation 21% vs 12%, and treatment-related deaths 3% vs 2%.

records.title: RATIONALE-306
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic ESCC not amenable to definitive surgery or radiotherapy; prior perioperative platinum allowed only after a ≥6-mo treatment-free interval; enrolled regardless of PD-L1; excluded CNS disease, untreatable obstruction/fistula, active autoimmune disease and prior checkpoint therapy Tislelizumab 200 mg IV q3w + investigator-choice platinum/fluoropyrimidine or platinum/paclitaxel vs placebo + the same chemotherapy; platinum could stop after 6 cycles, remaining therapy until progression/toxicity/withdrawal with conditional stop at 2 y; no crossover Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, health-related quality of life, safety At the primary interim analysis, which crossed its prespecified boundary and replaced the planned final analysis, tislelizumab-chemotherapy improved OS (17.2 vs 10.6 mo; HR 0.66), PFS and response; TAP subgroup findings did not establish predictive selection. Severe treatment-related events were 67% vs 64%, serious events 29% vs 19%, discontinuation 29% vs 19%, and investigator-attributed treatment-related deaths 6 vs 4 after excluding progression.

records.title: ATTRACTION-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous — second-line immunotherapy · III · 2019
records.body: Unresectable advanced or recurrent cervical/thoracic oesophageal or GEJ squamous/adenosquamous carcinoma, refractory or intolerant to one prior fluoropyrimidine-platinum regimen and not indicated for radical resection; enrolled irrespective of PD-L1; excluded major malnutrition, adjacent-organ invasion, ILD, autoimmune disease and CNS metastases Nivolumab 240 mg IV q2w vs investigator-choice paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 weekly 6 of 7 wk or docetaxel 75 mg/m2 q3w; until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with protocol-permitted treatment beyond progression Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, disease control, quality of life, safety Nivolumab improved OS (10.9 vs 8.4 mo; HR 0.77) vs taxane chemotherapy, but ORR did not favour nivolumab (19% vs 22%), stopping protected PFS testing; median PFS was 1.7 vs 3.4 mo. Severe treatment-related events were 18% vs 63%, with treatment-related deaths 2 vs 3.

records.title: DRAGON-01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Peritoneal metastasis — intraperitoneal (bidirectional) therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated gastric adenocarcinoma with laparoscopy-confirmed peritoneal metastasis; ovarian involvement alone allowed but other extraperitoneal distant metastasis excluded; age ≤75; all enrolled tumours ERBB2-negative (IHC 0/1+ or IHC 2+/FISH-negative); excluded obstruction and prior anticancer therapy Paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 IV + 20 mg/m2 intraperitoneally d1,8 + S-1 80 mg/m2/d d1–14 q3w vs paclitaxel 70 mg/m2 IV d1,8 + S-1 80 mg/m2/d d1–14 q3w; until progression/toxicity/withdrawal; no crossover Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, conversion-surgery rate, major pathological response, safety Intraperitoneal plus IV paclitaxel/S-1 improved OS (19.4 vs 13.9 mo; HR 0.67), PFS and conversion-surgery rate vs IV paclitaxel/S-1; pathology outcomes used operated post-randomisation subsets. Severe adverse events were 39% vs 42%; port complications occurred in 27% and required surgery in 11%; no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: RENAISSANCE (AIO-FLOT5)
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oligometastatic disease — role of surgery · III · 2024
records.body: Previously untreated patients with limited-metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal-junction adenocarcinoma, defined by retroperitoneal lymph-node metastases only or at most one potentially resectable or locally controllable incurable organ site, with or without retroperitoneal nodes, after four induction FLOT cycles Arm A: 4 induction FLOT cycles, with trastuzumab if HER2-positive or nivolumab if PD-L1-positive, then radical complete resection of primary and metastases followed by the same systemic treatment vs Arm B: after the same induction and no progression, additional FLOT; exact doses, antibody continuation after randomisation, and post-randomisation duration were not reported in the abstract Primary: overall survival. Secondary: quality of life, surgery, R0 resection, perioperative mortality, treatment delivery Adding radical surgery after induction FLOT did not meet the OS primary endpoint; early postoperative mortality offset later separation in crossing survival curves. Surgery occurred in 91%, with 30-day and 90-day mortality of 3% and 8%. The apparent retroperitoneal-node subgroup difference was exploratory and does not support subgroup selection.

records.title: TROG 03.01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal — palliative radiotherapy · III · 2018
records.body: Incurable advanced or metastatic oesophageal cancer with symptomatic dysphagia (Mellow 1–4), excluding Seifert type 2–3 lesions; no prior chemotherapy or chest radiotherapy; no tracheo-oesophageal fistula or stent in situ Palliative chemoradiotherapy: radiotherapy 35 Gy/15 fractions over 3 wk (Australia, NZ) or 30 Gy/10 fractions over 2 wk (Canada, UK) + cisplatin (80 mg/m2 d1 or 20 mg/m2/d d1-4) + fluorouracil 800 mg/m2/d continuous infusion d1-4 vs Radiotherapy alone: same radiotherapy dose schedule (35 Gy/15# or 30 Gy/10#) Primary: dysphagia relief. Secondary: dysphagia progression-free survival, overall survival, dysphagia response, complete dysphagia relief, secondary treatment, quality of life, acute toxicity, late toxicity Adding chemotherapy to palliative radiotherapy did not improve dysphagia relief (45% vs 35%; statistical significance not reached), dysphagia-PFS or OS, and increased severe acute toxicity (36% vs 16%). Radiotherapy alone provided similar palliation with less acute toxicity.

records.title: ESPAC-1
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2004
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma Adjuvant 5-FU/folinic acid vs chemoradiotherapy (2x2 factorial) vs observation Overall survival Adjuvant chemotherapy improved median OS (19.7 vs 14.0 months) with 5-year OS 21% vs 8% (HR 0.71), whereas chemoradiotherapy was deleterious (5-year OS 10% vs 20%); established adjuvant chemotherapy, not chemoradiation, as the standard.

records.title: ESPAC-3
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2010
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma Adjuvant gemcitabine vs 5-FU/folinic acid Overall survival Gemcitabine and 5-FU/folinic acid gave equivalent median OS (23.6 vs 23.0 months, HR 0.94) but gemcitabine caused fewer serious adverse events; established gemcitabine as the preferred, better-tolerated backbone.

records.title: CONKO-001
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2007
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (R0/R1) Adjuvant gemcitabine vs observation Disease-free survival Adjuvant gemcitabine prolonged disease-free survival. The 2007 primary analysis (median follow-up 53 months) reported median DFS 13.4 months (95% CI 11.4-15.3) vs 6.9 months (6.1-7.8), P<.001, among the 354 eligible randomised patients, and reports no hazard ratio for any endpoint; its overall-survival comparison was not significant (22.1 vs 20.2 months, P=.06, with 27% of patients still alive). The 2013 long-term analysis (median follow-up 136 months) reported DFS HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.44-0.69, P<.001; 13.4 vs 6.7 months) and OS HR 0.76 (0.61-0.95, P=.01), with 5-year OS 20.7% vs 10.4%. Established adjuvant gemcitabine as a standard of care.

records.title: ESPAC-4
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2017
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma Adjuvant gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² weekly (3 of 4 weeks) + capecitabine 1660 mg/m²/day, days 1–21 (28-day cycle), 6 cycles vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² alone (same schedule) Overall survival Adding capecitabine to gemcitabine improved median OS (28.0 vs 25.5 months, HR 0.82, p=0.032); established gemcitabine-capecitabine as an adjuvant standard for fit patients.

records.title: PRODIGE 24/CCTG PA.6
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2018
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-1 Adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX — oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 180 mg/m² (reduced to 150 after a safety analysis) + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, Q2W ×12 (6 months) vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² on days 1, 8, 15 every 28 days ×6 Disease-free survival mFOLFIRINOX markedly improved DFS (21.6 vs 12.8 months, HR 0.58) and OS (54.4 vs 35.0 months, HR 0.64); established mFOLFIRINOX as the adjuvant standard for fit patients.

records.title: APACT
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma Adjuvant nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² on days 1, 8, 15 of each 28-day cycle ×6 vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² alone (same schedule) Independently-assessed disease-free survival Adding nab-paclitaxel did not improve independently-reviewed DFS (19.4 vs 18.8 months, HR 0.88, p=0.18) though OS trended better (41.8 vs 37.7 months, HR 0.82); failed to establish the doublet as an adjuvant standard.

records.title: GITSG
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · N/A · 1985
records.body: Resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma Postop 5-FU chemoradiation + maintenance 5-FU vs observation Overall survival Adjuvant 5-FU chemoradiation doubled median OS (20 vs 11 months, p=0.035) and 2-year OS (42% vs 15%); first trial to suggest an adjuvant benefit, though small and slow-accruing.

records.title: EORTC 40891
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · III · 1999
records.body: Resected pancreatic head or periampullary cancer (T1-2 N0-1) Postop 40 Gy + 5-FU chemoradiation vs observation Overall survival Adjuvant 5-FU chemoradiation did not improve OS (death-rate ratio 0.91, p=0.54); failed to confirm a chemoradiation benefit and tempered enthusiasm for the GITSG result.

records.title: RTOG 9704
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · III · 2008
records.body: Resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma 5-FU vs gemcitabine before and after 5-FU-based chemoradiation Overall survival For pancreatic-head tumors, gemcitabine numerically improved median OS (20.5 vs 16.9 months, HR 0.82, p=0.09) but without statistical significance; supported gemcitabine sequencing without proving superiority.

records.title: Prep-02/JSAP-05
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · III · 2026
records.body: Resectable (or borderline by portal vein) pancreatic adenocarcinoma Neoadjuvant gemcitabine + S-1 then surgery vs upfront surgery (both → adjuvant S-1) Overall survival Neoadjuvant gemcitabine + S-1 improved median OS over upfront surgery (37.0 vs 26.6 months, HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.56-0.95, p=0.018); mature full-text results confirm and supersede the earlier ASCO-GI 2019 abstract (which reported 36.7 vs 26.6 months, HR 0.72, p=0.015). First RCT to show a neoadjuvant survival benefit in resectable disease.

records.title: SWOG S1505
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · II · 2021
records.body: Resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma Perioperative (12 weeks pre-op + 12 weeks post-op) modified FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 180 mg/m² + leucovorin + 5-FU 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, Q2W) vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² (days 1, 8, 15) 2-year overall survival Neither perioperative regimen cleared the prespecified 40% benchmark for 2-year overall survival: 47% (95% CI 31-61) with mFOLFIRINOX and 48% (95% CI 31-63) with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, with median overall survival of 23.2 and 23.6 months. Because that threshold was not met in either arm, the pick-the-winner design never ran a head-to-head survival comparison, so the two regimens were not shown to be equivalent and neither was selected. Central radiology review found 43 of the 146 patients it reviewed (29%) ineligible; with one further ineligibility and one withdrawal, 102 of the 147 enrolled were eligible and evaluable.

records.title: NORPACT-1
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · II · 2024
records.body: Resectable pancreatic head ductal adenocarcinoma per NCCN resectable criteria (no arterial contact, venous contact ≤180° without contour irregularity, no metastasis); fit for pancreatoduodenectomy; WHO PS 0-1; radiologically strongly suspected adenocarcinoma, excludes grade ≥2 neuropathy Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX x4 cycles → surgery → adjuvant chemo vs upfront surgery → adjuvant chemo (gemcitabine+capecitabine or modified FOLFIRINOX per amendment) Primary: overall survival at 18 months. Secondary: median overall survival, progression-free survival, R0 resection, ypN0, resection rate, surgical complications, safety Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX did not improve survival in resectable pancreatic head cancer and may have worsened it: 18-month OS 60% vs 73% and median OS 25.1 vs 38.5 months (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.00-2.33) favouring upfront surgery. Resection rate unchanged (82% vs 89%). R0 (56% vs 39%) and node-negative (29% vs 14%) status improved with neoadjuvant therapy, but severe toxicity rose (58% vs 40%, including 2 deaths after the first neoadjuvant cycle). Argues against routine neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX for clearly resectable disease.

records.title: PREOPANC
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · III · 2020
records.body: Resectable & borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma Neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy then surgery vs upfront surgery Overall survival At long-term follow-up, neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy versus upfront surgery showed 5-year overall survival of 20.5% versus 6.5% and HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.56-0.96), nominal P=0.025. The R0 resection rate by intention to treat was 41% (49/119) versus 28% (35/127), nominal P=0.025. The resectability interaction P was 0.56.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2020;38:1763-1773   J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1220-1230 long-term results 35084987

records.title: Alliance A021501
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · II · 2022
records.body: Borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma (head) Neoadjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX vs mFOLFIRINOX + hypofractionated radiotherapy 18-month overall survival Adding hypofractionated/SBRT radiotherapy did not help; the mFOLFIRINOX-alone arm reached 18-month OS 66.4% and median OS 29.8 months and was favored, arguing against routine radiotherapy after FOLFIRINOX.

records.title: ESPAC-5 (ESPAC-5F)
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · II · 2023
records.body: Borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma Immediate surgery vs neoadjuvant gem-cap, FOLFIRINOX, or capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy Recruitment & resection rate (1-year OS secondary) Short-course neoadjuvant therapy improved 1-year overall survival over immediate surgery (76% vs 39%; HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.14-0.60, p=0.0052), and did so despite a lower crude resection rate (55% vs 68%, p=0.33). By arm, 1-year survival was 84% with FOLFIRINOX, 78% with gemcitabine plus capecitabine, 60% with chemoradiotherapy and 39% with immediate surgery (p=0.0028 across all four groups). Survival was a secondary outcome of a feasibility trial powered only for resection rate, with 90 randomised and 86 analysed, at 12.2 months median follow-up and with no multiplicity control.

records.title: PREOPANC-2
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · III · 2025
records.body: Resectable & borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX vs neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy (+ adjuvant gemcitabine) Overall survival Total neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX did not improve OS over neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy (median 21.9 vs 21.3 months, HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.69-1.13, p=0.32); both neoadjuvant strategies are acceptable options.

records.title: CASSANDRA (PACT-21)
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · III · 2025
records.body: Stage I-III resectable & borderline resectable PDAC, age ≤75, KPS ≥70 Preoperative PAXG (cisplatin 30 mg/m² + nab-paclitaxel 150 mg/m² + gemcitabine 800 mg/m² + capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily [1250 mg/m²/day], every 14 days) vs modified FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 150 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 2400 mg/m², every 14 days) Event-free survival Preoperative PAXG (cisplatin, nab-paclitaxel, gemcitabine, capecitabine) improved EFS over modified FOLFIRINOX (median 16.0 vs 10.2 months, HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.47-0.84, p=0.0018; corrected from a prior HR 0.64/p=0.003 transcription); positions PAXG as a more active neoadjuvant regimen pending mature OS from the first-randomisation analysis. The previously-listed "3-year EFS 31% vs 13%" figure has been removed: it is not stated in the PMID 41275879 Lancet abstract (which reports only median EFS in months), could not be verified against this citation, and is likely from an unconfirmed conference slide.

records.title: Burris (gemcitabine)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 1997
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, symptomatic Gemcitabine vs bolus 5-fluorouracil Clinical benefit response Clinical benefit response 23.8% vs 4.8% (p=0.0022) and median OS 5.65 vs 4.41 months (p=0.0025); established gemcitabine as the first-line standard.

records.title: NCIC PA.3
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2007
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma Gemcitabine + erlotinib vs gemcitabine + placebo Overall survival Median OS 6.24 vs 5.91 months (HR 0.82, p=0.038) and 1-year OS 23% vs 17%; first targeted agent to improve survival, though benefit was marginal.

records.title: GEM-CAP (Cunningham)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2009
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma Gemcitabine + capecitabine vs gemcitabine Overall survival Median OS 7.1 vs 6.2 months (HR 0.86, p=0.077), not significant, though a meta-analysis supported benefit; a modest combination option.

records.title: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11 (FOLFIRINOX)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2011
records.body: Untreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-1 FOLFIRINOX — oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 180 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, Q2W vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² weekly (7 of 8 weeks, then 3 of 4 weeks) Overall survival Median OS 11.1 vs 6.8 months (HR 0.57, p<0.001) and PFS 6.4 vs 3.3 months; established FOLFIRINOX as a standard for fit patients.

records.title: MPACT
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2013
records.body: Untreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² on days 1, 8, 15 every 4 weeks vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² weekly (7 of 8 weeks, then days 1, 8, 15 every 4 weeks) Overall survival Median OS 8.5 vs 6.7 months (HR 0.72, p<0.001) and PFS 5.5 vs 3.7 months; established gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel as an alternative first-line standard.

records.title: NAPOLI-3 (NALIRIFOX)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-1 NALIRIFOX — liposomal irinotecan 50 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 60 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, days 1 & 15 of a 28-day cycle vs nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² (days 1, 8, 15 of a 28-day cycle) Overall survival Median OS 11.1 vs 9.2 months (HR 0.83, p=0.036) and PFS 7.4 vs 5.6 months; a liposomal-irinotecan triplet alternative to FOLFIRINOX.

records.title: PANOPTIMOX (PRODIGE 35)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Maintenance therapy · II · 2021
records.body: Untreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma controlled on FOLFIRINOX induction 6 mo FOLFIRINOX vs 4 mo FOLFIRINOX then 5-FU/LV maintenance vs alternating gemcitabine/FOLFIRI.3 Progression-free survival at 6 months Median OS 10.1 vs 11.2 vs 7.3 months across arms; 5-FU/LV maintenance after FOLFIRINOX induction is feasible and effective, supporting an induction-maintenance strategy.

records.title: POLO
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Maintenance therapy · III · 2019
records.body: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, germline BRCA1/2 mutation, no progression on platinum Maintenance olaparib vs placebo Progression-free survival Median PFS 7.4 vs 3.8 months (HR 0.53, p=0.004); OS not improved; first biomarker-driven maintenance, establishing olaparib for germline BRCA-mutated disease.

records.title: CONKO-003
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Second-line therapy · III · 2014
records.body: Advanced gemcitabine-refractory pancreatic adenocarcinoma Oxaliplatin/folinic acid/5-FU (OFF) vs folinic acid/5-FU (FF) Overall survival Median OS 5.9 vs 3.3 months (HR 0.66, p=0.01); established a fluoropyrimidine/oxaliplatin option after gemcitabine failure.

records.title: NAPOLI-1
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Second-line therapy · III · 2016
records.body: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma after gemcitabine-based therapy Liposomal irinotecan (nal-IRI) 80 mg/m² (70 mg/m² irinotecan base) + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, Q2W vs 5-FU/leucovorin; a nal-IRI monotherapy arm (120 mg/m² Q3W) was also included Overall survival Median OS 6.1 vs 4.2 months (HR 0.67, p=0.012) and PFS 3.1 vs 1.5 months; established nal-IRI/5-FU/LV as a second-line standard after gemcitabine.

records.title: CodeBreaK 100 (sotorasib)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Biomarker-directed therapy · II · 2023
records.body: Previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma Sotorasib 960 mg once daily (single-arm; KRAS G12C) Objective response rate ORR 21% with median PFS 4.0 months and OS 6.9 months; first KRAS G12C inhibitor with activity in pancreatic cancer, an option for the rare G12C subset.

records.title: RASolute 302 (daraxonrasib)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Biomarker-directed therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Previously treated metastatic PDAC, RAS-mutant (91.8% RAS G12) Daraxonrasib (oral RAS(ON) inhibitor) 300 mg once daily vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy (e.g. gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel) Overall survival & progression-free survival (RAS G12) Daraxonrasib roughly doubled OS vs chemotherapy (13.2 vs 6.7 months, HR 0.40) and improved PFS (7.2 vs 3.6 months, HR 0.49), with fewer treatment discontinuations; first targeted therapy to show a major survival benefit in RAS-mutant pancreatic cancer.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: FOLFIRINOX in LAPC (Suker meta-analysis)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · N/A · 2016
records.body: Locally advanced unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma FOLFIRINOX (patient-level pooled analysis) Overall survival Pooled median OS 24.2 months, far exceeding historical gemcitabine (6-13 months); supports FOLFIRINOX induction for locally advanced disease.

records.title: LAP07
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · III · 2016
records.body: Locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma controlled after 4 months of gemcitabine-based induction Chemoradiotherapy vs continued chemotherapy (after induction) Overall survival Median OS 15.2 vs 16.5 months (HR 1.03, p=0.83), no survival benefit, though chemoradiotherapy reduced local progression (32% vs 46%); chemotherapy alone remained standard.

records.title: PANOVA-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · III · 2025
records.body: Adults aged 18 years and older with unresectable, locally advanced, biopsy-confirmed, previously untreated pancreatic adenocarcinoma (LA-PAC), life expectancy >=3 months, ECOG PS 0-2. Excluded: implantable electronic medical devices in the torso, and severe hypersensitivity to medical adhesives, hydrogel or the study chemotherapies. 196 sites in 20 countries; enrolled May 2018 to March 2023. TTFields 150 kHz (NovoTTF-200T) worn continuously, recommended average usage >=75% (>=18 h/d), arrays replaced 2-3x/wk + nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 IV followed immediately by gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle; to local progression (RECIST v1.1), intolerable toxicity, noncompliance, pregnancy or withdrawal of consent vs Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 IV followed immediately by gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle; to local progression (RECIST v1.1), intolerable toxicity, noncompliance, pregnancy or withdrawal of consent Overall survival (OS) — time from random assignment to date of death or censoring Adding Tumor Treating Fields (150 kHz, worn continuously) to gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel met its primary endpoint: median OS 16.2 vs 14.2 months (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.99; stratified log-rank P=.039 against a prespecified boundary of .04794). PFS, the only other endpoint inside the testing hierarchy, was not improved (10.6 vs 9.3 months; HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.68-1.05; P=.137), so the hierarchy stopped there and every remaining endpoint carries a nominal, alpha-unprotected p-value: pain-free survival 15.2 vs 9.1 months (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.56-0.97; P=.027), 1-year survival 68.1% vs 60.2% (P=.029), ORR 36.1% vs 30.0% (P=.094, not significant), and resectability numerically lower with TTFields (7.0% vs 10.1%, no p-value reported). Device-related adverse events affected 209 of 274 treated patients (76.3%) and were mainly mild-to-moderate skin reactions, most frequently dermatitis (27.7%); no death was attributed to TTFields. Open-label with no sham device and investigator-assessed response, so the 2.0-month difference in median OS must be weighed against continuous device wear.

records.title: SURF Trial
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Curative-intent locoregional therapy — ablation · N/A · 2022
records.body: Initial HCC, ≤3 nodules and largest lesion ≤3 cm, amenable to both resection and percutaneous RFA after multidisciplinary review; excludes lesions near vasculature, biliary tree or adjacent organs, or not clearly visualised by ultrasound, when RFA is infeasible Surgical resection (open or laparoscopic, local technique) vs percutaneous ultrasound-guided RFA with CT margin confirmation; repeat RFA within 2 weeks for incomplete treatment. Single local-treatment course; no fixed postoperative course reported. Primary: recurrence-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: local recurrence, serious adverse effects, treatment for recurrence Resection did not improve OS or RFS over RFA for small initial HCC; early closure means the results do not establish equivalence. At median follow-up 6.4/6.6 years, 5-year OS was 74.6% versus 70.4% (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.64-1.43) and 5-year RFS 42.9% versus 42.7% (HR 0.90, 0.67-1.22). Local recurrence was 8.0% versus 15.8%; serious adverse effects 3.3% versus none. Accrual stopped at 308 of 600 target.
records.keywords: Liver Cancer 2022;11:209-218   J Clin Oncol 2025;43:2628-2638 final OS and updated RFS analysis 40554738

records.title: Llovet (BCLC)
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) · N/A · 2002
records.body: Unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A/B, Okuda I/II, not for curative therapy Arterial embolisation or chemoembolisation (doxorubicin) vs symptomatic care Overall survival Chemoembolisation improved survival (1- and 2-year 82% and 63% vs 63% and 27% for control; HR of death 0.47); established TACE as standard of care for unresectable intermediate-stage HCC.

records.title: SARAH
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Transarterial radioembolization (Y-90 / SIRT) · III · 2017
records.body: Locally advanced or inoperable HCC, including portal vein invasion Y-90 resin microsphere radioembolisation (SIRT) vs sorafenib Overall survival SIRT did not improve OS over sorafenib (median 8.0 vs 9.9 months, HR 1.15) despite higher tumour response (19% vs 12%) and better tolerability/quality of life; Y-90 is not a substitute for systemic therapy in advanced HCC.

records.title: DOSISPHERE-01
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Transarterial radioembolization (Y-90 / SIRT) · II · 2021
records.body: Locally advanced HCC ≥7 cm, eligible for Y-90 glass microspheres Personalised dosimetry (≥205 Gy to index lesion) vs standard dosimetry (120 Gy) Objective response rate (EASL) Personalised dosimetry doubled response (71% vs 36%) and markedly improved OS (median 26.6 vs 10.7 months); established tumour-dose–guided Y-90 radioembolisation.

records.title: TACTICS
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · II · 2020
records.body: Adults with liver-confined unresectable HCC amenable to TACE but unsuitable for resection/ablation; no vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread, ≤10 tumours each ≤10 cm, ECOG 0-1, Child-Pugh ≤7. Prior systemic therapy excluded. On-demand conventional TACE plus sorafenib 400 mg/day for 2-3 weeks before first TACE, held around TACE then restarted 400 mg/day with optional escalation to 800 mg/day vs on-demand conventional TACE alone; continue until unTACEable progression, refractoriness, intolerable toxicity or withdrawal. Primary: TACE-specific progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, safety TACE plus sorafenib improved the trial-specific PFS endpoint but did not improve final OS. In 156 ITT patients, TACE-specific PFS, which did not count new intrahepatic lesions as progression, was 22.8 versus 13.5 months (HR 0.661, 95% CI 0.466-0.938); OS was 36.2 versus 30.8 months (HR 0.861, 0.607-1.223). In 77/71 treated, grade-3 hypertension within 8 weeks after first TACE was 10.4% versus 4.2%.

records.title: EMERALD-1
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with HCC not amenable to resection, ablation or transplant but amenable to up to four TACE procedures within 16 weeks; no extrahepatic disease, Child-Pugh A-B7, ECOG 0-1 and measurable intrahepatic disease. Endoscopy assessed variceal bleeding risk. TACE 1-4 procedures within 16 weeks plus durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks starting ≥7 days after first TACE → durvalumab 1120 mg IV plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks starting ≥14 days after last TACE vs the same durvalumab schedule plus bevacizumab placebo vs double placebo; continue to mRECIST progression, toxicity, withdrawal or other discontinuation, with treatment beyond progression allowed for clinical benefit Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, time to progression, safety Adding bevacizumab to durvalumab-TACE improved PFS; durvalumab-TACE alone did not. BICR RECIST PFS was 15.0 versus 8.2 months with durvalumab-bevacizumab versus placebo (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.98) and 10.0 versus 8.2 months with durvalumab alone (HR 0.94, 0.75-1.19). In the 154/232/200 treatment-received safety sets, grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs were 27%/6%/6%; haemorrhagic AEs 28%/10%/14%, with fatal haemorrhage 0%/3%/1%.

records.title: LEAP-012
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with unresectable, non-metastatic liver-only HCC amenable to TACE, no portal-vein invasion or extrahepatic spread, measurable disease, ECOG 0-1 and Child-Pugh A; excluded tumour ≥10 cm, >10 tumours or ≥50% liver involvement. TACE plus lenvatinib 12 mg orally daily (≥60 kg) or 8 mg daily (<60 kg) plus pembrolizumab 400 mg IV every 6 weeks for up to 2 years vs matched oral/IV placebos plus TACE; oral therapy held around TACE and otherwise continued to progression, toxicity, physician discontinuation or withdrawal. Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, time to progression, safety Lenvatinib-pembrolizumab-TACE improved PFS, but first-interim OS did not reach statistical significance. In 480 randomised patients, BICR RECIST PFS was 14.6 versus 10.0 months (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.51-0.84); interim OS HR was 0.80 (0.57-1.11), with 29% versus 34% deaths. In 237/241 treated, grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 71%/32% and treatment-related deaths 2%/<1%.

records.title: EMERALD-3
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Adults ≥18 years with confirmed unresectable embolisation-eligible HCC; liver function, ECOG status, stage, vascular invasion, extrahepatic disease and exclusion criteria were not reported TACE plus STRIDE (tremelimumab 300 mg plus durvalumab 1500 mg on day 1, then durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks) plus lenvatinib 8 or 12 mg once daily vs TACE plus STRIDE vs TACE; durvalumab and lenvatinib continued for ≤36 months, progression, toxicity or consent withdrawal; TACE schedule not reported Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety The abstract-only triplet improved primary PFS, while interim OS benefit was not established; STRIDE-TACE had favourable key-secondary PFS and OS estimates versus the first 175 TACE controls. Triplet versus TACE had PFS 13.0 versus 9.8 months (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.57-0.86) and interim OS 39.5 versus 34.7 months (HR 0.84, 0.65-1.09; 40% maturity). STRIDE-TACE versus TACE had PFS 12.9 versus 8.1 months (HR 0.71, 0.56-0.91) and median OS not calculable versus 32.9 months (HR 0.70, 0.51-0.95; 45% maturity). Grade 3/4 treatment-related AEs were 62.7%, 48.6% and 18.6% with triplet, STRIDE-TACE and TACE; safety denominators were not reported.

records.title: STORM
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Adjuvant therapy after resection / ablation · III · 2015
records.body: HCC at high recurrence risk after curative resection or ablation Adjuvant sorafenib vs placebo Recurrence-free survival Sorafenib did not improve RFS (median 33.4 vs 33.8 months, HR 0.94) or OS; showed adjuvant TKI therapy has no role after curative HCC treatment.

records.title: IMbrave050
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Adjuvant therapy after resection / ablation · III · 2023
records.body: Resected or ablated HCC at high risk of recurrence Adjuvant atezolizumab + bevacizumab (1 year) vs active surveillance Recurrence-free survival Improved RFS at the interim analysis (HR 0.72), but the benefit was not maintained on updated analysis; adjuvant atezolizumab/bevacizumab is not established as standard.

records.title: SHARP
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2008
records.body: Advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A, no prior systemic therapy (Western) Sorafenib vs placebo Overall survival Sorafenib improved median OS (10.7 vs 7.9 months, HR 0.69) and time to progression (5.5 vs 2.8 months); established the first systemic standard for advanced HCC.

records.title: Asia-Pacific (Cheng)
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2009
records.body: Advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A, Asia-Pacific (largely HBV-related) Sorafenib vs placebo Overall survival Sorafenib improved OS (6.5 vs 4.2 months, HR 0.68) and TTP (2.8 vs 1.4 months); confirmed sorafenib benefit in a predominantly hepatitis B Asian population.

records.title: REFLECT
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated unresectable HCC, BCLC B/C, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1 with measurable disease; excluded ≥50% liver occupation, main portal-vein invasion, bile-duct invasion and prior systemic HCC therapy. Lenvatinib 12 mg orally daily (≥60 kg) or 8 mg daily (<60 kg) in 28-day cycles vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily in 28-day cycles; no protocol stopping rule was reported, with median treatment duration 5.7 versus 3.7 months Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to progression, objective response rate, quality of life, pharmacokinetics, safety Lenvatinib was non-inferior but not superior to sorafenib for OS; it improved PFS and ORR without a validated treatment-selecting subgroup. In 954 ITT patients, OS was 13.6 versus 12.3 months (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.79-1.06); independent RECIST PFS 7.3 versus 3.6 months (HR 0.65, 0.56-0.77) and mRECIST ORR 40.6% versus 12.4%. In 476/475 treated, grade ≥3 AEs were 75%/67%; treatment-related deaths 11/4.

records.title: IMbrave150
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2020
records.body: Adults with locally advanced, metastatic or unresectable HCC, no prior systemic liver-cancer therapy, measurable disease, ECOG 0-1 and Child-Pugh A; untreated/incompletely treated high-risk oesophageal/gastric varices excluded after endoscopic assessment. Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily; continue to loss of clinical benefit or unacceptable toxicity. Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, quality of life, safety Atezolizumab-bevacizumab retained longer OS and PFS than sorafenib at the descriptive update. In 501 ITT patients at 15.6-month median follow-up, OS was 19.2 versus 13.4 months (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.52-0.85), PFS 6.9 versus 4.3 months (HR 0.65, 0.53-0.81), and ORR 30% versus 11% in 326/159 measurable-disease patients. In 329/156 treated, grade 3/4 treatment-related AEs were 43%/46% and treatment-related deaths 6/1; hypertension/proteinuria increased with longer exposure.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2020;382:1894-1905   J Hepatol 2022;76:862-873 updated OS analysis 34902530

records.title: HIMALAYA
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2022
records.body: Adults with histologically confirmed unresectable HCC, no prior systemic therapy and ineligible for locoregional treatment; BCLC B/C, Child-Pugh A, ECOG 0-1 and measurable disease. Main portal-vein thrombosis and clinically meaningful ascites were excluded. STRIDE: tremelimumab 300 mg IV once plus durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks vs durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily; continue to progression, toxicity, withdrawal or protocol discontinuation. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, quality of life, safety STRIDE retained a longer-term OS advantage over sorafenib, and durvalumab monotherapy was noninferior but not superior. In the 393/389 STRIDE/sorafenib ITT arms, median OS was 16.4 versus 13.8 months (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.67-0.92) and 48-month OS 25.2% versus 15.1%. In the 389/389 durvalumab/sorafenib ITT arms at the primary analysis, the OS HR was 0.86 (95.67% CI 0.73-1.03). In 388/388/374 treated, serious treatment-related AEs were 17.5%, 8.5% and 9.6% with STRIDE, durvalumab and sorafenib.
records.keywords: NEJM Evid 2022;1:EVIDoa2100070   Ann Oncol 2024;35:448-457 4-yr OS update 38382875

records.title: CheckMate 9DW
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with advanced HCC not eligible for curative/locoregional therapy or progressing after it, no prior systemic therapy, measurable disease, Child-Pugh 5-6 and ECOG 0-1; Vp4 invasion and clinically significant ascites excluded. Nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for ≤4 doses then nivolumab 480 mg IV every 4 weeks (maximum 2 years) vs investigator-choice lenvatinib 8/12 mg daily or sorafenib 400 mg twice daily; continue to progression, toxicity or withdrawal. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, time to symptom deterioration, progression-free survival, quality of life, safety At the preplanned interim, nivolumab-ipilimumab improved OS and ORR but not median PFS versus a comparator that was 85% lenvatinib; crossed OS curves showed early harm before later benefit. In 668 ITT patients, OS was 23.7 versus 20.6 months (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.65-0.96); exploratory piecewise HR was 1.65 in the first 6 months and 0.61 thereafter. ORR was 36% versus 13% and PFS 9.1 versus 9.2 months (HR 0.87, 0.72-1.06). In 332/325 treated, grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs were 41%/42%, serious grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs 25%/13%, and treatment-related deaths 12/3, including 11/1 within 6 months.

records.title: CARES-310
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2023
records.body: Adults with BCLC B/C HCC not amenable to or progressed after surgery/locoregional therapy, no prior systemic therapy, measurable disease, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1. Recent/high-risk gastrointestinal bleeding and uncontrolled hypertension were excluded. Camrelizumab 200 mg IV every 2 weeks plus rivoceranib 250 mg orally daily vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily; continue to BIRC progression, toxicity, consent withdrawal or investigator decision, with treatment beyond progression allowed for clinical benefit; rivoceranib reductions to 5-days-on/2-days-off then alternate days, no camrelizumab reduction Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, time to progression, quality of life, safety Camrelizumab-rivoceranib retained longer OS and PFS than sorafenib at final follow-up, with substantial toxicity. In 543 ITT patients at 351 deaths, OS was 23.8 versus 15.2 months (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.52-0.79) and updated PFS 5.6 versus 3.7 months (HR 0.54, 0.44-0.67). In 272/269 treated, grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 81%/54%, grade 3-4 hypertension 38%/15%, rivoceranib/sorafenib dose reduction 48%/33%, and treatment-related deaths 1/1.
records.keywords: Lancet 2023;402:1133-1146   Lancet Oncol 2025;26:1598-1611 final OS analysis 41308676

records.title: RESORCE
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2017
records.body: HCC progressing on sorafenib, Child-Pugh A, sorafenib-tolerant Regorafenib + best supportive care vs placebo + BSC Overall survival Regorafenib improved OS (median 10.6 vs 7.8 months, HR 0.63); first agent to show benefit after sorafenib progression.

records.title: CELESTIAL
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Adults with pathological advanced HCC not amenable to curative treatment, previously treated with sorafenib and progressed after ≥1 systemic regimen; up to 2 prior systemic regimens, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1 Cabozantinib 60 mg orally once daily versus placebo; reductions to 40 then 20 mg permitted. Treatment continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or protocol discontinuation. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, safety Cabozantinib improved OS and PFS after sorafenib, but most patients required dose reduction. In the 707-patient ITT second interim, OS was 10.2 versus 8.0 months (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.63-0.92) and PFS 5.2 versus 1.9 months (HR 0.44, 0.36-0.52). In 467/237 treated, grade 3/4 AEs were 68%/36%; 62% reduced dose to median 35.8 mg from 60 mg. Treatment-related deaths were 6/1.

records.title: REACH-2
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2019
records.body: Advanced HCC after sorafenib with AFP ≥400 ng/mL Ramucirumab + best supportive care vs placebo + BSC Overall survival Ramucirumab improved OS (median 8.5 vs 7.3 months, HR 0.71) in AFP-high patients; first biomarker-selected systemic therapy in HCC.

records.title: CheckMate 040 / 459
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · I/II–III · 2022
records.body: CheckMate 459: untreated first-line advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1 (743 randomised). CheckMate 040 reports: sorafenib-experienced nivolumab monotherapy (154 treated) and nivolumab-ipilimumab after progression on or intolerance of sorafenib (148 randomised; 146 previously received sorafenib), Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1 CheckMate 459: nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily until progression, toxicity, consent withdrawal or study closure. CheckMate 040 monotherapy: nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks until progression, toxicity or discontinuation, with the escalation phase capped at 2 years. CheckMate 040 combination: arm A nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks ×4 → nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks; arm B nivolumab 3 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg on the same induction/maintenance schedule; arm C nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks; combination-cohort treatment duration and stopping rules were not reported Primary: overall survival, safety, tolerability, objective response rate. Secondary: progression-free survival, duration of response, disease control, time to progression, quality of life Nivolumab monotherapy activity did not translate into confirmed first-line OS benefit, whereas nivolumab-ipilimumab remained active and was later confirmed first-line in CheckMate 9DW. CheckMate 459 missed its OS primary endpoint: 16.4 versus 14.7 months (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.72-1.02); grade-3 treatment-related AEs were 18% versus 47% in 367/363 treated. At 5 years, sorafenib-experienced nivolumab monotherapy ORR was 14% by BICR (22/154). In the 148-patient combination cohort, arm A ORR was 32% and median OS 22.8 months (95% CI 9.4-not reached); the study was not powered for arm comparisons, and 1 treatment-related death occurred in 146 treated. At its preplanned interim, CheckMate 9DW showed OS 23.7 versus 20.6 months (HR 0.79), but OS curves crossed (first-6-month HR 1.65) and 11 of 12 versus 1 of 3 treatment-related deaths occurred within 6 months.

records.title: KEYNOTE-394
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2023
records.body: Asian adults with advanced HCC after progression on/intolerance to sorafenib or oxaliplatin chemotherapy, BCLC B/C not amenable to curative/locoregional therapy, Child-Pugh A, ECOG 0-1 and measurable disease. Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks plus best supportive care versus saline placebo IV every 3 weeks plus best supportive care, each for up to 35 cycles. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, disease control, time to progression, safety and tolerability Pembrolizumab modestly improved OS, PFS and ORR after sorafenib or oxaliplatin chemotherapy in Asian patients. In 453 ITT patients, final OS was 14.6 versus 13.0 months (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.99); PFS was 2.6 versus 2.3 months (HR 0.74) and BICR ORR 12.7% versus 1.3%. In 299/153 treated, treatment-related grade 3/4 AEs were 12.0%/1.3% versus 5.9%/0%. Three grade-5 treatment-related AEs occurred with pembrolizumab—gastrointestinal haemorrhage, immune-mediated hepatitis and soft-tissue infection—and none with placebo.

records.title: IMbrave251
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Locally advanced/metastatic HCC after ≥4 cycles of atezolizumab-bevacizumab, ≥2 tumour assessments and prior disease control before progression; hepatic function, ECOG status and other exclusion criteria were not reported Atezolizumab 1200 mg every 3 weeks plus lenvatinib 8 mg (<60 kg) or 12 mg (≥60 kg) QW or sorafenib 800 mg QW vs the same TKI alone, preserving the source-printed schedules; 92.1% received lenvatinib and 7.9% sorafenib overall, but arm-specific TKI allocation, atezolizumab route and stopping rule were not reported; median lenvatinib duration 5.6 versus 4.7 months and sorafenib 2.9 versus 2.3 months Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, time to progression, quality of life, safety Continuing atezolizumab with a TKI after atezolizumab-bevacizumab progression did not improve OS or PFS over TKI alone. In 557 patients, OS was 14.6 versus 12.5 months (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.72-1.08), PFS 4.3 versus 4.8 months (HR 1.05, 0.88-1.25), and ORR 7.5% versus 5.8%. In 279/275 safety patients, grade 3/4 AEs were 74.2%/66.2%, grade-5 AEs 5.4%/5.8%, serious AEs 40.1%/36.7%, and withdrawal for AEs 11.8%/6.9%.

records.title: NEO-GAP
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · II · 2023
records.body: Resectable high-risk intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (>5 cm, multifocal, vascular invasion, or node+) Single-arm neoadjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin + nab-paclitaxel (GAP) x4 Feasibility (completion of therapy and resection) Neoadjuvant GAP was feasible: 77% completed chemotherapy and underwent resection (PR 23%, DCR 90%) without excess surgical morbidity; supported further perioperative study.

records.title: GAIN (AIO/CALGP/ACO)
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · III · 2025
records.body: Resectable biliary tract cancer / incidental gallbladder carcinoma Neoadjuvant gem-cis then resection vs immediate resection (± adjuvant) Overall survival Neoadjuvant gem-cis improved median OS (27.8 vs 14.6 months) and R0 resection (62.5% vs 33.3%) vs upfront surgery; closed early at N=68, so signal-generating rather than definitive.

records.title: GOLP (ZSAB-neoGOLP)
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · III · 2026
records.body: Resectable high-risk intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma Neoadjuvant GEMOX + lenvatinib + toripalimab then surgery vs immediate surgery Event-free survival Neoadjuvant GOLP prolonged EFS (18.0 vs 8.7 months, HR 0.43) without compromising resection at the interim analysis (not yet crossing the significance boundary); first randomized support for neoadjuvant therapy in high-risk iCCA.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: PRODIGE 12/ACCORD 18
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Adjuvant therapy after resection · III · 2019
records.body: Resected (R0/R1) biliary tract cancer, all sites Adjuvant gemcitabine + oxaliplatin (GEMOX) x12 vs surveillance Relapse-free survival GEMOX did not improve RFS (median 30.4 vs 18.5 months, HR 0.88) or OS; a negative trial that did not support adjuvant GEMOX.

records.title: BILCAP
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Adjuvant therapy after resection · III · 2019
records.body: Resected (R0/R1) cholangiocarcinoma or muscle-invasive gallbladder cancer Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily, days 1–14 of a 21-day cycle ×8 vs observation Overall survival Missed the ITT OS endpoint (51.1 vs 36.4 months, HR 0.81, p=0.097) but improved OS in the prespecified per-protocol analysis (53 vs 36 months, HR 0.75); adopted as the adjuvant standard of care.

records.title: ASCOT (JCOG1202)
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Adjuvant therapy after resection · III · 2023
records.body: Resected biliary tract cancer (all sites), Asian patients Adjuvant S-1 (40/50/60 mg by body-surface area, twice daily) 4 weeks on / 2 weeks off ×4 cycles vs observation Overall survival S-1 improved 3-year OS (77.1% vs 67.6%, HR 0.69); established adjuvant S-1 as a standard for resected BTC in Asian patients.

records.title: ABC-02
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · First-line advanced — chemotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2010
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer Cisplatin + gemcitabine vs gemcitabine alone Overall survival Cisplatin-gemcitabine improved OS (11.7 vs 8.1 months, HR 0.64) and PFS (8.0 vs 5.0 months); established gem-cis as the first-line standard for over a decade.

records.title: TOPAZ-1
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · First-line advanced — chemotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2022
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic biliary tract cancer Durvalumab 1500 mg IV day 1 of each 21-day cycle + gemcitabine–cisplatin (up to 8 cycles) → durvalumab 1500 mg monotherapy Q4W to progression vs placebo + gemcitabine–cisplatin → placebo Overall survival Adding durvalumab improved OS (12.8 vs 11.5 months, HR 0.80) with higher 24-month survival (24.9% vs 10.4%); first chemo-immunotherapy standard in advanced BTC.
