records.body: Advanced endometrial cancer after ≥1 prior platinum regimen Lenvatinib 20 mg orally once daily + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) vs physician's-choice chemotherapy (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² IV Q3W or paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly) Progression-free survival and overall survival Lenvatinib/pembrolizumab improved PFS (all-comers 7.2 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.56; pMMR 6.6 vs 3.8 months) and OS (18.3 vs 11.4 months, HR 0.62); established the standard second-line regimen for pMMR disease.

records.title: Fader (HER2+ serous)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Recurrent — immunotherapy & targeted therapy (pretreated) · II · 2018
records.body: Advanced (stage III-IV) or recurrent HER2-positive uterine serous carcinoma Carboplatin–paclitaxel Q3W ×6 cycles ± trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg IV Q3W, continued to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival Adding trastuzumab improved PFS (12.6 vs 8.0 months, HR 0.44), with the largest gain in stage III-IV disease; established HER2-directed therapy for HER2-positive uterine serous carcinoma.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2018;36:2044-2051   Clin Cancer Res 2020;26:3928-3935 updated OS analysis 32601075

records.title: DESTINY-PanTumor02 (endometrial cohort)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Recurrent — immunotherapy & targeted therapy (pretreated) · II · 2024
records.body: Previously treated HER2-expressing (IHC 3+/2+) advanced endometrial cancer (basket cohort) Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W to progression or toxicity (single-arm; HER2-expressing endometrial cohort) Objective response rate In the endometrial cohort, T-DXd produced ORR 57.5% (the highest among basket tumour types), with greatest activity in HER2 IHC3+ disease; supported the tumour-agnostic FDA approval of T-DXd for HER2 IHC3+ solid tumours, extending HER2-directed options beyond trastuzumab.

records.title: SIENDO / ENGOT-EN5 (Vergote)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Maintenance — emerging · III · 2023
records.body: Advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer in response after first-line chemotherapy Maintenance oral selinexor vs placebo Progression-free survival Maintenance selinexor modestly improved PFS in the ITT population (5.7 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.70); a pre-specified TP53-wild-type subgroup showed a large benefit (27.4 vs 5.2 months, HR 0.42), now under confirmatory study.

records.title: MACH-NC (Pignon)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Definitive chemoradiation & EGFR inhibition · N/A · 2009
records.body: Previously untreated, non-metastatic oral-cavity, oropharyngeal, hypopharyngeal or laryngeal SCC receiving potentially curative identical locoregional therapy with versus without chemotherapy; nasopharyngeal-only trials excluded Individual-patient-data meta-analysis: potentially curative surgery and/or radiotherapy plus chemotherapy versus the same locoregional treatment alone; timing cohorts included induction, concomitant and adjuvant chemotherapy Primary: overall survival. Secondary: event-free survival, locoregional failure, distant failure, cancer mortality, non-cancer mortality Adding chemotherapy to curative locoregional therapy improved overall survival (HR 0.88; 4.5% absolute 5-year benefit), but timing modified effect: concomitant chemotherapy gave the clearest benefit (HR 0.81; 6.5% absolute 5-year benefit), whereas induction and post-locoregional adjuvant chemotherapy did not improve OS. Benefit declined with age. This IPD meta-analysis spans historical regimens; timing analyses are exploratory and do not establish a single modern regimen

records.title: Bonner
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Definitive chemoradiation & EGFR inhibition · III · 2006
records.body: Stage III/IV, non-metastatic measurable SCC of the oropharynx, hypopharynx or larynx suitable for definitive radiotherapy; Karnofsky score at least 60 Definitive radiotherapy (once-daily, twice-daily or concomitant-boost schedule) plus cetuximab loading 400 mg/m² then 250 mg/m² weekly during RT versus the same RT alone Primary: duration of locoregional control. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival, overall response, safety, quality of life Cetuximab plus RT improved locoregional control and survival over RT alone; the 5-year update reported OS HR 0.73 and 5-year OS 45.6% versus 36.4%. Acneiform rash and infusion reactions increased, while severe mucositis was similar; the rash-survival association is post-randomisation and non-predictive. The comparator was RT alone—not cisplatin-CRT—and HPV/p16 was not assessed; the update did not collect new recurrence or late-toxicity data
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2006;354:567-578   Lancet Oncol 2010;11:21-28 5-year update 19897418

records.title: Pan-Asian ESMO Guideline (Keam et al.)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Definitive chemoradiation & EGFR inhibition · N/A · 2021
records.body: Pan-Asian 2021 guideline scope: SCC of oral cavity, larynx, oropharynx and hypopharynx; nasopharyngeal carcinoma excluded Descriptive EHNS-ESMO-ESTRO adaptation using evidence review, regional availability assessment and society voting; not a randomised treatment comparison Primary: not applicable. Secondary: guideline recommendations, evidence/grade descriptors, regional availability and management algorithms Historical 2021 Pan-Asian guidance identifies concomitant cisplatin-RT as standard for locally advanced disease, reserves induction mainly for larynx preservation, and recommends postoperative CRT for R1 resection or extranodal extension. Recommendations are consensus descriptors, not independently verified trial effects; linked supplements, source guideline and cited trials were not filed. Current approvals, availability and reimbursement require a current-source check

records.title: VA Larynx (Wolf)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Larynx preservation · III · 1991
records.body: Previously untreated, resectable AJCC stage III/IV glottic or supraglottic laryngeal SCC curable with laryngectomy and postoperative RT; large-volume T4 and T1 excluded Induction cisplatin 100 mg/m² plus fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m²/day for 5 days, response-directed cycle 3 then definitive RT or immediate laryngectomy plus RT for nonresponse/progression versus initial laryngectomy plus postoperative RT Primary: not explicitly stated. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free interval, relapse pattern, larynx preservation, induction response, toxicity Response-directed induction PF followed by RT preserved the larynx in 64% without a 2-year OS difference (68% in both groups) versus immediate surgery plus RT. Primary-site recurrence was more frequent with the induction strategy, while distant metastases were less frequent. This is an interim, 1991-era larynx-only study with historical imaging/RT and no extrapolation to nonlaryngeal disease; it is separate from RTOG 91-11

records.title: RTOG 91-11 (Forastiere)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Larynx preservation · III · 2003
records.body: Stage III/IV glottic or supraglottic laryngeal SCC for which surgery required total laryngectomy; curable with surgery plus postoperative RT; T1 and large-volume T4 excluded Induction cisplatin/fluorouracil then RT with response-directed laryngectomy versus concurrent cisplatin 100 mg/m² plus RT versus RT alone Primary: laryngeal preservation, laryngectomy-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free survival, local/locoregional control, distant metastasis, toxicity, speech/swallowing, cause-specific mortality Concurrent cisplatin-RT produced the greatest larynx preservation, while long-term laryngectomy-free survival did not distinguish the two chemotherapy strategies and OS did not improve. The 10-year update confirmed preservation but recorded more non-cancer deaths in the concurrent arm; late functional data have selected, shrinking denominators. Primary-endpoint definition and analysed denominator differ between the 2003 and 2013 reports; long-term comparisons are exploratory and must not be pooled
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2003;349:2091-2098   J Clin Oncol 2013;31:845-852 10-year long-term results 23182993

records.title: TAX 323 (Vermorken)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Induction (sequential) chemotherapy · III · 2007
records.body: Adults 18–70 with previously untreated, measurable, unresectable stage III/IV M0 SCCHN; WHO performance status 0–1; nasopharyngeal and nasal/paranasal sites excluded Induction TPF (docetaxel 75, cisplatin 75 mg/m² day 1; fluorouracil 750 mg/m²/day days 1–5) versus PF (cisplatin 100 mg/m²; fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m²/day days 1–5), every 3 weeks up to 4 cycles; then protocol RT Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, response after induction and RT, duration of response, time to treatment failure, toxicity, quality of life TPF improved primary PFS (HR 0.72; 11.0 vs 8.2 months) and OS (HR 0.73; 18.8 vs 14.5 months) over PF before RT, with greater response and fewer toxic deaths but more grade 3/4 neutropenia. This is unresectable-disease induction followed by RT alone; its doses and pathway differ from TAX 324, so results should not be pooled

records.title: TAX 324 (Posner)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Induction (sequential) chemotherapy · III · 2007
records.body: Previously untreated, measurable stage III/IV M0 SCC of oral cavity, larynx, oropharynx or hypopharynx; technically unresectable, low surgical curability or organ-preservation candidates; WHO performance status 0–1 Three 3-weekly induction cycles: TPF docetaxel 75 mg/m² and cisplatin 100 mg/m² day 1 plus fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m²/day days 1–4 versus PF cisplatin 100 mg/m² day 1 plus fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m²/day days 1–5; then RT 70–74 Gy with weekly carboplatin AUC 1.5 Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, induction response, toxic effects TPF improved primary OS (HR 0.70; median 71 vs 30 months) and PFS over PF before subsequent carboplatin-CRT. Induction response was not significantly different, and grade 3/4 neutropenia increased with TPF despite fewer protocol delays. This mixed unresectable/low-curability/organ-preservation population and its post-induction CRT differ from TAX 323; do not collapse the trials

records.title: EORTC 22931 (Bernier)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Postoperative (adjuvant) therapy · III · 2004
records.body: Resected stage III/IV or earlier high-risk HNSCC with positive margin, extracapsular extension or other specified risk; Bernier 2005 is a cross-trial comparative risk analysis, not a new randomised trial EORTC 22931: postoperative RT 66 Gy plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² days 1, 22 and 43 versus RT alone; 2005 analysis compared risk-factor patterns across EORTC 22931 and RTOG 9501 Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, locoregional relapse, distant metastasis, second primary tumours, acute toxicity, late toxicity, risk-factor associations Postoperative cisplatin-RT improved PFS, OS and locoregional control versus RT alone in EORTC 22931. The separate 2005 comparative analysis supports benefit concentrated in extracapsular extension and/or positive margins, but is post-hoc and cross-trial; it does not supply a new randomised estimate. Findings apply to the trial-defined high-risk postoperative population and must not be conflated with sequential adjuvant chemotherapy after completed locoregional therapy
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2004;350:1945-1952   Head Neck 2005;27:843-850 comparative EORTC/RTOG risk-stratification analysis 16161069

records.title: RTOG 9501 (Cooper)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Postoperative (adjuvant) therapy · III · 2004
records.body: Resected high-risk HNSCC with at least two positive nodes, extracapsular extension and/or microscopically involved margin; the Bernier 2005 comparison is cross-trial/post-hoc context Postoperative RT 60 Gy plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² days 1, 22 and 43 versus RT alone Primary: locoregional control. Secondary: disease-free survival, overall survival, acute and late toxicity Postoperative cisplatin-RT improved locoregional control and disease-free survival but not OS in the eligible RTOG 9501 analysis. Cross-trial Bernier 2005 findings suggest that extracapsular extension and/or positive margins—not node count alone—identify the group most likely to benefit; this is exploratory comparative context, not an RTOG randomised subgroup proof. The RTOG population included a node-count-defined group and cannot be treated as identical to EORTC 22931
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2004;350:1937-1944   Head Neck 2005;27:843-850 comparative EORTC/RTOG risk-stratification analysis 16161069

records.title: JCOG1008 (Kiyota)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Postoperative (adjuvant) therapy · II/III · 2022
records.body: Japanese patients with resected high-risk locally advanced SCCHN and positive margin and/or extranodal extension; 2026 update does not restate detailed original eligibility Postoperative RT with cisplatin 40 mg/m² weekly for 7 cycles versus cisplatin 100 mg/m² every 3 weeks for 3 cycles Primary: treatment completion, overall survival. Secondary: relapse-free survival, local relapse-free survival, nutrition support-free survival, nonhospitalised treatment duration, adverse events Weekly cisplatin remained noninferior to 3-weekly cisplatin for OS at the final analysis (HR 0.76; 5-year OS 71.2% vs 58.7%) with mature 5.6-year follow-up. Late efficacy and safety comparisons are exploratory or supplement-limited; two treatment-related deaths occurred with weekly dosing. This is a schedule comparison on the established postoperative CRT backbone, in a Japanese high-risk population, not a re-test of CRT versus RT
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1980-1990   long-term follow-up J Clin Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print, doi:10.1200/JCO-25-01708)

records.title: NIVOPOSTOP (Bourhis)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Postoperative (adjuvant) therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Adults 19–74 with completely resected, disease-free oral-cavity, oropharyngeal, laryngeal or hypopharyngeal SCC; ECOG 0–1; cisplatin-eligible; high risk by extranodal extension, positive/close margin, at least 4 nodes or multiple perineural invasions; no prior current-cancer therapy except surgery Postoperative IMRT 66 Gy/33 fractions plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² every 3 weeks for 3 cycles versus the same CRT with nivolumab 240 mg after surgery, then 360 mg every 3 weeks for 3 concurrent doses and 480 mg every 4 weeks for 6 adjuvant doses Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, central-review disease-free survival, locoregional relapse, distant relapse, second primary malignancies, safety Adding nivolumab to postoperative cisplatin-RT improved investigator-assessed DFS (HR 0.76; 3-year DFS 63.1% vs 52.5%), with an immature OS analysis. Central-review DFS was weaker and not significant, and serious and grade 4 treatment-related events increased; treatment-related deaths were unchanged. PD-L1 subgroup findings do not establish a selection rule, and the combined concurrent/adjuvant exposure prevents phase-specific attribution

records.title: RTOG 1016 (Gillison)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · HPV-positive oropharynx — de-escalation · III · 2019
records.body: Centrally p16-positive AJCC7 T1–2 N2a–3 or T3–4 N0–3 M0 oropharyngeal SCC; Zubrod 0–1 with adequate marrow, liver and renal function; suitable for definitive chemoradiation; tobacco exposure was stratified Accelerated IMRT 70 Gy/35 fractions over 6 weeks plus cetuximab 400 mg/m² loading then 250 mg/m² weekly for 7 doses versus the same IMRT plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² on days 1 and 22 Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, locoregional failure, distant metastasis, second primary tumours, early death, feeding-tube placement, dental health, toxicity, quality of life Cetuximab-RT failed the prespecified OS noninferiority test versus cisplatin-RT and had worse PFS and locoregional control. Acute, late and quality-of-life outcomes did not justify substituting cetuximab. The trial applies to p16-positive oropharyngeal disease; tobacco and other subgroup displays lack a validated predictive interaction, so cetuximab is not a de-escalation replacement for cisplatin

records.title: De-ESCALaTE (Mehanna)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · HPV-positive oropharynx — de-escalation · III · 2019
records.body: Adults with centrally p16-positive TNM7 T3–4 N0 or T1–4 N1–3 oropharyngeal SCC; non-smoker or lifetime smoking below 10 pack-years; ECOG 0–1 and fit for cisplatin-based curative chemoradiation IMRT 70 Gy/35 fractions plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² on days 1, 22 and 43 versus the same RT plus cetuximab 400 mg/m² loading then 250 mg/m² weekly for 7 infusions Primary: severe toxicity. Secondary: overall survival, recurrence, acute toxicity, late toxicity, quality of life, swallowing Cetuximab did not reduce the primary severe-toxicity endpoint, while OS and recurrence favoured cisplatin-RT. The trial was powered for toxicity rather than survival, and its survival and recurrence findings remain secondary. In this selected low-risk HPV-positive population, cetuximab is not a lower-toxicity de-escalation substitute for cisplatin

records.title: KEYNOTE-412 (Machiels)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Definitive chemoradiation + immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Adults with newly diagnosed, unresected high-risk locally advanced HNSCC, ECOG 0–1 and eligible for definitive cisplatin-CRT rather than surgery; site- and p16-specific stage criteria applied; PD-L1 was not used for selection Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 1 lead-in, 2 concurrent and 14 maintenance doses versus matched placebo, each with cisplatin-CRT: accelerated RT with 2 cisplatin 100 mg/m² doses or standard RT with 3 doses Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety, quality of life, physical functioning, swallowing, speech, pain Pembrolizumab added before, during and after definitive CRT did not meet the prespecified EFS criterion (HR 0.83); OS was immature and not different. Serious adverse events and discontinuations increased. The treatment phases are inseparable, and PD-L1 subgroup trends, including post-hoc CPS≥20, are not predictive selection evidence; this negative trial does not support adding pembrolizumab to definitive CRT outside trials

records.title: KEYNOTE-689 (Uppaluri)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Resectable disease — perioperative immunotherapy · III · 2025
records.body: Resectable stage III–IVA locally advanced HNSCC planned for surgery and risk-adapted postoperative RT with or without cisplatin Two neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg 3-weekly cycles, surgery, then 3 pembrolizumab cycles with risk-adapted postoperative RT/CRT and 12 adjuvant cycles versus surgery and risk-adapted postoperative RT/CRT alone Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: major pathological response, pathological complete response, overall survival, safety, surgical outcomes Perioperative pembrolizumab improved EFS in CPS≥10, CPS≥1 and total populations at the first interim analysis (total-population HR 0.73; 3-year EFS 57.6% vs 46.4%) without reducing surgical completion. OS was immature and not yet positive. Immune-mediated events and treatment-related deaths increased; PD-L1 findings do not establish a restrictive selection rule, and neoadjuvant/adjuvant contributions cannot be separated

records.title: EXTREME (Vermorken)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line therapy · III · 2008
records.body: Previously untreated recurrent/metastatic SCC of oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx or larynx; performance status 0–2; not candidates for curative local therapy Platinum plus fluorouracil for up to 6 cycles with cetuximab loading then weekly maintenance versus platinum plus fluorouracil alone Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, response, disease control, time to treatment failure, duration of response, safety Adding cetuximab to platinum/fluorouracil improved OS, PFS and response versus chemotherapy alone, establishing EXTREME as a historical first-line backbone. Grade 3/4 events occurred in 82% versus 76%, with 3 versus 7 treatment-related deaths; cetuximab added rash, infusion reactions and hypomagnesaemia. This pre-immunotherapy trial did not compare against PD-1 therapy, and its exploratory primary-site interaction is not predictive

records.title: KEYNOTE-048 (Burtness)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line therapy · III · 2019
records.body: Previously untreated recurrent/metastatic HNSCC not amenable to curative local therapy; CPS analyses use protocol-defined PD-L1 populations and separate 2019, 2022 and 2023 report cutoffs Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks alone or with platinum/fluorouracil for up to 6 cycles, then pembrolizumab maintenance, versus cetuximab plus platinum/fluorouracil Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: response, duration of response, safety, quality of life Pembrolizumab monotherapy improved OS in CPS≥20, while pembrolizumab-chemotherapy improved OS in CPS≥1 and the total population versus EXTREME. PFS superiority was not established in the total population, monotherapy response rates were lower, and grade≥3 treatment-related events were 17%, 71.7% and 69.3% with monotherapy, combination and EXTREME. Later reports are cutoff-specific; subsequent therapy and PD-L1 population definitions limit regimen selection
records.keywords: Lancet 2019;394:1915-1928   J Clin Oncol 2022;40:2321-2332 PD-L1 CPS subgroup analysis 35333599 J Clin Oncol 2023;41:790-802 4-yr updated results 36219809

records.title: TMC-I (Tata Memorial)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line therapy · III · 2026
records.body: India: first-line palliative, platinum-sensitive recurrent/metastatic HNSCC; filed ASCO 2026 abstract only Ultra-low-dose nivolumab 20 mg plus oral methotrexate, celecoxib and erlotinib versus paclitaxel-carboplatin Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, toxicity, quality of life The abstract reports longer OS with ultra-low-dose nivolumab plus triple oral metronomic therapy than paclitaxel-carboplatin, with fewer grade 3 or higher events. This is a one-page conference abstract: eligibility, full regimen delivery, analysis methods, safety windows, interaction tests and detailed maturity are not printed. It compares against chemotherapy alone, not pembrolizumab-chemotherapy; no full-manuscript or practice-changing inference should be made

records.title: METRO PLUS
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Single-centre North Indian adults with unresectable/recurrent oral-cavity, oropharyngeal, hypopharyngeal or laryngeal SCC selected for palliative platinum chemotherapy; prior curative therapy and prior curative platinum each required at least 6-month intervals; ECOG 0–2; 85.3% oral cavity; exact prior-platinum count unreported Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC 5 every 3 weeks for 6 cycles with erlotinib 150 mg daily, celecoxib 200 mg twice daily and methotrexate 9 mg/m² weekly continued thereafter versus paclitaxel-carboplatin alone for up to 9 cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, toxicity, quality of life Adding triple metronomic therapy to paclitaxel-carboplatin improved OS and PFS in this single-centre study; the OS proportional-hazards assumption failed, so restricted mean survival was also reported. Grade 3+ toxicity was not higher but all-grade rash, diarrhoea and mucositis increased. The chemotherapy-alone comparator, resource-limited setting and oral-cavity predominance limit inference versus PD-1-based first-line standards

records.title: KEYNOTE-B10 (Dzienis)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line therapy · IV · 2024
records.body: Previously untreated recurrent/metastatic HNSCC, any PD-L1 status, unsuitable for curative local therapy; single-arm cohort Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks with carboplatin and paclitaxel for up to 6 cycles, followed by pembrolizumab maintenance for up to 35 cycles Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety In this single-arm phase IV study, pembrolizumab plus carboplatin-paclitaxel showed an ORR of 49%, including 7% complete responses, supporting a fluorouracil-free option when 5-FU is unsuitable. Grade 3–5 treatment-related events occurred in 75%, with 3 possibly treatment-related deaths. There is no randomized comparator, treatment phases are inseparable, and no quality-of-life result was printed; comparative efficacy versus KEYNOTE-048 is unproven

records.title: CheckMate 141 (Ferris)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line & post-platinum · III · 2016
records.body: Recurrent/metastatic SCCHN progressing or recurring within 6 months of platinum; the 2018 report is an update of the same trial Nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks versus investigator’s choice methotrexate, docetaxel or cetuximab Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, duration of response, safety, quality of life Nivolumab improved OS over investigator’s choice in platinum-refractory disease at the planned interim analysis; the 2018 update confirmed durable survivors. PFS was not improved, but responses lasted longer. Grade 3/4 treatment-related events were 13.1% versus 35.1%; questionnaire-responder quality of life favoured nivolumab but was limited through week 15, and subsequent immunotherapy was imbalanced. PD-L1 and p16/HPV patterns lack predictive interaction proof; keep the 2016 and 2018 cuts distinct
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2016;375:1856-1867   Oral Oncol 2018;81:45-51 2-yr long-term survival update by PD-L1 expression 29884413

records.title: KEYNOTE-040 (Cohen)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line & post-platinum · III · 2019
records.body: Adults with incurable, measurable recurrent/metastatic oral-cavity, oropharyngeal, hypopharyngeal or laryngeal SCC progressing during/after platinum or within 3–6 months of multimodal platinum; no more than 2 prior recurrent/metastatic lines; ECOG 0–1; prior checkpoint inhibitor excluded Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for up to 24 months versus investigator’s choice methotrexate, docetaxel or cetuximab Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to progression, objective response, duration of response, safety Pembrolizumab did not meet the primary OS significance threshold in the overall population despite numerically longer median OS; its more favourable safety profile and PD-L1-associated subgroup patterns require the prespecified CPS/TPS boundaries and interaction limits. PFS and response did not establish broad superiority, and subsequent therapy/control heterogeneity limit comparison. This is a platinum-pretreated population, not first-line KEYNOTE-048 evidence

records.title: Intergroup 0099 (Al-Sarraf)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · III · 1998
records.body: Previously untreated, biopsy-proven, measurable stage III/IV M0 NPC; SWOG performance status 0-2; no prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy RT 70 Gy in 35-39 daily fractions vs the same RT plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² on days 1, 22 and 43, then cisplatin plus fluorouracil every 4 weeks for 3 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: response, treatment toxicity Concurrent-adjuvant chemoradiotherapy improved 3-year PFS (69% vs 24%) and OS (78% vs 47%) over RT alone in the eligible 147-patient analysis. The only authorised 5-year result is OS 67% vs 37% from a separate ASCO 2001 abstract, never fully published. Grade 3 leukopenia was 23/78 vs 1/68 and grade 3-4 vomiting 11/78 vs 2/68; no planned-treatment fatal toxicity occurred
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 1998;16:1310-1317   Proc Am Soc Clin Oncol 2001;20:227a (abstract 905)

records.title: MAC-NPC (Blanchard)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · N/A · 2015
records.body: Non-metastatic NPC treated with radiotherapy in individual-patient-data meta-analyses: 19 trials/4,806 patients (2015) and 28 trials/8,214 patients (2023) Chemotherapy added before, during, and/or after radiotherapy; 2015 pairwise analysis used RT alone as reference, whereas 2023 network analysis used concurrent chemoradiotherapy as reference Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, locoregional control, distant-metastasis control, acute toxicity, late toxicity Adding chemotherapy to RT improved OS; the 2015 pairwise analysis showed a 6.3% absolute 5-year benefit, confined to concomitant-containing timing subsets, while the 2023 network ranked induction plus CCRT highest against CCRT. These are historical, indirect timing comparisons, not direct regimen comparisons. Severe acute neutropenia was 25.7% vs 4.9% and late hearing deficit 20.9% vs 15.1% in availability-limited toxicity subsets
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2015;16:645-655   Lancet Oncol 2023;24:611-623 updated meta-analysis 37269842

records.title: Guangzhou-01 (Wu, oxaliplatin CCRT)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · III · 2005
records.body: Adults with ECOG 0-2 and WHO type II/III, M0, T3-4 any N and/or N2-3 any T NPC treated at a single Chinese centre Conventional RT 70-74 Gy to primary tumour and 60-64 Gy to involved neck vs the same RT plus weekly oxaliplatin 70 mg/m² for 6 cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response, safety, relapse-free survival, metastasis-free survival Oxaliplatin CCRT improved 5-year OS (73.2% vs 60.2%) and metastasis-free survival at 114-month median follow-up, while locoregional failure-free survival did not differ. Late toxicity was higher (66.1% vs 48.2%), driven by xerostomia. The 2005 and 2013 reports disagree on oxaliplatin infusion duration (2 vs 1 hour). The endemic single-centre setting, conventional RT and RT-alone comparator do not validate oxaliplatin as a cisplatin replacement
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2005;23:8461-8468 Guangzhou-01 primary report; 2-year preliminary results 16230677 Ann Oncol 2013;24:2131-2136 long-term follow-up at median 114 months; source of the col-H figures 23661293

records.title: Sun (TPF induction)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — induction chemotherapy · III · 2016
records.body: Previously untreated non-keratinising stage III-IVB NPC, excluding T3-4N0; age 18-59 years and KPS at least 70 TPF induction every 3 weeks for 3 cycles → IMRT for 6-7 weeks with cisplatin 100 mg/m² on days 1, 22 and 43 vs the same cisplatin-IMRT alone Primary: failure-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant failure-free survival, locoregional failure-free survival, response, treatment compliance, safety, quality of life TPF induction improved 3-year failure-free survival (80% vs 72%) and reduced distant failure; OS also improved, while locoregional failure-free survival did not differ. Grade 3-4 neutropenia was 42% vs 7%. Median follow-up was 45 months and late toxicity was deferred; applicability is limited to fit patients aged 18-59 with non-keratinising disease

records.title: Zhang (GP induction)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — induction chemotherapy · III · 2019
records.body: Newly diagnosed nonkeratinising stage III-IVB NPC, excluding T3-4N0; age 18-64 years and KPS at least 70 GP induction every 3 weeks for 3 cycles → IMRT plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² every 3 weeks for 3 cycles vs the same cisplatin-IMRT alone Primary: recurrence-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant recurrence-free survival, locoregional recurrence-free survival, response, treatment adherence, safety GP induction improved 3-year recurrence-free survival (85.3% vs 76.5%) and OS (94.6% vs 90.3%), chiefly through lower distant recurrence; locoregional control was unchanged. Grade 3-4 acute toxicity was 75.7% vs 55.7%, while late grade 3-4 toxicity was similar. At 42.7-month median follow-up this was not final long-term evidence, and it does not compare GP with TPF

records.title: Chen (metronomic capecitabine)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — adjuvant therapy · III · 2021
records.body: Adults aged 18-65 with ECOG 0-1 and high-risk non-keratinising stage III-IVA NPC in remission 12-16 weeks after cisplatin-IMRT, with or without induction chemotherapy; excludes T3-4N0 and T3N1 Capecitabine 650 mg/m² orally twice daily for 1 year after chemoradiotherapy vs observation; stop for unacceptable toxicity, recurrence, withdrawal or protocol discontinuation Primary: failure-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant failure-free survival, locoregional failure-free survival, safety, health-related quality of life Post-CRT metronomic capecitabine improved 3-year failure-free survival (85.3% vs 75.7%) and OS (93.3% vs 88.6%) in the high-risk remission population. Grade 3-4 adverse events were 17% vs 6%, including grade 3 hand-foot syndrome in 9%; no treatment-related deaths were reported. OS was based on 37 deaths and remained immature; the studied 1-year duration is not proven optimal

records.title: CSCO/ASCO Guideline (Chen et al.)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — adjuvant therapy · N/A · 2021
records.body: CSCO/ASCO definitive-intent guideline for AJCC 8th-edition stage II-IVA NPC, with stage-specific recommendations for T2N0, T1-2N1, T3N0 and other stage III-IVA disease Guideline: daily image-guided IMRT 70 Gy in 33-35 fractions; concurrent cisplatin 40 mg/m² weekly or 80-100 mg/m² every 3 weeks, cumulative at least 200 mg/m²; nedaplatin 100 mg/m² every 3 weeks, carboplatin AUC 5-6 every 3 weeks or oxaliplatin 70 mg/m² weekly are alternatives; stage-specific GP, TPF, PF, PX or TP induction every 3 weeks for 3 cycles (minimum 2) → CCRT or CCRT → adjuvant PF every 4 weeks for 3 cycles Primary: guideline recommendations. Secondary: survival, distant control, locoregional control, quality of life Historical 2021 guidance recommends daily image-guided IMRT 70 Gy in 33-35 fractions (high-quality, strong). For stage III-IVA except T3N0, induction plus CCRT is high-quality/strong; CCRT plus adjuvant chemotherapy if induction was not given is intermediate-quality/moderate. T2N0 chemotherapy is not routine, T1-2N1 may receive concurrent chemotherapy, and T3N0 should receive CCRT. Sequence superiority is untested. Literature ended August 2020, mostly from endemic regions; online evidence tables are unfiled

records.title: CONTINUUM (sintilimab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — adding immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Newly diagnosed high-risk, non-metastatic stage III-IVA NPC, age 18-65 years, excluding T3-4N0 and T3N1; PD-L1 status unrestricted GP induction every 3 weeks for 3 cycles → IMRT 69.96 Gy in 33 fractions with cisplatin for 2 cycles + sintilimab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 12 cycles across induction, concurrent and adjuvant phases vs the same GP-CCRT backbone without sintilimab Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant metastasis-free survival, locoregional recurrence-free survival, safety, health-related quality of life Adding sintilimab across induction, concurrent and adjuvant therapy improved 36-month event-free survival (86% vs 76%) at the source-defined final primary analysis. Distant and locoregional recurrence outcomes also favoured sintilimab, but 36-month OS was 92% in both arms and remains immature. Grade 3-4 adverse events were 74% vs 65%; 2 grade-5 immune-related deaths occurred with sintilimab and 1 grade-5 nasopharyngeal-necrosis death with standard therapy. Effects cannot be attributed to a single treatment phase

records.title: DIPPER (adjuvant camrelizumab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — adding immunotherapy · III · 2025
records.body: Chinese adults aged 18-65 with ECOG 0-1 and AJCC 8th T4N1M0 or T1-4N2-3M0 NPC after completed GP induction and cisplatin-IMRT After common GP induction every 3 weeks for 3 cycles → IMRT 69.96 Gy in 33 fractions with cisplatin for 2 cycles, camrelizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 12 cycles vs observation; 3 observation patients received adjuvant capecitabine Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: distant metastasis-free survival, locoregional relapse-free survival, overall survival, safety, health-related quality of life Adjuvant camrelizumab improved 3-year event-free survival (86.9% vs 77.3%) after completed GP induction and cisplatin-IMRT; distant metastasis-free and locoregional relapse-free survival also favoured camrelizumab, while OS remained immature with no demonstrated difference. Grade 3-4 adverse events were 11.2% vs 3.2%; 1 grade-5 death occurred per arm, without camrelizumab causality assigned. 3 observation patients received capecitabine, and optimal PD-1 sequencing remains uncertain

records.title: Zhang (GP vs FP)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — first-line chemotherapy · III · 2016
records.body: Adults with ECOG 0-1 and measurable recurrent NPC not amenable to local treatment or de novo metastatic stage IVC NPC; no systemic chemotherapy for recurrent/metastatic disease; Chinese cohort; prior curative therapy permitted if completed at least 6 months earlier Gemcitabine 1 g/m² days 1 and 8 plus cisplatin 80 mg/m² day 1 every 3 weeks vs fluorouracil 4 g/m² continuous infusion over 96 hours plus cisplatin 80 mg/m² day 1 every 3 weeks; both for up to 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, disease control, safety GP improved median PFS (7.0 vs 5.6 months) and objective response (64% vs 42%) versus FP in a Chinese cohort mixing recurrent and primary metastatic disease. Myelosuppression was more common with GP, whereas mucositis was less common; no treatment-related deaths were reported. OS was preliminary and immature. The historical FP comparator establishes a chemotherapy backbone, not a comparison with modern immunotherapy

records.title: JUPITER-02 (toripalimab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Adults aged 18-75 with untreated recurrent or de novo metastatic NPC not amenable to curative local therapy and no prior systemic chemotherapy in the recurrent/metastatic setting; Asian cohort Toripalimab 240 mg every 3 weeks or placebo plus GP for up to 6 cycles, then assigned maintenance every 3 weeks until progression, toxicity, withdrawal or 2 years Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, disease control, safety Toripalimab added during GP and continued as maintenance improved OS at 36-month median follow-up: 3-year OS was 64.5% vs 49.2%, with median OS not reached vs 33.7 months. Final median PFS was 21.4 vs 8.2 months but descriptive after the positive 2021 interim. Grade 3 or higher immune-related events were 9.6% vs 1.4%; fatal TEAEs were 3.4% vs 2.8%. The reports use different cutoffs, and Methods specify every 3 weeks while the Reporting Summary says every 2 weeks. All patients were Asian; chemotherapy-phase and maintenance effects cannot be separated

records.title: CAPTAIN-1st (camrelizumab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Adults aged 18-75 with ECOG 0-1 and untreated recurrent or de novo metastatic NPC not amenable to local treatment; all enrolled patients had distant metastases at Chinese centres Camrelizumab 200 mg IV or placebo plus gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 and cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV day 1 every 3 weeks for 4-6 cycles, then assigned treatment every 3 weeks until progression, unacceptable toxicity, new anticancer therapy, investigator decision, withdrawal or 2 years Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, disease control, duration of response, safety Long-term OS favoured camrelizumab added during GP and continued as maintenance: at 63.4-month median follow-up, median OS was 34.5 vs 26.6 months and 5-year OS 37.8% vs 24.2%. This 5-year analysis was post hoc after unblinding and unequal subsequent treatment; primary PFS had improved in the 2021 report. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related events were 93% vs 90%, treatment-component-related deaths 5 vs 1 and grade 3 or higher immune-related events 15% with camrelizumab. Treatment-phase contributions are inseparable
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2021;22:1162-1174   JAMA Oncol 2026;12:295-302 5-year OS analysis 41609753

records.title: RATIONALE-309 (tislelizumab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Asian adults aged 18-75 with ECOG 0-1, measurable treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC; locally recurrent disease amenable to curative treatment was excluded, and prior curative therapy required at least a 6-month treatment-free interval Tislelizumab 200 mg IV or placebo plus gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 and cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV day 1 every 3 weeks for 4-6 cycles, then assigned monotherapy until IRC progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal; protocol-eligible placebo patients could cross over to tislelizumab after progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, disease control, progression-free survival 2, safety, quality of life Tislelizumab added during GP and continued as maintenance improved median PFS (9.2 vs 7.4 months) at the prespecified interim analysis. Updated PFS2 also favoured tislelizumab, while OS was immature and limited by 49% placebo-to-tislelizumab crossover. Grade 3 or higher immune-mediated events were 2.3%; TEAEs leading to death occurred in 5 vs 2 patients, including 2 treatment-component-related deaths in each arm. The predominantly nonkeratinising Asian cohort and inseparable treatment phases limit generalisation; exploratory subgroup findings do not establish a predictive biomarker

records.title: Penpulimab (AK105-304)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2026
records.body: Adults aged 18-75 with untreated recurrent or metastatic NPC, including de novo metastatic disease unsuitable for local management Penpulimab 200 mg IV or placebo plus gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 and cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV or carboplatin AUC5 day 1 every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles, then assigned treatment every 3 weeks to no clinical benefit, intolerable toxicity, withdrawal or 24 months; placebo could switch after BICR progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, disease control, safety, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity, quality of life Penpulimab added during chemotherapy and continued as maintenance improved blinded-review median PFS (9.63 vs 7.00 months) at the prespecified interim analysis. OS was immature (HR 0.94) and placebo-to-penpulimab crossover limits later attribution. Grade 3 or higher immune-related events were 4.1%, with 2 treatment-related deaths. Most participants were Asian; treatment phases are inseparable, and PD-L1/EBV findings do not select treatment

records.title: Liu et al.
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — maintenance therapy · III · 2022
records.body: Adults aged 18-65 with newly diagnosed metastatic NPC and IRC-confirmed disease control after 4-6 TPC induction cycles; randomised 8-12 weeks after induction at a single Chinese centre Capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² orally twice daily on days 1-14 every 3 weeks plus best supportive care vs best supportive care; capecitabine for up to 2 years or until progression, toxicity, death or withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response, duration of response, overall survival, adverse events Among induction responders, capecitabine maintenance improved median PFS from randomisation (35.9 vs 8.2 months) and objective response. OS was immature and statistical significance was not reached. Grade 3-4 toxicities included anemia and hand-foot syndrome, with no treatment-related death. This single-centre, age-limited maintenance-randomisation population starts PFS after induction disease control

records.title: Yang (izalontamab brengitecan)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — second-line & beyond · III · 2025
records.body: Chinese adults aged 18-75 with ECOG 0-1 and measurable recurrent/metastatic NPC progressing after at least 2 systemic chemotherapy lines including platinum and PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition Izalontamab brengitecan 2.5 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks vs capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1-14, gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 or docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks; stop at progression, intolerable toxicity, withdrawal, delay over 28 days, new anticancer therapy or death Primary: objective response, overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, duration of response, disease control, safety, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity, quality of life At the final ORR analysis, izalontamab brengitecan improved blinded-review response (54.6% vs 27.0%) and PFS (8.38 vs 4.34 months) versus heterogeneous physician-choice chemotherapy. Co-primary OS was immature, with no estimate printed. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related events were 80% vs 62%, including more anemia and thrombocytopenia, and 4 treatment-related deaths occurred with izalontamab brengitecan. Results apply to a heavily pretreated post-PD-1 Chinese population and do not establish survival or predictive-biomarker benefit

records.title: Chong (pembrolizumab ± bevacizumab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — second-line & beyond · II · 2025
records.body: Adults aged at least 21 with EBER-positive, platinum-resistant, checkpoint-inhibitor-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC, ECOG 0-1, evaluable disease and a repeat-biopsy-amenable lesion at 2 Singapore hospitals Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks with or without bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg given 1 week before each pembrolizumab dose; continue to progression, toxicity or 32 cycles Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, duration of response, safety In this 48-patient randomised phase 2 study, bevacizumab plus pembrolizumab improved objective response (58.3% vs 12.5%); median PFS was 13.8 vs 1.6 months as a secondary result. OS was post hoc and confounded by crossover and unequal subsequent therapy. Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events were 29% vs 8%; grade 3 thrombosis or bleeding occurred in 4/24 with bevacizumab, including carotid blowout. Phase 3 confirmation is needed

records.title: RTOG-MRC Neutron (Laramore)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Locoregional — radiotherapy (adenoid cystic carcinoma) · N/A · 1993
records.body: Inoperable or recurrent adenoid cystic carcinoma of major/minor salivary glands Fast-neutron radiotherapy vs photon/mixed-beam radiotherapy Locoregional control Neutrons improved 10-yr locoregional control (56% vs 25%) but not survival (dominated by distant metastasis); historical basis for neutron RT in unresectable ACC.
records.keywords: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 1993;27:235-240

records.title: ASCO Guideline (Geiger et al.)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Locoregional — radiotherapy (adenoid cystic carcinoma) · N/A · 2021
records.body: Salivary gland malignancy, all histologies and stages N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A First formal evidence-based ASCO guideline for salivary gland malignancy (SGM), covering preoperative workup, surgery, radiotherapy, systemic therapy, follow-up, and recurrent/metastatic disease. Surgical excision is the mainstay of curative treatment; postoperative RT is recommended for all resected adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) and for high-grade tumors, positive margins, perineural/lymphovascular invasion, nodal metastases, or T3-T4 disease. Concurrent chemoradiation is not routinely recommended outside a clinical trial. In the recurrent/metastatic setting, targeted therapy should be guided by molecular alterations: multitargeted TKIs (lenvatinib, sorafenib) for ACC; NTRK inhibitors for NTRK-fusion secretory carcinoma; HER2-directed therapy for HER2-positive salivary duct carcinoma; and androgen deprivation for AR-positive disease. Checkpoint inhibitors are not routinely recommended except for high-TMB or MSI-H tumors. This guideline provides the evidentiary/decision framework underlying the targeted-therapy trials (lenvatinib, axitinib, trastuzumab, larotrectinib, androgen blockade) already filed on this sheet.

records.title: Lenvatinib (Tchekmedyian)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Adenoid cystic carcinoma — antiangiogenic TKIs · II · 2019
records.body: Progressive recurrent/metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma Single-arm lenvatinib 24 mg daily Objective response rate ORR 15.6% (all partial) with 75% stable disease and median PFS 17.5 months; met its primary endpoint, showing meaningful TKI activity in ACC.

records.title: Axitinib (Kang)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Adenoid cystic carcinoma — antiangiogenic TKIs · II · 2021
records.body: Progressive recurrent/metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma Axitinib 5 mg twice daily vs observation 6-month progression-free survival Axitinib improved 6-mo PFS (73.2% vs 23.2%) and median PFS (10.8 vs 2.8 months); first randomized evidence of TKI benefit in ACC.

records.title: Takahashi (trastuzumab + docetaxel)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Salivary duct / HER2-positive — HER2-directed therapy · II · 2019
records.body: HER2-positive locally advanced/recurrent or metastatic salivary duct carcinoma Single-arm trastuzumab + docetaxel Objective response rate ORR 70.2% with median PFS 8.9 months and OS 39.7 months; established HER2-directed therapy for salivary duct carcinoma.

records.title: MYTHOS (trastuzumab deruxtecan)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Salivary duct / HER2-positive — HER2-directed therapy · II · 2024
records.body: HER2-expressing recurrent/metastatic salivary gland carcinoma Single-arm trastuzumab deruxtecan Objective response rate ORR 68.4% by independent review with median PFS 15.9 months; supports the HER2 antibody-drug conjugate in HER2-positive salivary cancer.

records.title: Limaye (trastuzumab in SDC)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Salivary duct / HER2-positive — HER2-directed therapy · N/A · 2013
records.body: HER2-positive (IHC 1-3+) salivary duct carcinoma, adjuvant or palliative setting Trastuzumab + paclitaxel/carboplatin (TCH), adjuvant (n=8) or palliative (n=5) Retrospective outcome review 62% of adjuvant patients disease-free beyond 2 years; all 5 metastatic patients responded to TCH (1 complete response, ongoing at 52 months); median response duration 18 months — early evidence supporting routine HER2 testing and trastuzumab-based therapy in SDC.

records.title: EORTC 1206 (Locati)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Androgen receptor-positive — androgen blockade · II · 2024
records.body: Recurrent/metastatic androgen receptor-positive salivary gland cancer (chemo-naive) Androgen deprivation (triptorelin + bicalutamide) vs chemotherapy Progression-free survival ADT was neither superior nor inferior to chemotherapy (median PFS 4.0 vs 6.5 months; ORR 23% vs 35%) but was far less toxic, supporting ADT as a tolerable option in AR-positive disease.

records.title: Larotrectinib (salivary cohort)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · TRK fusion (secretory carcinoma) — TRK inhibition · II · 2024
records.body: TRK fusion-positive (ETV6-NTRK3) salivary gland cancers, mostly secretory carcinoma Single-arm larotrectinib 100 mg twice daily, continuous 28-day cycles, to progression (pooled phase I/II) Objective response rate ORR 92% (13% complete) with durable responses; TRK inhibition is highly active where an NTRK fusion is present.

records.title: ASCO Guideline (Saba et al.)
records.subtitle: Thyroid Cancer · Thyroid carcinoma · N/A · 2026
records.body: Thyroid carcinoma (differentiated, medullary, anaplastic), adults N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A ASCO guideline on systemic therapy across thyroid cancer subtypes (well-differentiated, differentiated high-grade/poorly differentiated, anaplastic, medullary). Primary treatment of well-differentiated disease is surgery ± radioactive iodine (RAI); for RAI-refractory well-differentiated disease, lenvatinib is the preferred first-line multikinase inhibitor (SELECT — PFS benefit; ORR ~65% vs 1.5% placebo), with sorafenib an alternative (DECISION). Biomarker-directed options for BRAF V600E, RET mutation/fusion, and NTRK fusion. Distinct systemic strategies outlined for medullary and anaplastic subtypes.

records.title: Dabrafenib + trametinib (Gao)
records.subtitle: Thyroid Cancer · Thyroid carcinoma · III · 2026
records.body: Adults with locally advanced or metastatic radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer, centrally confirmed BRAF V600E, progressing after one or two previous VEGFR-targeted therapies; ECOG 0-2. Entry allowed any differentiated histology; all 153 enrolled had papillary carcinoma, 86% Asian, 50% from mainland China Dabrafenib 150 mg orally twice daily + trametinib 2 mg orally once daily until progression vs matching placebos (2:1; crossover to open-label dabrafenib + trametinib on centrally confirmed progression) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall response rate, overall survival, duration of response, safety, serous retinopathy In BRAF V600E-mutant papillary thyroid cancer progressing after VEGFR-targeted therapy, dabrafenib plus trametinib markedly prolonged progression-free survival: median 12.8 against 3.7 months with placebo (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.25-0.57, p<0.0001), response 57% against 4% (p<0.0001), disease control 88% against 63%. Overall survival at this interim analysis did not reach statistical significance - median not reached against 25.9 months, HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.36-1.19), p=0.083 - with 58% of the placebo arm crossing over after progression. Toxicity was near-universal in both arms (any adverse event 98% against 90%): pyrexia 48%, anaemia 45%, serious adverse events 43% against 25%, pneumonia the commonest grade 3 or worse event at 8%, serous retinopathy 7% against none, and one treatment-related death from cerebrovascular accident.

records.title: EORTC 18071
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2015
records.body: Completely resected high-risk stage III cutaneous melanoma Adjuvant ipilimumab 10 mg/kg vs placebo Recurrence-free survival (OS co-primary) Adjuvant ipilimumab improved RFS and OS (5-yr OS 65.4% vs 54.4%, HR 0.72) but caused grade 3-4 immune toxicity in ~54% and 5 treatment-related deaths; proof-of-concept for adjuvant checkpoint blockade, later supplanted by anti–PD-1.

records.title: COMBI-AD
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2017
records.body: Resected stage III BRAF V600E/K-mutant melanoma Adjuvant dabrafenib + trametinib (12 mo) vs placebo Relapse-free survival Dabrafenib plus trametinib lowered recurrence (3-yr RFS 58% vs 39%, HR 0.47); established adjuvant BRAF/MEK-targeted therapy as an option for resected BRAF-mutant stage III disease.

records.title: CheckMate 238
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2017
records.body: Resected stage IIIB/C or IV melanoma Adjuvant nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W vs ipilimumab 10 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses then Q12W; both up to 1 year, to recurrence or toxicity Recurrence-free survival Nivolumab improved RFS over ipilimumab (12-mo RFS 70.5% vs 60.8%, HR 0.65) with far less grade 3-4 toxicity (14% vs 46%); established anti–PD-1 over ipilimumab in the adjuvant setting.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2017;377:1824-1835   N Engl J Med 2026;394:333-342 9-yr final analysis 41124198

records.title: KEYNOTE-054 (EORTC 1325)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2018
records.body: Completely resected high-risk stage III melanoma Adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×18 doses (~1 year) vs placebo; to recurrence or toxicity Recurrence-free survival Pembrolizumab improved RFS versus placebo (1-yr RFS 75.4% vs 61.0%, HR 0.57) across subgroups including BRAF wild-type; a standard adjuvant option regardless of BRAF status.

records.title: KEYNOTE-716
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2022
records.body: Resected stage IIB/IIC melanoma, sentinel-node negative Adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×17 cycles (~1 year) vs placebo; to recurrence or toxicity Recurrence-free survival Pembrolizumab improved RFS versus placebo (HR 0.65) and distant metastasis-free survival (HR 0.64); extended adjuvant anti–PD-1 to high-risk node-negative stage II disease.

records.title: CheckMate 76K
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2023
records.body: Resected stage IIB/IIC melanoma, sentinel-node negative Adjuvant nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W vs placebo; to 12 months, recurrence, or toxicity Recurrence-free survival Nivolumab reduced recurrence versus placebo (12-mo RFS 89.0% vs 79.4%, HR 0.42) and improved DMFS (HR 0.47); a second adjuvant anti–PD-1 option for stage II melanoma.

records.title: SWOG S1801
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · II · 2023
records.body: Resectable stage IIIB-IV cutaneous melanoma Neoadjuvant + adjuvant pembrolizumab vs adjuvant-only pembrolizumab Event-free survival Giving 3 doses of pembrolizumab before surgery improved EFS versus the same drug given only after surgery (2-yr EFS 72% vs 49%, HR 0.58); demonstrated the value of neoadjuvant immunotherapy sequencing.

records.title: NADINA
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2024
records.body: Resectable macroscopic stage III melanoma Neoadjuvant ipilimumab 80 mg + nivolumab 240 mg IV Q3W ×2 cycles → therapeutic lymph-node dissection, then response-driven adjuvant (major pathological response → no adjuvant; partial response/non-response → dabrafenib + trametinib if BRAF-mutant or nivolumab 480 mg Q4W if BRAF wild-type) vs upfront lymph-node dissection → adjuvant nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W ×12 cycles Event-free survival Two cycles of neoadjuvant ipilimumab + nivolumab then response-driven adjuvant therapy beat adjuvant nivolumab (12-mo EFS 83.7% vs 57.2%, HR 0.32); ~59% had a major pathologic response and skipped adjuvant therapy, establishing neoadjuvant dual checkpoint blockade as a standard for macroscopic stage III.

records.title: KEYNOTE-942 (mRNA-4157/V940)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · II · 2024
records.body: Resected high-risk stage IIIB-IV cutaneous melanoma Intismeran autogene (individualized neoantigen mRNA vaccine) + pembrolizumab vs pembrolizumab Recurrence-free survival Adding the personalized mRNA neoantigen vaccine to adjuvant pembrolizumab prolonged RFS (18-mo RFS 79% vs 62%, HR 0.56), with benefit sustained at 3- and 5-year follow-up (~49% reduction in recurrence or death); first randomized signal for an individualized cancer vaccine, with phase 3 confirmation (V940-001) ongoing.

records.title: BRIM-3
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — BRAF / MEK-targeted therapy · III · 2011
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600E-mutant unresectable/metastatic melanoma Vemurafenib vs dacarbazine Overall survival and progression-free survival Vemurafenib reduced the risk of death by 63% (HR 0.37) and prolonged PFS (5.3 vs 1.6 months) versus dacarbazine; first targeted therapy to improve survival in melanoma and validated BRAF as a drug target.

records.title: coBRIM
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — BRAF / MEK-targeted therapy · III · 2014
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600-mutant advanced melanoma Vemurafenib + cobimetinib vs vemurafenib Progression-free survival Adding the MEK inhibitor cobimetinib improved PFS (9.9 vs 6.2 months, HR 0.51) and response rate; established combined BRAF + MEK inhibition over BRAF inhibition alone.

records.title: COMBI-v
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — BRAF / MEK-targeted therapy · III · 2015
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma Dabrafenib + trametinib vs vemurafenib Overall survival The dabrafenib/trametinib doublet improved OS over vemurafenib (12-mo OS 72% vs 65%, HR 0.69) and PFS (11.4 vs 7.3 months); confirmed BRAF/MEK combination as a first-line targeted standard.

records.title: COLUMBUS
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — BRAF / MEK-targeted therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated/1 prior line BRAF V600-mutant advanced melanoma Encorafenib + binimetinib vs vemurafenib (vs encorafenib) Progression-free survival Encorafenib + binimetinib improved PFS versus vemurafenib (14.9 vs 7.3 months, HR 0.54) with favorable tolerability; a third BRAF/MEK doublet standard.

records.title: DREAMseq (EA6134)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — BRAF / MEK-targeted therapy · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma Arm A→C: nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W to 72 weeks, then dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily + trametinib 2 mg once daily at progression vs Arm B→D: dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily + trametinib 2 mg once daily to progression → nivolumab + ipilimumab at progression 2-year overall survival Starting with nivolumab/ipilimumab and switching to dabrafenib/trametinib at progression gave higher 2-year overall survival than the reverse sequence (71.8%, 95% CI 62.5-79.1, vs 51.5%, 95% CI 41.7-60.4; log-rank P=.010 on Kaplan-Meier estimates). The protocol-specified primary comparison - a Mantel-Haenszel test of 2-year landmark rates among the 176 patients followed at least 2 years - did not cross its efficacy boundary (P=.163); the trial was stopped early on the DSMC's recommendation after the Kaplan-Meier analysis crossed the O'Brien-Fleming boundary at 59% information time, with the 95% repeated CI for the difference 2.6% to 37.9%. Established immunotherapy-first sequencing for BRAF V600-mutant disease.

records.title: MDX010-20 (ipilimumab)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · III · 2010
records.body: Previously treated HLA-A*0201+ metastatic melanoma Ipilimumab ± gp100 vaccine vs gp100 vaccine Overall survival Ipilimumab improved OS versus vaccine alone (median 10.0 vs 6.4 months, HR ~0.66); first agent ever to improve survival in advanced melanoma and validated CTLA-4 blockade.

records.title: KEYNOTE-006
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · III · 2015
records.body: Advanced melanoma, ≤1 prior therapy (ipilimumab-naive) Pembrolizumab (Q2W or Q3W) vs ipilimumab Progression-free and overall survival Pembrolizumab improved OS (HR 0.63-0.69; 1-yr OS ~74% vs 58%) and PFS versus ipilimumab with less high-grade toxicity; established anti–PD-1 monotherapy as first-line over ipilimumab.

records.title: CheckMate 067
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · III · 2015
records.body: Untreated advanced melanoma Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W vs nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W vs ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses; all to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival and ORR Nivolumab + ipilimumab and nivolumab alone improved PFS (11.5 and 6.9 vs 2.9 months) and ORR (58% and 44% vs 19%) over ipilimumab, with durable long-term survival on extended follow-up; established first-line dual checkpoint blockade.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2015;373:23-34   N Engl J Med 2017;377:1345-1356 overall survival 28889792

records.title: RELATIVITY-047
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · II/III · 2022
records.body: Untreated metastatic/unresectable melanoma Nivolumab + relatlimab (anti–LAG-3) fixed-dose vs nivolumab Progression-free survival Adding the LAG-3 inhibitor relatlimab improved PFS over nivolumab alone (median 10.1 vs 4.6 months, HR 0.75); established LAG-3 + PD-1 blockade as a first-line option with lower toxicity than nivolumab/ipilimumab.

records.title: OPTiM (T-VEC)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · III · 2015
records.body: Unresectable stage IIIB-IV melanoma Intralesional talimogene laherparepvec vs subcutaneous GM-CSF Durable response rate T-VEC improved durable response rate (16% vs 2%) and ORR (26% vs 6%) versus GM-CSF; first oncolytic immunotherapy approved for melanoma, useful for injectable locoregional disease.

records.title: C-144-01 (lifileucel)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · II · 2025
records.body: Advanced melanoma refractory to anti–PD-1 (and BRAF/MEK if indicated) (single-arm) One-time lifileucel autologous TIL infusion (1×10⁹–150×10⁹ cells) after nonmyeloablative lymphodepletion (cyclophosphamide + fludarabine), then high-dose IL-2 (≤6 doses) Objective response rate Lifileucel produced an ORR of 31.4% with median duration of response 36.5 months in checkpoint-refractory melanoma; first FDA-approved cellular (TIL) therapy for a solid tumor.

records.title: Rohaan (TIL vs ipilimumab)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · III · 2022
records.body: Unresectable stage IIIC/IV melanoma, 86% refractory to anti-PD-1 therapy TIL therapy: nonmyeloablative lymphodepletion (cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg/day IV ×2 days + fludarabine 25 mg/m²/day IV ×5 days) → single adoptive transfer of ≥5×10⁹ TILs → high-dose IL-2 600,000 IU/kg IV Q8H (max 15 doses) vs ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses PFS Median PFS 7.2 vs 3.1 months (HR 0.50); ORR 49% vs 21%; median OS 25.8 vs 18.9 months; first phase III trial establishing TIL therapy's benefit over standard checkpoint immunotherapy.

records.title: IGNYTE (RP1)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · II · 2025
records.body: Unresectable stage IIIB-IV cutaneous melanoma with confirmed progression while on ≥8 weeks of anti–PD-1 as the last prior therapy, given alone or combined with another anticancer agent and including adjuvant anti–PD-1; measurable disease plus an injectable lesion ≥1 cm required; prior oncolytic therapy or serious complications from checkpoint therapy excluded (single-arm) RP1 (vusolimogene oderparepvec) intratumorally 1 × 10⁶ PFU/mL then up to 7 further doses at 1 × 10⁷ PFU/mL Q2W (more allowed; ≤10 mL/dose) + nivolumab 240 mg Q2W from RP1 dose 2 ×8 cycles → 480 mg Q4W ×≤21 cycles (≤2 years) Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, complete response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety A third of anti-PD-1-failed melanomas responded to intratumoural RP1 with nivolumab (single-arm): the primary objective response rate by modified RECIST was 33.6% (95% CI 25.8-42.0) against a design null of below 15%, though no test result is reported; by conventional RECIST, response was 32.9% (25.2-41.3) with complete response in 15.0%. Responses were deep and durable - median duration 33.7 months (95% CI 14.1-not reached), 69.5% ongoing at 1 year - and noninjected lesions regressed nearly as often as injected. Median progression-free survival was only 3.6 months (2.0-5.0); overall survival 75.3% at 1 year and 63.3% at 2 years, median not reached. Treatment-related adverse events were 90.0% any-grade - commonest fatigue 32.9%, chills 32.1%, pyrexia 30.7%, almost all grade 1-2 - but 12.9% grade 3-4, with five grade 4 events including myocarditis and splenic rupture, and no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: IMCgp100-202 (tebentafusp)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Uveal & mucosal melanoma · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated HLA-A*02:01+ metastatic uveal melanoma Tebentafusp (gp100×CD3 ImmTAC) vs investigator's choice (pembrolizumab/ipilimumab/dacarbazine) Overall survival Tebentafusp improved OS versus investigator's choice (median 21.7 vs 16.0 months, HR 0.51) despite low response rates; first therapy to improve survival in metastatic uveal melanoma.

records.title: OptimUM-02
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Uveal & mucosal melanoma · II/III · 2026
records.body: First-line HLA-A*02:01-negative metastatic uveal melanoma Darovasertib (PKC inhibitor) + crizotinib vs investigator's choice (pembrolizumab, ipilimumab+nivolumab, or dacarbazine), 2:1 Progression-free survival Darovasertib plus crizotinib improved progression-free survival over investigator's choice (median 6.9 versus 3.1 months; HR 0.42, p<.0001) with objective response 37.1% versus 5.8% - the first randomised win in HLA-A2-negative metastatic uveal melanoma, the population tebentafusp cannot treat. These are the phase 2 efficacy primary results of a nested phase 2/3 trial; overall survival is the phase 3 primary endpoint and has not been reported. ASCO 2026 LBA9503 - a conference abstract, not yet a full publication.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2026;44(suppl 17):LBA9503   Orloff et al. - 2026 - Darovasertib plus crizotinib vs investigator's choice as first-line treatment for HLA-A2 negative [1126b8da]

records.title: Sheng et al (toripalimab + axitinib)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Uveal & mucosal melanoma · I · 2019
records.body: Treatment-naive metastatic mucosal melanoma Toripalimab (anti–PD-1) + axitinib Safety and objective response Toripalimab + axitinib achieved an ORR of 48.3% with median PFS 7.5 months in treatment-naive mucosal melanoma, a subtype largely resistant to single-agent checkpoint blockade; key early evidence for IO + VEGF-TKI in mucosal disease.

records.title: SECOMBIT (Ascierto)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — sequencing of targeted therapy & immunotherapy · II · 2023
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma Arm A: encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily to progression → ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W; Arm B: ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W to progression → encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily; Arm C: encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily ×8 weeks → ipilimumab + nivolumab to progression → encorafenib + binimetinib 2-year OS 2-year/3-year OS 65%/54% (A), 73%/62% (B), 69%/60% (C); all arms exceeded the prespecified OS threshold; immunotherapy-first and sandwich sequencing trended better than targeted-therapy-first.

records.title: EBIN (Robert)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — sequencing of targeted therapy & immunotherapy · II · 2025
records.body: Untreated, unresectable stage III/IV melanoma with BRAF V600E/K mutations Induction: encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily ×12 weeks → nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W to progression, toxicity, or 2 years vs no induction: nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W to progression, toxicity, or 2 years PFS No PFS benefit from targeted-therapy induction before checkpoint inhibition (median PFS 9 vs 9 months, HR 0.87); more grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs with induction (42% vs 32%) — does not support induction sequencing.

records.title: Stupp (EORTC-NCIC 26981-22981)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · III · 2005
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, age ≤70, WHO PS 0-2 RT 60 Gy in 30 fractions + concurrent oral temozolomide 75 mg/m²/day throughout RT (max 49 days), then after a 4-week break six cycles of adjuvant temozolomide 150→200 mg/m² days 1–5 Q4W vs RT alone (60 Gy in 30 fractions) Overall survival Temozolomide added to RT improved median OS (14.6 vs 12.1 months, HR 0.63) and 2-yr OS (26.5% vs 10.4%), with benefit greatest in MGMT-methylated tumors; established the 'Stupp regimen' as standard of care.

records.title: AVAglio (Chinot)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · III · 2014
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma after surgery RT/temozolomide + bevacizumab vs RT/temozolomide + placebo Progression-free and overall survival (co-primary) Met one co-primary and missed the other: PFS 10.6 vs 6.2 months (stratified HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.55–0.74, p<0.001 against a prespecified alpha of 0.01) but OS 16.8 vs 16.7 months (HR 0.88, 0.76–1.02, p=0.10 against 0.04). Deterioration-free survival was longer on all five prespecified quality-of-life scales and on Karnofsky performance status, and among patients taking glucocorticoids at baseline these were discontinued in 66.3% vs 47.1% — all nominal, since no alpha sits below the two co-primaries. Grade ≥3 adverse events often associated with bevacizumab occurred in 32.5% vs 15.8%. The authors conclude a 4.4-month PFS gain “with quality of life and functional status maintained” at the cost of more adverse events; they do not conclude there is no role. The trial did not establish a survival benefit, and bevacizumab is not standard first-line.

records.title: RTOG 0825 (Gilbert)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · III · 2014
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma after surgery RT/temozolomide + bevacizumab vs RT/temozolomide + placebo Progression-free and overall survival (co-primary) Upfront bevacizumab did not improve OS (15.7 vs 16.1 months, HR 1.13) and the PFS gain (10.7 vs 7.3 months) missed the prespecified threshold, with more cognitive/QoL decline; reserved for symptomatic recurrence.

records.title: EF-14 (Stupp)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · III · 2017
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma after completing chemoradiation Tumor-treating fields + maintenance temozolomide vs maintenance temozolomide alone Progression-free survival Adding TTFields improved median OS (20.9 vs 16.0 months, HR 0.63) and PFS (6.7 vs 4.0 months); established TTFields as an option added to maintenance temozolomide.

records.title: CeTeG/NOA-09 (Herrlinger)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · III · 2019
records.body: Newly diagnosed MGMT-methylated glioblastoma, age 18-70 Lomustine + temozolomide vs temozolomide (both with RT) Overall survival Lomustine-temozolomide improved median OS (48.1 vs 31.4 months, HR 0.60) in this small trial; an intensified option for fit MGMT-methylated patients.

records.title: Keime-Guibert
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · III · 2007
records.body: Glioblastoma/anaplastic astrocytoma, age ≥70, KPS ≥70 Radiotherapy (50 Gy) + supportive care vs supportive care alone Overall survival RT prolonged median OS (29.1 vs 16.9 weeks, HR 0.47) without worsening QoL or cognition; confirmed a survival benefit of RT in fit elderly patients.

records.title: Roa
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · III · 2004
records.body: Glioblastoma, age ≥60, KPS ≥50 Short-course RT (40 Gy/15) vs standard RT (60 Gy/30) Overall survival Abbreviated RT gave equivalent median OS (5.6 vs 5.1 months) with less steroid use; established hypofractionated RT as standard for older patients.

records.title: NOA-08 (Wick)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · III · 2012
records.body: Anaplastic astrocytoma/glioblastoma, age >65, KPS ≥60 Dose-dense temozolomide alone vs radiotherapy alone Overall survival (noninferiority) Temozolomide was noninferior to RT (median OS 8.6 vs 9.6 months; EFS 3.3 vs 4.7 months); MGMT methylation predicted benefit from temozolomide, supporting biomarker-guided monotherapy.

records.title: Nordic (Malmström)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · III · 2012
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, age >60 Temozolomide vs hypofractionated RT (34 Gy/10) vs standard RT (60 Gy/30) Overall survival Temozolomide (median OS 8.3 months) and hypofractionated RT (7.5 months) outperformed standard RT (6.0 months), especially in patients >70; temozolomide benefit confined to MGMT-methylated tumors.

records.title: CCTG CE.6 (Perry)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · III · 2017
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, age ≥65 Short-course RT (40 Gy/15) + concurrent/adjuvant temozolomide vs short-course RT alone Overall survival Adding temozolomide to short-course RT improved median OS (9.3 vs 7.6 months, HR 0.67), with greatest benefit in MGMT-methylated tumors (13.5 vs 7.7 months); established hypofractionated RT + temozolomide for fit elderly patients.

records.title: EORTC 26101 (Wick)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Recurrent glioblastoma · III · 2017
records.body: Glioblastoma at first progression after chemoradiation Lomustine + bevacizumab vs lomustine alone Overall survival Adding bevacizumab prolonged PFS (4.2 vs 1.5 months) but not OS (9.1 vs 8.6 months, HR 0.95); no survival role for the combination at recurrence.

records.title: REGOMA (Lombardi)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Recurrent glioblastoma · II · 2019
records.body: Glioblastoma at first relapse after surgery and Stupp chemoradiation Regorafenib vs lomustine Overall survival Regorafenib improved median OS (7.4 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.50); a signal supporting regorafenib as a recurrence option pending phase 3 confirmation.

records.title: EORTC 22845 (van den Bent)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · III · 2005
records.body: Adult grade 2 astrocytoma/oligodendroglioma after surgery Early postoperative RT (54 Gy) vs RT deferred until progression Overall and progression-free survival Early RT lengthened PFS (5.3 vs 3.4 years, HR 0.59) but not OS (7.4 vs 7.2 years); supported deferring RT in selected low-risk patients.

records.title: RTOG 9802 (Buckner)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · III · 2016
records.body: High-risk (age ≥40, or <40 with subtotal resection) grade 2 glioma RT + PCV (procarbazine/lomustine/vincristine) vs RT alone Overall survival Adding PCV to RT improved median OS (13.3 vs 7.8 years, HR 0.59) and PFS (10.4 vs 4.0 years), with benefit concentrated in IDH-mutant tumors; established RT+PCV for high-risk low-grade glioma.

records.title: INDIGO (Mellinghoff)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · III · 2023
records.body: Residual/recurrent grade 2 IDH1/2-mutant glioma, surgery only Vorasidenib vs placebo Progression-free survival Vorasidenib, a brain-penetrant IDH inhibitor, prolonged PFS (27.7 vs 11.1 months, HR 0.39) and time to next intervention, with durability confirmed on extended follow-up; established targeted therapy that can delay chemoradiation. FDA-approved August 2024 (Voranigo) - the first systemic therapy for grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma.

records.title: ASCO-SNO Guideline (Mohile et al.)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · N/A · 2022
