records.title: GHSG HD16
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated classic Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage I or II, or nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease in stage IB, IIA or IIB, without a large mediastinal mass, extranodal lesions, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas; aged 18-75. All 1,150 were randomised before any interim PET existed; the primary comparison rests on 628 PET-2-negative patients analysed per protocol 2 cycles of ABVD then 20 Gy involved-field radiotherapy in all patients vs 2 cycles of ABVD then 20 Gy only where the interim PET after cycle 2 was positive on central review Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, negative interim PET rate, second malignancy, toxicity. Radiotherapy cannot be dropped after a negative interim PET: omitting it cost tumour control and non-inferiority was not met. Among the 628 PET-2-negative patients analysed per protocol, 5-year progression-free survival was 86.1% with ABVD alone against 93.4% with chemotherapy plus 20 Gy, a difference of -7.3 points (95% CI -13.0 to -1.6); the hazard ratio was 1.78 and its interval reached 3.12, above the 3.01 margin, so a 10-point loss could not be excluded. The mechanism was local: in-field recurrence 9% with ABVD alone vs 2%, while out-field recurrence was 5% vs 4%. Survival showed nothing either way on 12 deaths in total, 5-year overall survival 98.4% vs 98.1%, and there were more deaths in the arm with better tumour control, 9 of 328 vs 3 of 300. Interim PET was positive in 34% of the 1,007 scans centrally reviewed.

records.title: GHSG HD13
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · III · 2015
records.body: Untreated classic Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage I or II, or nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease in stage IB, IIA or IIB only, without a large mediastinal mass, extranodal lesions, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas. 1,710 were randomised and 1,502 qualified for analysis; stage IA nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease was a named reason for exclusion 2 cycles of ABVD vs 3 reduced-intensity variants — ABV (no dacarbazine), AVD (no bleomycin) or AV (neither) — each followed by 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy, randomised 1:1:1:1 Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, complete remission, toxicity. Neither dacarbazine nor bleomycin can be omitted from ABVD. Both dacarbazine-omitted arms were closed early for higher event rates, AV in September 2005 and ABV in February 2006, and each is compared with the ABVD patients recruited alongside it: 5-year freedom from treatment failure 77.1% with AV against 92.3%, hazard ratio 2.57 (95% CI 1.51-4.40), and 81.4% with ABV against 92.9%, 2.06 (1.21-3.52). The bleomycin-omitted variant ran to the end and also fell short: AVD 89.2% against 93.1% for ABVD, hazard ratio 1.50 (95% CI 1.00-2.26), whose upper bound exceeded the 1.72 margin, so non-inferiority was not shown. Overall survival was 94-98% across the 4 groups and did not separate. No death was due to toxicity of first-line treatment in any group, and grade 3 or 4 leucopenia tracked bleomycin, 17-18% with it against 11-12% without. Unmodified ABVD remains the standard; radiotherapy was 30 Gy in every group here, chosen before HD10 established 20 Gy.

records.title: GHSG HD7
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · N/A · 2007
records.body: Newly diagnosed, previously untreated, histology-proven Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical or pathologic stage IA-IIB without GHSG risk factors (large mediastinal mass, extranodal disease, massive splenic involvement, high ESR); all HL subtypes incl. lymphocyte-predominant; age 16-75, Karnofsky >70%; prior malignancy and composite lymphoma excluded 2 cycles ABVD → 30 Gy extended-field RT (spleen 36 Gy) + 10 Gy involved-field boost vs 30 Gy extended-field RT (spleen 36 Gy) + 10 Gy involved-field boost Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, complete remission, relapse, second malignancy, acute toxicity. Two cycles of ABVD before radiotherapy transformed disease control in favourable early-stage disease and is why chemotherapy became part of the standard: 7-year freedom from treatment failure was 88% with combined-modality treatment against 67% with extended-field radiotherapy alone, a 21-point difference driven almost entirely by relapse, 3.2% against 21.9%. Survival did not separate, 7-year overall survival 94% against 92%, and 51 of 627 patients died in all. Treatment-related deaths ran 2 with chemotherapy added against 7 with radiotherapy alone, most after the salvage those relapses required. Adding ABVD did not increase acute radiotherapy toxicity, grade 3 in a few percent of either arm, though ABVD itself gave grade 3 leukopenia in 11% and hair loss in 9.9%. Second malignancies were 18 against 21, 39 in total, with similar cumulative incidence, though the authors caution that numbers at risk beyond year 9 are small and more events will follow. Median observation 87 months.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2007;25:3495-3502   J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1999-2007 long-term follow-up update 28418763 J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1444-1450 pooled late-relapse analysis (HD7-HD12) 28240973

records.title: GHSG HD14
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2012
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage IA, IB or IIA with at least one GHSG risk factor — a large mediastinal mass, extranodal involvement, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas — and stage IIB with only the last two of those. Median age 32, range 18-60. 1,655 were randomised and 1,528 qualified for the primary analysis 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP then 2 cycles of ABVD vs 4 cycles of ABVD, each followed by 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, response, toxicity. Two cycles of escalated BEACOPP before ABVD improved tumour control decisively, and the price is acute toxicity. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 94.8% against 87.7% with 4 cycles of ABVD, a difference of 7.2 points (95% CI 3.8 to 10.5), hazard ratio 0.44 (95% CI 0.30 to 0.66); 5-year progression-free survival 95.4% against 89.1%. Superiority was reached at the third of five planned interim analyses and randomisation was stopped early for it. Overall survival was 97.0% at 5 years and did not separate. The cost is in the marrow: at least one grade 3 or 4 event in 87.1% against 50.7%, grade 4 in 56.6% against 5.9%, and grade 3 or 4 leukopenia in 79.0% against 23.5%. All 4 deaths from first-line treatment toxicity were on the intensified arm, though 6 of the 7 salvage-toxicity deaths were on ABVD. Median follow-up was 43 months, short of the 5-year landmarks these figures quote.

records.title: GHSG HD11
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2010
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma of any histology in clinical stage IA, IB or IIA with at least one GHSG risk factor — a large mediastinal mass, extranodal involvement, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas — and stage IIB with only the last two of those. 1,570 were randomised and 1,395 qualified for the chemotherapy analysis; 1,351 for the radiotherapy analysis 4 cycles of ABVD vs 4 cycles of baseline BEACOPP, each followed by 30 vs 20 Gy involved-field radiotherapy — a 2x2 factorial in 4 groups Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, response, toxicity. Neither escalating the chemotherapy nor lowering the radiotherapy dose improved on 4 cycles of ABVD followed by 30 Gy, which the authors concluded should remain the standard. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 85.0% across the trial. At 30 Gy, baseline BEACOPP and ABVD did not differ, 1.6 points (95% CI -3.6 to 6.9); only at 20 Gy did BEACOPP come out ahead, 5.7 points (0.1 to 11.3). Dropping 30 Gy to 20 Gy after ABVD cost 4.7 points (-10.3 to 0.8), the bound falling outside the 7-point non-inferiority limit, so 20 Gy was not established there; after baseline BEACOPP the loss was 0.8 points (-5.8 to 4.2) and 20 Gy was non-inferior. The interaction between the two questions was not shown, at P=0.16. 5-year overall survival was 94-95% in all 4 groups. Baseline BEACOPP cost more acute toxicity, at least one grade 3 or 4 event in 73.8% against 51.5%, and 30 Gy more than 20 Gy, 12.0% against 5.7%.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2010;28:4199-4206  20713848 J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1999-2007 long-term follow-up update 28418763 J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1444-1450 pooled late-relapse analysis (HD7-HD12) 28240973

records.title: UK RAPID
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2015
records.body: Untreated classic Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage IA or IIA without mediastinal bulk, aged 16-75. 602 were registered and started ABVD; 571 were scanned after 3 cycles and 426 were PET-negative, of whom 420 were randomised; the 145 who were PET-positive received a fourth cycle with radiotherapy and were followed without randomisation After 3 cycles of ABVD and a negative PET: 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy vs no further treatment (single-arm follow-up for PET-positive patients, who received a 4th ABVD cycle plus radiotherapy) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: interim PET positivity rate, OS and cause of death, second cancers. Omitting radiotherapy after a negative PET was not shown to be non-inferior, though the absolute loss was small and survival was not harmed. Among the 420 randomised, 3-year progression-free survival was 90.8% without further treatment against 94.6% with radiotherapy, a difference of -3.8 points whose 95% interval ran to -8.8 and so fell outside the 7-point margin. Only 40 of the 46 events the trial was designed around had occurred. Per protocol the gap widened, 90.8% against 97.1%. Survival did not separate: 3-year overall survival 99.0% without radiotherapy against 97.1% with it, and of the 8 deaths in the radiotherapy arm 5 were in patients who never received it. The trade is a few points of tumour control against irradiating everyone, in a group whose 3-year survival exceeds 97% either way.

records.title: EORTC/LYSA/FIL H10
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2017
records.body: Untreated classic supradiaphragmatic Hodgkin lymphoma in Ann Arbor stage I or II, aged 15-70, assigned at entry to an EORTC favourable or unfavourable cohort. All 1,950 were randomised before any PET existed; treatment was then adapted to the PET after 2 cycles of ABVD, and the two cohorts were analysed separately PET-negative after 2 cycles of ABVD: 4 cycles of ABVD (favourable) or 6 cycles (unfavourable) with no radiotherapy vs 3 or 4 cycles plus involved-node radiotherapy. PET-positive: 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP plus involved-node radiotherapy vs continuing ABVD plus radiotherapy Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, second malignancy. Radiotherapy could not be dropped after a negative PET in either cohort, while intensifying after a positive PET improved control. In the favourable cohort 5-year progression-free survival was 87.1% with ABVD alone against 99.0% with ABVD plus involved-node radiotherapy, hazard ratio 15.8 (95% CI 3.79 to 66.07); in the unfavourable cohort 89.6% against 92.1%, 1.45 (0.84 to 2.50). Both upper bounds exceeded their margins, 3.2 and 2.10, so non-inferiority was not shown in either. Where the PET was positive, switching to 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP raised 5-year progression-free survival to 90.6% from 77.4%, hazard ratio 0.42 (0.23 to 0.74). Survival was not uniform: the PET-positive patients kept on ABVD with radiotherapy had 5-year overall survival of 89.3%, the lowest in the trial, against 96.0% with escalated BEACOPP, hazard ratio 0.45 (95% CI 0.19 to 1.07), which the authors call a trend. The PET-negative strands ran 96.7% to 100.0%.

records.title: GHSG HD17
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated stage IA, IB or IIA classical Hodgkin lymphoma or nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease with at least one GHSG risk factor, or stage IIB with a raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas and neither a bulky mass nor extranodal disease; aged 18-60. All 1,100 were randomised at entry, before the PET after 4 cycles; 905 formed the per-protocol population on which the verdict rests 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP then 2 cycles of ABVD in both groups, followed by 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy in all patients vs 30 Gy involved-node radiotherapy only where the PET after cycle 4 was positive Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, complete remission, PET-negative rate, late toxicity, second malignancy. Radiotherapy can be omitted after a negative PET in unfavourable early-stage disease. 5-year progression-free survival was 95.1% with PET-guided treatment against 97.3% when everyone was irradiated, a difference of 2.2 points whose upper bound of 5.3 stayed inside the 8-point margin, so non-inferiority was met; among the PET-negative patients alone it was 95.9% against 97.7%, a difference of 1.7 points with the same bound. The hazard ratio was 0.523 (95% CI 0.226 to 1.211) and crosses 1. 5-year overall survival was 98.8%, with 10 deaths among 1,096 patients and 1 attributed to treatment. Late toxicity, which is the whole reason to omit radiotherapy, is not reported here and is deferred to a later analysis; second malignancies were 7 of 546 against 8 of 550 so far. Median follow-up 46.2 months and 25 progression-free survival events against the 35 the trial was powered for, so the 5-year figures are early.

records.title: GHSG HD8
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2003
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma of any histology in clinical stage I or II with one or more risk factors, or in stage IIIA with none — the stage IIIA route is the inverse of the stage I-II one, not a selection within it. Nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease was enrolled. 1,204 were randomised and 1,064 were informative for efficacy 2 cycles of COPP plus ABVD followed by 30 Gy extended-field radiotherapy vs 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy, each with 10 Gy to initial bulk Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, toxicity, second malignancy. Shrinking the radiotherapy field from extended to involved cost nothing in disease control and spared considerable acute toxicity, which is why involved-field became the standard. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 84.2% with involved-field against 85.8% with extended-field, a difference of 1.6 points whose upper 95% bound of 5.9 stayed inside the 8-point inferiority limit the trial set; 5-year overall survival was 92.4% against 90.8%. The design tested equivalence rather than non-inferiority and reports no hazard ratio. Acute radiotherapy toxicity was the reason to change practice: nausea 29.1% against 62.5%, leukopenia 33.3% against 49.1% and thrombocytopenia 5.5% against 16.7%, all lower with involved-field. Second malignancies occurred in 2.8% against 4.5% and deaths in 6.4% against 8.1%, neither difference established.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2003;21:3601-3608   J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1999-2007 long-term follow-up update 28418763 J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1444-1450 pooled late-relapse analysis (HD7-HD12) 28240973

records.title: GHSG HD9
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2003
records.body: Untreated advanced or unfavourable intermediate-stage Hodgkin lymphoma, ages 15-65: stage IIB or IIIA with a large mediastinal mass alone or with extranodal lesions or massive splenic involvement, stage IIIA with a raised sedimentation rate or 3 or more involved nodal areas, or any stage IIIB-IV; Karnofsky above 70%, HIV-negative. 1,282 were assigned and 1,196 assessable at 10 years (261, 469 and 466 by arm); COPP/ABVD closed early in 1996. 8 cycles COPP/ABVD vs 8 cycles baseline BEACOPP vs 8 cycles escalated BEACOPP (cyclophosphamide 1,200, etoposide 200, doxorubicin 35 mg/m2 with filgrastim from day 8); consolidation radiotherapy to residual or initially bulky disease Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, treatment outcome as complete remission or early progression, second malignancy, causes of death, acute toxicity, survival after relapse. Escalated BEACOPP held its advantage over COPP/ABVD to 10 years, at the price of secondary leukaemia. Freedom from treatment failure was 82% with escalated BEACOPP, 70% with baseline BEACOPP and 64% with COPP/ABVD, and overall survival 86%, 80% and 75% in the same order, at a median 111 months; escalated beat baseline BEACOPP on both (P<.0001 and P=.0053). Secondary leukaemia or myelodysplasia tracked dose - 3.0% with escalated BEACOPP against 1.5% and 0.4%, 10-year cumulative incidence 3.2%, 2.2% and 0.4% (P=.030) - and 13 of the 14 escalated-arm cases arose within 7 years. Second malignancy overall did not separate (cumulative incidence 6.5%, 7.9% and 5.3%, P=.82), non-Hodgkin lymphoma and solid tumours running the other way. COPP/ABVD was closed at the first interim analysis and contributes 261 patients against 469 and 466. This 10-year cut sits outside the trial's prespecified analysis schedule, so none of its comparisons is a protected result.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2003;348:2386-2395   J Clin Oncol 2009;27:4548-4554 10-year follow-up 19704068 J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1444-1450 pooled late-relapse analysis (HD7-HD12) 28240973

records.title: GHSG HD15
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2012
records.body: Untreated, histology-confirmed advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma: stage IIB with a large mediastinal mass or extranodal lesions, or any stage III or IV; ages 18-60; ECOG 0-2; HIV-negative and without concurrent disease. Expert-panel reference histology was mandatory and excluded 44 patients from all analyses. 2,182 were randomised and 2,126 analysed. 8 cycles escalated BEACOPP (21-day cycles) vs 6 cycles escalated BEACOPP vs 8 cycles BEACOPP-14 (baseline doses, 14-day cycles); by protocol 30 Gy radiotherapy was planned for residual masses of 2.5 cm or more that remained PET-positive, and withheld otherwise Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, complete remission, treatment-related toxicity. Independent endpoint: negative predictive value of PET. Six cycles of escalated BEACOPP were non-inferior to eight and less toxic, and the investigators concluded 6 cycles should be the treatment of choice. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 89.3% with 6 cycles, 84.4% with 8 cycles and 85.4% with 8 cycles of BEACOPP-14; both reduced-intensity arms met non-inferiority on a hazard-ratio margin of 1.51. Superiority on freedom from treatment failure was not established: 6 cycles separated from 8 there only in the trial's descriptive analysis, not in its protected one. Toxicity favoured 6 cycles: treatment-related death 0.8% vs 2.1%, secondary leukaemia or myelodysplasia 0.3% vs 2.7% (P=0.0001). 5-year overall survival was 95.3% vs 91.9%, a difference of 3.3 points (97.5% CI 0.2 to 6.5). Confining radiotherapy to PET-positive residua cut its use to 11%, with a negative predictive value of 94.1%. Reported at the fourth preplanned interim analysis, median 48 months and 3 years early.

records.title: RATHL
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2016
records.body: Previously untreated advanced classic Hodgkin lymphoma: stage IIB-IV, or stage IIA with bulky disease or 3 or more involved sites; aged 18 or over, no upper limit, fit for full chemotherapy. Of 1,214 registered and 1,203 eligible, 937 were PET-negative after 2 cycles of ABVD and 935 of those were randomised; of the 182 PET-positive, 172 escalated to BEACOPP without randomisation. After 2 cycles of ABVD and a negative central interim PET-CT: continue ABVD for cycles 3-6 vs omit bleomycin (AVD) for cycles 3-6; interim-PET-positive patients escalated to BEACOPP-14 or escalated BEACOPP Primary: 3-year progression-free survival. Secondary: PFS among interim-PET-positive patients given BEACOPP, OS, short- and long-term toxicity, respiratory function. Omitting bleomycin after a negative interim PET fell just short of the prespecified non-inferiority margin, so AVD was not formally established as non-inferior, though efficacy was not significantly lower and pulmonary toxicity was less. 3-year progression-free survival was 85.7% continuing ABVD and 84.4% with AVD; the 1.6-percentage-point difference carried a 95% CI of -3.2 to 5.3, whose upper bound exceeded the 5-point margin, and the hazard ratio was 1.13 (95% CI 0.81-1.57). 3-year overall survival was 97.2% and 97.6%. Pulmonary harm was lower with AVD: grade 3 or 4 pulmonary events 1% vs 3%, and a smaller fall in carbon monoxide diffusing capacity, differing by 7.4 points at end of treatment (P<0.001) and 4.6 points at 1 year. Escalating the 172 interim-PET-positive patients to BEACOPP gave 3-year progression-free survival of 67.5% and overall survival of 87.8%. Median follow-up 41.2 months.

records.title: GHSG HD18
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2017
records.body: Untreated, histology-confirmed classic or nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma: stage III-IV, or stage II with B symptoms plus a large mediastinal mass or extranodal lesions; ages 18-60, ECOG 0-2, HIV-negative. Of 2,101 recruited, 1,964 were randomised and 1,945 analysed; treatment was then assigned by central PET after 2 cycles, counting Deauville 3 as positive. All received 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP, then assignment by central PET-2. PET-2-positive: 8 cycles total vs 8 cycles plus rituximab 375 mg/m2 (maximum total 700 mg). PET-2-negative: 4 cycles total vs 6-8 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, assessed separately in the PET-2-positive and PET-2-negative cohorts. Secondary: OS, second malignancy, complete response, Hodgkin lymphoma-specific death, grade 3-4 toxicity, treatment-related morbidity, late toxicity, quality of life. HD18 met one primary objective and missed the other: adding rituximab to escalated BEACOPP after a positive PET-2 did not improve outcome, while cutting to 4 cycles after a negative PET-2 held tumour control and reduced harm. In the PET-2-positive cohort 5-year progression-free survival was 88.1% with rituximab against 89.7% without, hazard ratio 1.25 (95% CI 0.69-2.26), P=0.46, far short of the 15-percentage-point gain the trial was powered to detect. In PET-2-negative patients 4 cycles gave 92.2% against 90.8% for 6-8 cycles, a 1.4-point difference (95% CI -2.7 to 5.4) clearing the -6-point non-inferiority margin, on the per-protocol set. 4 cycles also cut harm: no treatment-related death against 6 of 504, severe infection 8% vs 15%, organ toxicity 8% vs 18%, and 5-year overall survival 97.7% vs 95.4% (hazard ratio 0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.72), though survival was not a protected endpoint. Median follow-up 66 months for the rituximab comparison and 55 months for the 4-cycle comparison.

records.title: ECHELON-1
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated stage III or IV classic Hodgkin lymphoma, aged 18 or over with no upper limit; ECOG 0-2. 1,334 were randomised and all analysed. 84 and 102 patients by arm were 60 or older, and enrolment continued after an amendment recommending primary G-CSF prophylaxis for patients yet to be enrolled. Brentuximab vedotin 1.2 mg/kg IV plus doxorubicin, vinblastine and dacarbazine on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle for up to 6 cycles vs ABVD, the same regimen with bleomycin instead of brentuximab vedotin, on the same schedule; primary G-CSF prophylaxis recommended by amendment after 75% of enrolment Primary: modified progression-free survival by independent review. Secondary: OS. The trial's remaining secondary and exploratory endpoints are in its protocol, which is not filed. Brentuximab vedotin with AVD improved the trial's primary endpoint and reduced bleomycin lung injury, at the cost of neuropathy and neutropenia. That endpoint was MODIFIED progression-free survival, which counts noncomplete response plus subsequent therapy as an event: 2-year rate 82.1% vs 77.2%, hazard ratio 0.77 (95% CI 0.60-0.98), P=0.04, at a median 24.6 months. Interstitial lung disease fell to 2% from 7%, while peripheral neuropathy rose to 67% from 43%, grade 3 or worse 11% vs 2%, and febrile neutropenia to 19% from 8%; 7 of the 9 on-treatment deaths were neutropenia-associated and almost all occurred without G-CSF prophylaxis, which the trial's monitoring committee then recommended. A separately reported interim survival analysis at a median 73 months showed a survival benefit: 6-year overall survival 93.9% vs 89.4%, hazard ratio 0.59 (95% CI 0.40-0.88), P=0.009, with 1 death from a second cancer against 11.

records.title: GHSG HD21
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated advanced-stage classic Hodgkin lymphoma, ages 18-60: stage III-IV, or stage II with B symptoms plus a large mediastinal mass or extranodal lesions. 1,500 were randomised and 1,482 analysed; treatment length was set by PET after 2 cycles, 4 cycles if negative and 6 if positive. PET-2-guided 4 or 6 cycles at 21-day intervals: BrECADD - brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg to a maximum 180 mg IV day 0 with etoposide, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, dacarbazine and dexamethasone - vs escalated BEACOPP Primary: treatment-related morbidity and progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, gonadal function, second malignancy, quality of life, safety. BrECADD met both co-primary endpoints: it caused less treatment-related morbidity than escalated BEACOPP and gave superior progression-free survival. Treatment-related morbidity was 42% vs 59%, relative risk 0.72 (95% CI 0.65-0.80), P<0.0001. 4-year progression-free survival was 94.3% vs 90.9%, hazard ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.45-0.97), P=0.035, at a median 48 months, and 4-year survival 98.6% vs 98.2%, with no treatment-related death on BrECADD against 3 on escalated BEACOPP. The toxicity advantage is haematological rather than general: grade 3 or worse anaemia 30% vs 59% and thrombocytopenia 55% vs 72%, but organ toxicity did not differ (19% vs 17%, P=0.46) and neutropenic fever, cardiac and gastrointestinal events were commoner on BrECADD. Gonadal recovery was far better - 95.3% vs 72.5% in women and 86.0% vs 39.2% in men.

records.title: SWOG S1826
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated advanced-stage classic Hodgkin lymphoma, aged 12 or over with no upper limit, including adolescents; stage III-IV. 994 were randomised and 970 formed the efficacy cohort after 24 were found ineligible. Nivolumab 240 mg IV, or 3 mg/kg capped at 240 mg if aged 12 to under 18, plus doxorubicin, vinblastine and dacarbazine on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle for 6 cycles vs brentuximab vedotin 1.2 mg/kg IV capped at 100 kg plus the same AVD backbone and schedule Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: adverse events, OS, event-free survival. Nivolumab with AVD roughly halved progression or death compared with brentuximab vedotin plus AVD. The trial was reported early at a planned interim analysis, at a median follow-up of only 12.1 months: hazard ratio 0.48 (99% CI 0.27-0.87), P=0.001, with 1-year progression-free survival 94% vs 86%. A later cut at a median 2.1 years gave 2-year progression-free survival 92% vs 83% and hazard ratio 0.45 (95% CI 0.30-0.65). Whole-trial survival is immature and unproven: hazard ratio for death 0.39, 95% CI 0.15-1.03, crossing 1. In planned subset analyses, 3 of 50 patients aged 60 or over died on nivolumab against 10 of 49 on brentuximab, with grade 3 or worse sepsis 6.1% vs 21.3%. Brentuximab was stopped early in 55.3% of them, nivolumab in 14%. Among the 236 adolescents, 3-year progression-free survival was 93% vs 82%, with protocol radiotherapy in only 3 of 236. Grade 3 or worse neutropenia was commoner with nivolumab, 48% vs 26%, but G-CSF was mandatory only on the brentuximab arm.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2024;391:1379-1389   J Clin Oncol 2025;43:2968-2973 older-patient subset analysis 40523203 J Clin Oncol 2026;44:449-454 adolescent subset, 3-year follow-up 41512237

records.title: GHSG/EBMT HD-R1
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory disease — salvage, transplant & novel agents · N/A · 2002
records.body: Relapsed Hodgkin's disease after chemotherapy for advanced disease, at first or later relapse, age 16-60 with Karnofsky >70; late first relapse eligible only if first-line therapy used 7-8 drugs, and stage I-II at relapse only with added risk factors or previously advanced-stage disease; results apply to the 117 chemosensitive after 2 induction cycles, who alone proceeded to the assigned arms Dexa-BEAM x2 → 2 further Dexa-BEAM cycles (4 total) vs Dexa-BEAM x2 → high-dose BEAM + autologous stem-cell transplant Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, ORR, complete response rate, safety High-dose BEAM with autologous transplant improved disease control but not survival in chemosensitive relapse, and became standard salvage: 3-yr freedom from treatment failure 55% vs 34% with 4 cycles of Dexa-BEAM (p=0.019); median time to treatment failure not reached vs 12 mo. Survival did not differ (3-yr OS 71% vs 65%; p=0.331), from a trial stopped early for slow accrual at 117 of the 150 chemosensitive patients it was designed to need. The advantage held in early first relapse (41% vs 12%) and late first relapse (75% vs 44%), but not in multiple relapses (34% vs 44%). Most toxic deaths fell on the shared induction: the 2 Dexa-BEAM cycles every patient received caused 8 treatment-related deaths; after that, 5 of 56 (9%) died early on Dexa-BEAM cycles 3-4 vs 1 of 61 (2%) after transplant. Grade 3-4 infection 47% vs 49%; oral mucositis 37% vs 24%.

records.title: Brentuximab vedotin (pivotal)
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory disease — salvage, transplant & novel agents · II · 2012
records.body: Relapsed or refractory Hodgkin lymphoma after high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem-cell transplant; CD30-positive Reed-Sternberg cells on central pathology review; age >=12, ECOG 0-1, FDG-avid measurable disease >=1.5 cm; prior allogeneic transplant excluded (single-arm) Brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV q3w, maximum 16 cycles Primary: ORR. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, PFS, OS, safety Brentuximab vedotin gave durable responses after autologous transplant had failed, in patients with a median 3.5 prior regimens: ORR 75% (95% CI 64.9-82.6) on independent review with CR in 34%. Median PFS was 5.6 mo overall but 21.7 mo in complete remitters, whose median response duration reached 20.5 mo; median OS 22.4 mo. Responses were fast — median 5.7 weeks to response, 12 weeks to CR — and 94% had some tumour reduction; 8 responders proceeded directly to allogeneic transplant. Peripheral sensory neuropathy dominated toxicity: 42% any grade and 8% grade 3, with no grade 4, cumulative and dose-related (median onset 12.4 weeks); it forced dose reduction in 10 patients and discontinuation in 6, and resolved or improved in 80%. Grade 3+ neutropenia 20% with no febrile neutropenia; no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: AETHERA
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory disease — salvage, transplant & novel agents · III · 2015
records.body: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma 30-45 days after autologous stem-cell transplant for relapsed or primary refractory disease, with >=1 risk factor for post-transplant progression: primary refractory disease, first remission <12 mo, or extranodal involvement at the start of pre-transplant salvage; CR, PR or SD to salvage required; prior brentuximab vedotin excluded Brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV q3w x16 cycles starting 30-45 days after autologous transplant vs placebo Primary: PFS. Secondary: OS, safety Brentuximab vedotin consolidation after autologous transplant delayed progression without a shown survival gain: median PFS 42.9 vs 24.1 mo on independent review (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.40-0.81; p=0.0013), 2-yr PFS 63% vs 51%. Survival did not differ at the prespecified interim analysis (HR 1.15, 95% CI 0.67-1.97; p=0.6204), confounded by crossover: 85% of the placebo group received brentuximab vedotin after progression vs 18% of the treated group. Peripheral neuropathy is the price — 67% any grade and 13% grade 3, none grade 4 — forcing dose modification in 31% and discontinuation in 23%; it resolved or improved in 85% over a median 23.4 weeks. Grade 3+ events overall 56% vs 32%; grade 3+ neutropenia 29% vs 10%, with 1 febrile episode.

records.title: CheckMate 205
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory disease — salvage, transplant & novel agents · II · 2016
records.body: One cohort of a multicohort trial: classical Hodgkin lymphoma progressing after both autologous stem-cell transplant and subsequent brentuximab vedotin, given in that order; refractoriness to brentuximab vedotin not required; ECOG 0-1; prior allogeneic transplant, prior PD-1/PD-L1/CTLA-4 blockade, and brentuximab vedotin given before transplant all excluded (single-arm) Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV q2w until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: ORR. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, PFS, OS, safety, quality of life Nivolumab produced frequent but mostly partial responses after failure of both autologous transplant and brentuximab vedotin: ORR 66.3% (95% CI 54.8-76.4) on independent review, with CR in 9% and PR in 58%. Investigators scored the same patients at 72.5% ORR and 28% CR, and central review downgraded 13 of 19 investigator-assessed CRs. Median response duration 7.8 mo and median PFS 10.0 mo at a median follow-up of 8.9 mo; 6-mo OS 98.7%, with no median OS reported. Responses came early, 58% by the first scan at week 9. Drug-related events affected 89%, grade 3 in 21% and grade 4 in 4%, most often neutropenia (5% grade 3) and raised lipase; pneumonitis occurred in 3%, both cases resolving on steroids, and 5% stopped for toxicity. 3 patients died, none of a treatment-related cause.

records.title: KEYNOTE-204
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory disease — salvage, transplant & novel agents · III · 2021
records.body: Relapsed or refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma, second line or later, either after autologous stem-cell transplant or judged ineligible for one, so a transplant-eligible patient not yet transplanted did not qualify; prior brentuximab vedotin allowed only where it produced a complete or partial response; allogeneic transplant within 5 years and prior non-infectious pneumonitis requiring steroids excluded Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w vs brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV q3w, both up to 35 cycles or until progression Primary: PFS, OS. Secondary: ORR, complete response rate, duration of response, safety Pembrolizumab prolonged PFS over brentuximab vedotin in the second line and beyond: median 13.2 vs 8.3 mo on central review (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.48-0.88; p=0.0027), ORR 65.6% vs 54.2%, CR 25% vs 24%, median response duration 20.7 vs 13.8 mo. Overall survival, a co-primary endpoint, was not analysed at this second interim cut. Only 37% had had an autologous transplant; the PFS advantage was clearest in those never transplanted (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.42-0.89) and did not separate in the previously transplanted (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.42-1.23), with no interaction test reported. The toxicities differ in kind: any-grade immune-mediated events 33% vs 7%, including pneumonitis 11% vs 3% any grade and 5% vs 1% grade 3-5; brentuximab vedotin gave treatment-related peripheral neuropathy in 15% grade 1-2 and 3% grade 3. 1 treatment-related death, from pneumonia, on pembrolizumab.

records.title: Lugano Classification (Cheson et al.)
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Staging & response assessment — Lugano classification · N/A · 2014
records.body: Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, all subtypes N/A — staging and response assessment framework, not a trial N/A Made PET-CT the standard for staging and response in FDG-avid lymphoma — all but CLL/SLL, lymphoplasmacytic, mycosis fungoides and marginal zone, which use the CT criteria. Response is scored on the Deauville 5-point scale, and the document is not consistent about what counts as complete: table 3 accepts 1 to 3 with or without a residual mass, the text only 1 or 2. It calls a score of 3 a good prognosis on standard treatment, and says de-escalation trials may prefer to treat it as inadequate. Marrow biopsy is dropped in Hodgkin lymphoma once PET-CT is done, and in DLBCL only where the scan is negative and discordant histology would change management; 2.5 cm unilateral biopsy stands elsewhere. The X suffix for bulk is retired for the largest diameter, A and B symptoms are kept for Hodgkin alone, and CRu is abolished. Bulk in Hodgkin stays 10 cm or a third of the transthoracic diameter, with none set for non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Surveillance scanning is discouraged. Consensus, ungraded.

records.title: TROG 99.03
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Limited-stage (stage I–II) — radiotherapy & adjuvant systemic therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Treatment-naive Ann Arbor stage I–II follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3a, staged by CT and bone marrow biopsy, with a life expectancy over 5 years and fit for involved-field RT; PET staging was permitted throughout but never required; excludes thoracic disease too extensive to irradiate safely. A 2006 amendment added rituximab to the systemic arm, which therefore spans two eras — 44 patients given CVP and 31 R-CVP IFRT 30-36 Gy → 6 cycles CVP (R-CVP after the 2006 amendment) vs IFRT 30-36 Gy alone Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, histologic transformation, safety Adding systemic therapy after involved-field RT improved PFS in early-stage follicular lymphoma: 10-yr PFS 59% vs 41%, HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.33-0.95). OS did not differ (10-yr 95% vs 86%; HR 0.62) and transformation was not reduced (4 vs 10 of 75 per arm). Only 2 of 148 irradiated patients had isolated in-field progression, so RT controlled local disease and the systemic benefit lay in preventing distant relapse. The rituximab-era effect looks larger (HR 0.26, 95% CI 0.07-0.97) but is post-hoc and rests on few events. Toxicity after IFRT was mostly grade 1-2, grade 3-4 in 2%, with late salivary-gland toxicity in 8 (5%) and late skin toxicity in 4 (3%); among the 69 who started systemic therapy grade 4 neutropenia occurred in 10 (14%), grade 3 infection in 8 (12%) and grade 3 vincristine neuropathy in 3 (4%), with 2 late grade 3 vincristine neuropathies. One patient died of myelodysplasia in remission after IFRT plus CVP.

records.title: Ardeshna (NCRI)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — timing of therapy & single-agent rituximab · III · 2014
records.body: Asymptomatic, treatment-naive follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3a, stage II–IV, ECOG 0–1, entered within 3 months of diagnostic biopsy; low tumour burden was the entry gate, defined as normal LDH, no mass over 7 cm, no more than 3 nodal sites with nodes over 3 cm, spleen up to 16 cm and no significant effusion; excludes histological transformation and near-critical organ compression. The rituximab-induction-only arm closed to recruitment in 2007 Rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly ×4 → maintenance q2mo ×2 yr vs rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly ×4 vs watch-and-wait Primary: time to start of new treatment, quality of life at month 7. Secondary: spontaneous remission rate, response at month 25, overall survival, quality of life, progression-free survival, time to histological transformation, safety Early rituximab markedly delays new treatment but did not improve the quality of life it was co-designed to test. At 3 yr, 88% on rituximab maintenance vs 46% on watch-and-wait had not started new therapy (HR 0.21, 95% CI 0.14-0.31); median 31.1 mo with observation, not reached with maintenance. The quality-of-life co-primary — better functional wellbeing, less anxiety and depression at month 7 — was not met (p=0.87, 0.51, 0.70), though mental adjustment to cancer favoured rituximab (p=0.0004). OS showed no difference (3-yr 97% vs 94%; HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.34-1.54) but is immature at 28 deaths in 379; transformation was not reduced (7% vs 11%). Induction alone matched maintenance for time to new treatment (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.41-1.34) but was worse on PFS (3-yr 60%; HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.32-0.87, p=0.011). 18 rituximab-related serious adverse events, 12 grade 3-4, mainly infection and neutropenia; no treatment-related deaths. Observation remains reasonable for asymptomatic low-burden disease.

records.title: GLSG (Hiddemann)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2005
records.body: Previously untreated stage III–IV follicular lymphoma, WHO grade 1–2, all requiring treatment at entry — B symptoms, bulky disease (mediastinal over 7.5 cm or other over 5 cm), impaired haematopoiesis, or rapidly progressive disease — so asymptomatic non-bulky disease suitable for watch-and-wait was out of scope; excludes grade 3 follicular lymphoma. Central pathology confirmation was not a gate before randomisation, still pending in 38 of 428 at analysis Induction: R-CHOP vs CHOP, both 6-8 cycles q3w → in responders under 60, a second randomisation to DexaBEAM then myeloablative radiochemotherapy with peripheral blood stem-cell transplantation vs interferon-α maintenance; all responders 60 and over received interferon-α maintenance Primary: time to treatment failure. Secondary: overall response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, time to next therapy, overall survival, safety Adding rituximab to CHOP cut treatment failure by 60% and established R-CHOP as the frontline standard in advanced follicular lymphoma: 28 of 223 failed on R-CHOP vs 61 of 205 on CHOP (p<0.001). Response was higher (96% vs 90%) though CR was not clearly different (20% vs 17%); duration of response and time to next therapy were both longer. Survival also favoured R-CHOP at this early follow-up, 6 vs 17 deaths within 3 yr (p=0.016), with lymphoma progression accounting for 1 vs 9. Median follow-up was only 18 mo, so these are early estimates. Grade 3-4 granulocytopenia was commoner with R-CHOP (after 63% vs 53% of cycles) but infections were as frequent in both arms (5% vs 7% of courses), and 4 patients in each arm died of infection, 8 of the 23 deaths; infusion reactions occurred in 7% of first rituximab infusions.

records.title: PRIMA
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2011
records.body: Previously untreated follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3a, with at least one high-tumour-burden criterion — a mass over 7 cm, 3 or more nodes of 3 cm or more, symptomatic splenomegaly, organ compression or effusion, raised LDH or beta2-microglobulin, or B symptoms; excludes grade 3b and transformed disease. Randomisation to maintenance required a complete or partial response to R-CVP, R-CHOP or R-FCM induction and no major induction toxicity, so it applies only to responders who tolerated induction Rituximab 375 mg/m² q8wk ×12 (2 yr) vs observation Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: event-free survival, time to next chemotherapy, time to next antilymphoma treatment, overall survival, response rate at end of maintenance, quality of life, safety 2 yr of rituximab maintenance after frontline immunochemotherapy improved 3-yr PFS 74.9% vs 57.6% (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.44-0.68) and raised CR/CRu at the end of maintenance to 71.5% vs 52.2%; 52% of those in partial response at randomisation converted to CR/CRu vs 30%. Time to next antilymphoma treatment (HR 0.62) and to next chemotherapy (HR 0.60) were both longer. OS did not differ (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.51-1.47) and quality of life did not differ (FACT-G 86.6 vs 87.2). Grade 3-4 adverse events 24% vs 17%, grade 2-4 infections 39% vs 24%, discontinuation for toxicity 4% vs 2%, and 1 death from fulminant hepatitis B without antiviral prophylaxis, reported as possibly treatment-related. Maintenance is a standard option for responders, at the cost of added infection risk and no survival gain so far.

records.title: FOLL05 (FIL)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2013
records.body: Previously untreated follicular lymphoma, WHO grade 1–3a, Ann Arbor stage II–IV, with active disease requiring treatment, aged 18–75; excludes grade 3b, stage I disease, histological transformation and CNS involvement. Central pathology review was required only for grade 3 or ungraded cases, all others entering on local diagnosis R-CVP ×8 cycles vs R-CHOP ×6 cycles vs R-FM ×6 cycles, all q3w Primary: time to treatment failure. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, overall response rate, complete response rate, safety R-CHOP and R-FM both beat R-CVP on 3-yr time to treatment failure (62% and 59% vs 46%; HR 0.62 and 0.63) and on 3-yr PFS (68% and 63% vs 52%), with no difference between R-CHOP and R-FM (p=0.76 for time to treatment failure). Response was similar across arms (ORR 88-93%, CR 67-73%) and 3-yr OS was 95% for the whole series, with no between-arm comparison made. R-FM carried the worst toxicity — grade 3-4 neutropenia 64% vs 50% with R-CHOP and 28% with R-CVP, thrombocytopenia 8% vs 3% and 0%, and 14 of the 23 second malignancies — so R-CHOP has the better risk-benefit balance and became the preferred backbone. Grade 3-4 infections were uncommon in all arms (2.4-4.7%) and there were no treatment-related deaths, but granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, not routinely given under protocol, was used at least once by 46% overall and unevenly by arm: 30% with R-CVP, 52% R-CHOP, 57% R-FM (p<0.001).

records.title: StiL NHL1 (Rummel)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2013
records.body: Treatment-naive stage III–IV CD20-positive indolent lymphoma — follicular grade 1–2, lymphoplasmacytic/Waldenström, small lymphocytic or marginal-zone — or mantle-cell lymphoma, WHO performance status 0–2; the indolent subtypes also had to need treatment, on cytopenia, B symptoms, bulk over 7.5 cm or 3 sites over 5 cm, organ compression, rapid progression or hyperviscosity, while mantle-cell entered on stage alone Bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1-2 + rituximab 375 mg/m² q4w vs R-CHOP q3w, both up to 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall response rate, complete response rate, overall survival, time to next antilymphoma treatment, event-free survival, safety Bendamustine-rituximab more than doubled median PFS over R-CHOP in untreated indolent and mantle-cell lymphoma: 69.5 vs 31.2 mo, HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.44-0.74), on the 514 of 549 randomised analysed per protocol. The trial was designed as a non-inferiority comparison. Time to next treatment was longer (HR 0.52) and CR higher (40% vs 30%), with the same overall response (93% vs 91%). OS did not differ (43 vs 45 deaths). On exploratory subgroups the gain was seen in follicular (HR 0.61), mantle-cell (0.49) and Waldenstrom (0.33) disease but not in marginal-zone lymphoma (0.70, 95% CI 0.34-1.43). BR was the better tolerated arm: grade 3-4 neutropenia 29% vs 69%; and at any grade, no alopecia at all against 100% of those given 3 or more R-CHOP cycles, infectious episodes 37% vs 50% and paraesthesia 7% vs 29%; 1 vs 5 deaths from sepsis. Commoner with BR were grade 3-4 lymphocytopenia (74% vs 43%) and, at any grade, erythematous (16% vs 9%) and allergic (15% vs 6%) skin reactions.

records.title: BRIGHT
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2014
records.body: Treatment-naive CD20-positive indolent NHL — follicular grade 1–2, lymphoplasmacytic, or splenic, extranodal MALT or nodal marginal-zone — or mantle-cell lymphoma, ECOG 0–2, needing treatment for B symptoms, bulk (over 3 cm at 3 or more sites or over 7 cm at 1), lymphoma-related complications or hyperviscosity; excludes CLL/SLL, grade 3 follicular lymphoma, stage I disease, transformed disease and CNS involvement Bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1-2 + rituximab 375 mg/m² q4w vs R-CHOP or R-CVP q3w (the comparator regimen chosen by the investigator before randomisation), all 6 cycles and up to 8 Primary: complete response rate. Secondary: overall response rate, progression-free survival, event-free survival, duration of response, overall survival, quality of life, safety Bendamustine-rituximab was non-inferior to R-CHOP or R-CVP for complete response in untreated indolent NHL and MCL — 31% vs 25% by blinded independent review, with a higher overall response (97% vs 91%). The CR gap did not clear the trial's superiority test. By histology it narrows: non-inferiority was not reached in the indolent-NHL subgroup (CR-rate ratio 1.16, 95% CI 0.81-1.65) and only approached in follicular lymphoma (1.27, 0.87-1.84). BR bettered standard therapy only in MCL (1.95, 1.01-3.77), on 33 standard-therapy patients. PFS, EFS, duration of response, OS and quality of life are unreported here, immature at this cut. Toxicity differed rather than lessened: against R-CHOP, BR gave less grade 3-4 neutropenia (39% vs 87%) but more grade 3-4 lymphopenia (61% vs 33%), and less alopecia (4% vs 51%) and neuropathy (9% vs 44%), both any grade; against R-CVP, more any-grade nausea (63% vs 39%), vomiting (25% vs 13%) and hypersensitivity (13% vs 3%). 12 deaths (5%) vs 9 (4%).

records.title: GALLIUM
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2017
records.body: Previously untreated CD20-positive follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3a, stage III–IV or stage II with a mass of 7 cm or more, ECOG 0–2, with treatment indicated by GELF tumour-burden criteria. GALLIUM also randomised a marginal-zone cohort, but was powered for the follicular stratum and only that stratum is reported here Obinutuzumab 1000 mg + chemotherapy (CHOP, CVP or bendamustine, stipulated by site) → obinutuzumab q2mo ×2 yr in responders vs rituximab 375 mg/m² + the same chemotherapy → rituximab q2mo ×2 yr in responders Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall response rate at end of induction, event-free survival, disease-free survival, duration of response, overall survival, time to new antilymphoma treatment, safety Obinutuzumab-based immunochemotherapy with obinutuzumab maintenance lengthened investigator-assessed PFS over the rituximab equivalent in untreated advanced follicular lymphoma: 3-yr PFS 80.0% vs 73.3%, HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.51-0.85); independent review of the same endpoint gave HR 0.71 (0.54-0.93). These are interim results, at 245 of the 370 planned events. OS did not differ (3-yr 94.0% vs 92.1%, HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.49-1.17), nor did response at end of induction (88.5% vs 86.9%), and CR was numerically lower with obinutuzumab (19.5% vs 23.8%). The cost is toxicity: grade 3-5 events 74.6% vs 67.8%, serious events 46.1% vs 39.9%, fatal events 4.0% vs 3.4%, grade 3-5 infusion reactions 12.4% vs 6.7%, grade 3-5 infection 20.0% vs 15.6% and grade 3-5 neutropenia 45.9% vs 39.5%; 6 obinutuzumab patients (1.0%) developed a second haematological cancer and no rituximab patient did.

records.title: RELEVANCE
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2018
records.body: Histologically confirmed CD20-positive follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3a, needing treatment by GELF tumour-burden criteria, with no previous systemic therapy for lymphoma; stage I–II disease was not excluded Rituximab + lenalidomide 10-20 mg/day ×18 cycles → rituximab q8wk ×12 vs rituximab + investigator's choice of CHOP, bendamustine or CVP → rituximab q8wk ×12; 120 weeks of treatment in both arms Primary: confirmed or unconfirmed complete response rate at 120 weeks, progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, duration of response, histologic transformation, safety Chemo-free rituximab-lenalidomide did not beat rituximab-chemotherapy in untreated follicular lymphoma, and neither co-primary endpoint was met: confirmed or unconfirmed CR at 120 wk 48% vs 53% (p=0.13) and PFS HR 1.10 (95% CI 0.85-1.43, p=0.48) at the first interim look. 3-yr PFS 77% vs 78%, no median reached for PFS or OS; OS immature, 3-yr 94% in both arms. Best CR at any point in the trial separated further, 59% vs 67%. The one subgroup interaction was by stage: among the 70 with stage I–II disease, CR at 120 wk was 10 of 30 on lenalidomide vs 30 of 40 on chemotherapy. Toxicity is the trade: lenalidomide gave more grade 3-4 skin reactions (7% vs 1%) and, at any grade, tumour flare (6% vs under 1%), with dose reduction in 36% vs 14% and discontinuation in 11% vs 3%; chemotherapy more grade 3-4 neutropenia (50% vs 32%) and, at any grade, febrile neutropenia (7% vs 2%) and infection with grade 3-4 neutropenia (12% vs 5%). Overall grade 3-4 events were similar, 65% vs 68%.

records.title: EORTC 20981 (van Oers)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — immunochemotherapy & maintenance · III · 2006
records.body: Relapsed or resistant CD20-positive follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3, Ann Arbor stage III–IV at initial diagnosis, after no more than 2 prior non-anthracycline regimens, WHO performance status 0–2; excludes prior anthracycline, prior rituximab, prior stem-cell transplantation and histological transformation, so the result does not extend to an anthracycline- or rituximab-exposed relapse. Only patients in complete or partial remission after induction entered the maintenance randomisation Induction: CHOP vs R-CHOP, both q3w ×6 → in responders, a second randomisation to rituximab 375 mg/m² q3mo for up to 2 yr vs observation Primary: response to induction, progression-free survival from the maintenance randomisation. Secondary: progression-free survival and overall survival from the first randomisation, overall survival from the maintenance randomisation, safety Rituximab maintenance after salvage immunochemotherapy improved both progression-free and overall survival in relapsed follicular lymphoma. Among the 334 responders randomised a second time, median PFS was 51.5 vs 14.9 mo with observation (HR 0.40) and 3-yr OS 85.1% vs 77.1% (HR 0.52, p=0.011). The gain held in patients who had already had rituximab during induction (51.8 vs 23.0 mo, HR 0.54), which is the trial's structural point. At the first randomisation R-CHOP beat CHOP for induction response (85.1% vs 72.3%) and CR (29.5% vs 15.6%) and for PFS (33.1 vs 20.2 mo, HR 0.65), but induction OS did not differ (3-yr 82.5% vs 71.9%, p=0.096). Maintenance cost more grade 3-4 infection (9% vs 2.4%, p=0.009); neutropenia was 10.8% vs 5.4%, which did not reach statistical significance; 6 of 167 stopped for toxicity and no death was attributed to it. Efficacy is on the 465 of 474 randomised with a valid consent form.

records.title: GADOLIN
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — immunochemotherapy & maintenance · III · 2016
records.body: Rituximab-refractory CD20-positive indolent NHL — follicular grade 1–3a, marginal zone, small lymphocytic or Waldenström's — after previous anti-lymphoma treatment including up to 4 chemotherapy-containing regimens, ECOG 0–2; refractory meant failure to respond to or progression during a previous rituximab-containing regimen, or progression within 6 months of the last dose; excludes histological transformation and bendamustine within the previous 2 yr Obinutuzumab 1000 mg + bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1-2 q4w ×6 → obinutuzumab 1000 mg q2mo for up to 2 yr in non-progressors vs bendamustine 120 mg/m² d1-2 q4w ×6 Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, overall response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, disease-free survival, event-free survival, time to next antilymphoma treatment, quality of life, safety Obinutuzumab-bendamustine then obinutuzumab maintenance prolonged survival in rituximab-refractory indolent NHL: at a median 31.8 mo, OS HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.47-0.96), with median PFS by investigator 25.8 vs 14.1 mo (HR 0.57) and time to next treatment 40.8 vs 19.4 mo (HR 0.59); in the 335 with follicular lymphoma OS HR was 0.58. The primary endpoint was met earlier, at a 2014 interim analysis of the 396 randomised by then, on independent review: median PFS not reached vs 14.9 mo, HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.40-0.74); survival had not separated at that cut (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.52-1.30), and no PFS benefit was shown in the 75 with non-follicular histology (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.46-1.90), a cohort the authors call too small to establish a difference. Response at end of induction did not differ (66.7% vs 64.4%). Grade 3-5 events 72.5% vs 65.5%, most commonly neutropenia (34.8% vs 27.1%), with infusion reactions (9.3% vs 3.4%); serious events 43.6% vs 36.9%; fatal events 7.8% vs 6.4%.
